00 The Rulings

The rulings

Read this first. Then do the task.

1 · Design rulings — structure, duration, exercises, what happens in the room

  1. No minutes. Show structure and beats, never per-beat minute allocations. "Get rid of the minutes. Get rid of all these things." — 2026-09-08, 15-inputs/hunter-notes/workshop/2026-09-08-founder-the-full-content-bank.md
  2. A run sheet cannot be locked; a spine can. "It shouldn't be broken into minutes. It should be broken into the structure and the beats, and those beats just get extended out in terms of the time depending on the session." — 2026-09-08, 30-decisions/D-0131
  3. The spine is four movements over fourteen beats. Order never changes; beats widen. Duration is a property of a beat in a product, not part of the spine. — 2026-09-08, D-0131
  4. One participant foundation; the 58, 90 and 240 are compressions of it. Nothing is added as a product gets longer — things are given back. "why can't that, but an improved version that we test with our agents, be the foundation for all services." — 2026-09-08, 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md
  5. All products follow one shared narrative. "introduction is not a different design brief. Change that." — 2026-08-31, supersedes D-0111 §1
  6. A room cannot perform a Do. No staged Do exercise, at any depth, ever. Reps used are ones participants have already done in their own lives. — 2026-09-08, 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md
  7. It is a keynote, not a workshop. "If it's in the sixty minute, we're not pulling out a butcher's sheet." No butcher's paper, nothing written by participants, nothing asked out loud. — 2026-09-07, 2026-09-07-founder-the-talk-as-hunter-gives-it.md
  8. Nobody speaks unless they want to. Nothing is collected. Max 20 with one facilitator; 30 only with a co-facilitator. — 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md
  9. Experience first, name second. The breath beat runs before the word Stop exists: "bring your attention to your breath… we caught the moment. We stopped. Then we name it." — 2026-09-07, founder capture
  10. The Radar is given, not built. "Here's a radar we recommend to start… Just three nice reps. Simple. It's there. So we're not getting them to get out their phone and spend ten minutes trying to build it." Sixty seconds in the room to swap one for their own. — 2026-09-07, ratified D-0130
  11. The room leaves rehearsing ONE rep. The Radar still holds three. Different objects. — 2026-09-08, D-0131
  12. Peak and retrieval, both. Keep the peak at beat 13; add a silent cold recall between the peak and the Radar. — 2026-09-08, D-0131
  13. Both analogies stay — braking and physical-health-vs-physical-fitness. "they explain different things — one shows the gap… the other explains the category by comparison to the physical capacity of the body." — 2026-09-08, D-0131
  14. The braking analogy replaces the driving example. Nobody was ever taught to brake; the cost is a life getting smaller, not a crash. — 2026-09-07, founder capture; built in D-0130
  15. The finish does not crescendo. "we get to the finish, and the finish doesn't end on something crazy. It's: hey, this is practising, and this is how we can practise." — 2026-09-07
  16. The promises are distributed, not stacked. No-disclosure at minute 0, the safety door immediately before the first thing anyone does, the honest limit inside the argument. — D-0130
  17. Hands up is allowed for recognition, never for disclosure. ⚑ Corrected by Hunter 2026-09-09 — this was previously recorded as a flat ban and that was wrong. "If it's a hands up, if you've ever heard of this before, yeah, we want them to feel involved… If I know that you know, that we know together… I think that's actually beneficial." Allowed: have you heard of this, do you recognise this, have you been in a situation like this — questions about shared knowledge and shared experience, which build the social norm. ⛔ Never: "hands up if you've had a bad day recently" or anything asking a person to disclose their own state. The self-directed poll at beat 2 is unchanged — that one they answer to themselves. — 2026-09-09; supersedes the flat reading of D-0131 and founder capture §5
  18. Participants do not place themselves in the four positions. The mental-health/mental-fitness matrix is taught, not self-applied. — standing ruling, 24-THE-PLAN-HUNTER-ASKED-FOR.md
  19. Push low friction / high friction hard, and put it in the Introduction. "I think it's so important that we really push down low friction, high friction… So, so important we practise in the low friction moments." — 2026-09-08
  20. Length is not the constraint. "I don't think eighteen's too much for the flow, if we're speaking and it's interactive and we're explaining." — 2026-09-07
  21. A slide count is not design authority. "this has every right to be more than 38 slides." — 2026-08-13, 80-learning/L-062
  22. The personal story is optional, never baked in. "I don't think that should be in every single thing, but it's something I can speak to if I want to." Every card carrying personal history needs a neutral version too. — 2026-09-08 §29
  23. One consolidated take-home leave-behind, premade and identical, nothing written on it. "they need to be bringing paper, which is an extra cost for us, and they're probably just gonna chuck it in the bin." No printed prompts in the hour. — 2026-08-27, D-0112; 2026-09-07 ("We won't have printed ones.")
  24. The return session is a check-in, not a classification exercise. Branching design, six modules, thresholds, the eight-response floor and the paper-slip vote are all retired. "We're not trying to capture… If we can keep things digital, we can keep things simple." — 2026-08-30, D-0114
  25. The manager session is a separate product, never a compression of the participant foundation and never a double-up. "The manager session shouldn't be a double up of those other sessions… it's a different session with a different purpose, a different intention, and different outcomes we're wanting." — 2026-09-09, 03-MANAGER-SESSION-DESIGN.md
  26. The manager session is a planning session with an intention, and the working block is its centre. "I think it's in that manager session where we can work with the people, and they can come up with something that they think works for their team." — 2026-09-09
  27. No exclusion rule for a manager sitting with their own reports; the session runs identically. "I don't really understand that. I don't think this actually has anything to do with a boss or someone seeing it." — 2026-09-01 / 2026-09-03, D-0123
  28. Foundations' differentiator this cycle is the deepest individual teaching, not organisational readiness. Route B stays built and gated but is not a marketed differentiator. — 2026-08-27, D-0110
  29. Route B is agreement, not live design — "do we agree we want this, understand it, value it", selecting from options worked out with managers beforehand, not inventing them in the room. — 2026-08-27, D-0112

29a. The shift-tool menu IS in the Introduction — shown and spoken through, never performed. ⚑ Hunter 2026-09-09, correcting a proposal to drop it from the hour entirely. "the shift tool menu should be in the introduction, but it's there to show them, and we can speak through them. And while I'm on stage, while I'm speaking, I can give examples as to what each of those things could be. And, again, why that actually helps shift our state." He works through examples of each tool and why it moves a person from too high or too much to workable. The room still does not perform one — ruling 6 is untouched, and practising the menu stays in Essentials and Foundations. Closes contradiction A.

29c. The moment gallery is mandatory in Foundations, and gets made time for in Essentials if it can be. ⚑ Hunter 2026-09-09, on being shown it had been lost: "that should never have been lost… if we want to, we'll make time for it in the essentials, but it has to be in the foundations." Five arenas on the wall, walk and privately note three, no disclosure, no group formation, with the skill-referenced selection instruction and the seated/silent equivalent both required. — 26-RECOVERED-FOUNDATIONS-DEVICES.md

29d. Application studios run in Foundations only. "We could do the application studio. Yes. And the foundations only." The room splits by managing myself vs responding to another person, never by life domain — because nobody learns anything about your life from which studio you picked. ⛔ The facilitator demonstrates one complete worked example first; non-negotiable. — 2026-09-09

29e. The shift tools are the four on the live website, not K-07's locked names. ⚑ Hunter 2026-09-09: "This isn't the category for shift tools - refer to website html i did for Alysse." Through your body · through your attention · through your thinking · with other people, all answering too much, too little, or workable — too much shift down, too little shift up. ⚠ K-07/D-0083 still record Move it / Zoom in or out / Ask a different question / Bring someone in, and the website marks its own wording as a copy trial pending a decision record. That record is now owed — the trial wording is going into a delivered product. — 2026-09-09

29b. The Leadership Community sign-up goes in every service. ⚑ Hunter 2026-09-09, correcting a proposal to keep it off the paid hour. "I think that should be in every single service that we do. It's linking and showing people what we have and how they can maintain the practice or get involved or connect to other people." Closes contradiction C. ⚠ D-0111 §3 still records the Leadership Community as not authorised for build — the sign-up cannot point at something that does not exist yet, and that build gate is now on the critical path for all three products.

2 · Content rulings — what is sayable, what is not

  1. The five skills are mentioned in EVERY product, with why they matter — and taught in depth only in Essentials and Foundations. "the five skills should be mentioned in all of them… mentioning the skills and why those skills are important. Then in the essentials and the foundations, we can go into a bit more depth or detail about the specific skills… perhaps it's going through proper examples." In the Introduction: named with a rationale, not defined one by one, not practised, and "I'm not going to teach you all five in an hour" travels with the names. — 2026-09-09 extending D-0130
  2. The Human Operating System's tier one — Passenger, Engine, Driver — explains the knowing–doing gap in the hour. "Why is the knowing–doing gap a thing? And that's what we can explain — the driver, the passenger, the engine." The wider four stay in Essentials and Foundations. — 2026-09-08 §30; 2026-09-07
  3. Pathways and rewiring CAN be explained as mechanism. Blocking the mechanism is over-cautious; the claim is what K-08 bars, not the explanation. — standing ruling, 24-THE-PLAN-HUNTER-ASKED-FOR.md; wording unresolved, 2026-09-08 §15
  4. "We can't teach you skills. We can teach you the process." "it's up to you to practise that, to build the skills, and then apply it in the life you're living." — 2026-09-08 §13
  5. "Can, not will." "there are skills that can, not will, improve how you navigate life's moments." — DURABLE, 90-meta/agent-context-v1/13-founder-voice-v2-claim-limits.md, 2026-08-09
  6. State plainly what MFC is not claiming. "We're not trying to create the most mentally fit individuals ever — you will never, ever feel anxious or overwhelmed. That's not possible." — 2026-09-08 §18
  7. Where the environment is the real problem, MFC is not the answer, and says so. "Just because we have skills, that doesn't replace an intense, horrific environment. That's the truth." — DURABLE, 13-...-claim-limits.md
  8. MFC runs alongside treatment, never as a replacement for therapy or clinical care. — DURABLE, 13-...-explaining-mental-fitness.md
  9. The claim is the access and retrieval gap for the everyday person, not novelty of the loop. "it exists in the therapy rooms… but that's not being made with the intention of every single human being able to have that. That's the gap we're speaking about." — 2026-08-06, L-033
  10. Do not claim the loop is novel, and do not claim Stop/Shift/Do was invented. The surviving claim: nobody should need therapy to access it, plus Shift through the body. — DURABLE, 13-...-category-and-competitors.md
  11. The organisational-outcome formula is target-and-cite, never assertion. "this is how we think it will… that's an outcome. That's not why we're doing it." — 2026-08-19, D-0104
  12. Nothing may be said about the framework that has not been said and approved. "there's some things that I'm reading that we've never ever said before, and it's never been approved before." — 2026-08-23, L-081
  13. A rep counts by attempt, toward what matters — not by outcome. "the outcome doesn't tell whether it counts." Locked definition: "catching a moment and choosing your next move, on purpose, toward what matters." — D-0107, 2026-08-24
  14. The basis is thinking, feeling, acting, connecting. "In every moment, we're either thinking, we're feeling, we're acting, we're connecting. That's a process all humans have." — 2026-08-31, D-0117
  15. The sleep/movement/food/rest layer is called The Basics. "i don't love engine basics… if we say engine basics people need to know what the engine is." — 2026-08-24, D-0108
  16. External statistics are wanted and must be real. "I think what could be good in these talks is if we bring in a few stats — and I don't mean stats from us." No number enters a room without a registered source; the hospice-regrets study and the ~85% coffee figure are out until registered. — 2026-09-08 §4; D-0130
  17. The manager scope rule holds in full. Workload, staffing, safety and one person behaving badly are not habits, and a skill does not replace a bad environment. — kept, 2026-09-09, 03-MANAGER-SESSION-DESIGN.md
  18. A quiet, slow or flat employee is not a technique, and managers are told not to go looking for what their team wrote. — kept, 2026-09-09
  19. The 120,000 mental reps figure is participation in a 2025 campaign, never evidence of practice or behaviour change. "It wasn't crazy defined." — DURABLE, 13-...-hunter-formation.md
  20. Publication markings on founder-story items are binding. The suicide losses are do-not-publish; several other items are ask-first. — DURABLE, 13-...-hunter-formation.md

3 · Register and voice rulings — how it sounds

  1. High-friction workplace moments, not struggle moments. "I don't think it's about the struggle moments. It's about the high friction moments in the workplace." — 2026-09-09, 03-MANAGER-SESSION-DESIGN.md
  2. Open on the human, not the limitation. We all think, feel, act and connect — in every part of a life — and nobody ever taught us this. — 2026-09-07
  3. It is not on them. "It's not on you. It has always happened. You have not learned these things — and that's a problem, not a fault." — 2026-09-08 §23
  4. Market it like fitness, not like deficit. "It's not 'be less unhealthy.' It's to be stronger, to be healthier, to be fitter. To live the life you want to live." — 2026-09-08 §24
  5. Simplicity is the offer, against the wellness noise. "It's really hard to tell what's accurate… So what we're trying to do is bring everything to the simplest lens — something you can understand, that you can action." — 2026-09-08 §3
  6. Assume nothing. "We need to assume that these people have never ever heard of thoughts and feelings before." — 2026-09-08 §1
  7. Hunter's own phrasing is the copy. A generated alternative is offered beside it, never substituted. "My wording is way better… I feel you skimmed the meeting." — 2026-08-16, L-068
  8. No em dashes in MFC copy. — Hunter's explicit instruction, 13-...-value-proposition.md, 2026-08-09
  9. Copy works by recognition, not persuasion. "I'm not trying to make you care about why physical fitness is important." — CURRENT, 13-...-value-proposition-individual.md
  10. Not markety. He rejected a five-benefit draft: "I don't love this personally… I feel it's too markety." — CURRENT, same file
  11. Category-defining language, never a generic wellness tagline. The "X, for Y" tagline shape is banned. — 2026-08-02, L-014
  12. Honesty must not read as apologetic. "I don't want us to shoot ourselves in the foot… be precise, be powerful." — CURRENT, 13-...-value-proposition.md
  13. Not over-hedged, not clinically over-cautious, in committee and board prose as much as in copy. — 2026-08-31, L-084
  14. Shift is amber, not yellow, in the traffic-light teaching. — DURABLE, 13-...-explaining-mental-fitness.md
  15. "Strengthen", not "build"; never "train your mind" as a hero line. Endorsed opening: "you were never taught this, right, but we can actually learn this." — 2026-08-16, L-068
  16. Never "Manager Radar" or "Team Radar". The manager's construct is enabling conditions. — 2026-09-09, 03-MANAGER-SESSION-DESIGN.md; K-07
  17. Items presented as parallel must be the same category type. "on the field, that's not the same thing as a parent… As a parent has heaps of moments within it." — 2026-08-26, L-082
  18. Every section and sentence is intentional and not interchangeable. "every section and sentence is there with intention… not just random and I can switch it." — 2026-08-01, L-030
  19. Bold, not shocking. "Don't be afraid to think of things that haven't been done before" — but unconventional ideas carry their reasoning, and this is not a licence for shock tactics. — 2026-08-03, 11-founder-voice-agent-operating-model.md

4 · Product and commercial rulings

  1. Everything is inside the price. The return session, the written report and the manager session are not optional extensions, not separately contracted and not separately quoted. — 2026-08-30, D-0113
  2. A report is issued at every cohort size. "we are not doing a 10 respondent reporting floor! Should be a report no matter the number - just what we can report on changes!" What scales is what the report may contain, never whether it exists. — 2026-09-09, D-0132
  3. The three minimum rules are retired — the 12-person case-study minimum, the "never below six at any price" rule, and the n≥20 report floor. Designed for 3 to 20 people. — 2026-09-03, D-0121
  4. The manager's seat counts against the cap and is charged at the per-head rate. "Count and charge the seat - as it's based on their own lives and what happens i think." — 2026-09-03, D-0123
  5. Three products. Small Team Essentials is retired. — 2026-09-07, D-0129
  6. The Introduction is "The Mental Fitness Hour" and is not sold as a taster. — 2026-09-07, D-0129
  7. The digital Introduction is the entry rung, at $600, and it is the only published price. Everything else is quoted until ten quotes exist. — 2026-09-07, D-0129
  8. Essentials is $1,550 + $60 per person, capped at 20; Foundations $3,900 + $95 per person. "At the low price of a $1048 floor I think is way too low. We are providing a lot of value." — 2026-09-07, D-0129 Amendment 1 (supersedes D-0125, D-0128, D-0113 on figures)
  9. Quarterly check-ins are promised, not contracted. — 2026-09-07, D-0129
  10. An unadvertised concession lane exists across all products — never a published NFP tier. — 2026-09-07, D-0129
  11. MFC will work toward GST registration; every figure is ex GST until it lands. — 2026-09-07, D-0129
  12. MFC will not turn down a workplace whose real problem is workload and management — but says plainly that the environment is high risk. "No, I wouldn't turn it down. But I would be really clear… It changes the data capture, truthfully." — CURRENT, 13-...-money-committee-succession.md
  13. One flagship, not fifty programmes. — AG-165 (Jake Pepper), held by Hunter as the constraint the naming-not-teaching compromise protects, D-0130
  14. The framework is STABLE, not locked. ⚑ "Locked" retired by Hunter 2026-09-09 — he had changed the framework three times after locking it (D-0107, D-0108, D-0117), each time correctly, and the phrase was still being quoted back as though it barred change. Don't reopen it without reason; changes come from Hunter. Closes contradiction D. — 2026-09-09, supersedes the 2026-08-09 CURRENT/JUDGEMENT capture
  15. Complexity in the scaffolding, simplicity at the point of retrieval. Three steps, not four or five. Five public skills, not seven. Radar of three to five moments, held loosely. — DURABLE, 13-...-design-rationale.md
  16. Adults, not schools. The gap is adult delivery infrastructure. — DURABLE, 13-...-explaining-mental-fitness.md
  17. Community first, category second. Get people in the room, then explain the category. — DURABLE, 13-...-hunter-formation.md

5 · Working-method rulings — how the system operates

  1. He states an outcome and receives a converged result. "There's a goal. I give you a goal. You then give me the result. I don't care how that result gets done." — 2026-08-03, 11-founder-voice-agent-operating-model.md
  2. Internal back-and-forth never reaches him. "None of that should ever come back to me… Remove me. I need work done." — 2026-08-03
  3. He must not be the weakness detector. "I also do not understand why I am still the person identifying these gaps." — 2026-08-01, L-009
  4. He sees the thing, rendered, before anything is scored or reported as passing. "I am yet to even read or see the manager session nor the other sessions we have… this is a problem." — 2026-09-09, 03-MANAGER-SESSION-DESIGN.md
  5. A theme he raises repeatedly is a standing defect, not a queue of requests. — 2026-08-02, L-021
  6. Do not ask permission for already-authorised reversible work. "please fix - i shouldn't have to keep telling you what to do." — 2026-08-04, L-028
  7. Do not hand a settled decision back to him. "why are we going around in circles - this should be very straight forward." — 2026-08-02, L-016
  8. Don't give first answers. "you need to workshop this… test this with your agents… don't just give me the first answer." — 2026-08-03, L-025
  9. Diverge before narrowing. "don't narrow the scope because work has been done… consider everything", and "just because the evidence may not be fully established it doesn't make it poor." — 2026-08-12, L-057
  10. Research agents look outward for what is better and why. "get our research agent to maybe find things that might be better than what we currently have, and why that's better." — 2026-09-07
  11. Compose in his explanatory logic, not just check against it. "Do we need to create an agent that's like me — but in this world, in our system… this is how Hunter would like to communicate or explain this." — 2026-09-07
  12. Evidence offered to him must be something he can see. "i nevver see a hook - it isn't visible for me." — 2026-08-09, L-040
  13. Never defer to him a fact checkable in the vault or on the website. — 2026-08-03, L-023
  14. Content readiness is not launch readiness; stop producing blocker lists. "There shouldn't be eight things or six things that we need to achieve first… Stop it." — 2026-08-16, L-067
  15. Stop over-gating. "our current ruling system is too heavily gated, and it's impacting how the products and how we deliver and how we explain things." An internally-invented gate loses to a named advisor's position. — 2026-09-01, L-088 / CLAUDE.md §4a
  16. The committee governs; Claude does not. "As a charity… we have in real life committee members that can help and be that governing layer. I don't need you to be that for me." — 2026-08-13, L-064
  17. His pushback is method, not disapproval. Answer on the merits; do not concede reflexively. "It's okay to get things wrong." — DURABLE, 13-...-hunter-formation.md
  18. A named professional's artefact is authority inside their discipline — changes are proposed and marked, never silently replaced. — 2026-08-16, L-068
  19. Anything external-facing is drafted, not sent. — 2026-08-03, 11-founder-voice-agent-operating-model.md
  20. Merge finished work back into one current hub. No duplicates, no orphans. "I don't see a snapshot of everything… We don't have duplicates or doubles or confusing stuff." — 2026-08-12, L-061
  21. The vault is authoritative over the Drive source. "The latest things will be the correct things — please ensure our vault is updated." — 2026-08-31, D-0117
  22. He is not asking for a total redo. "I'm not saying redo it all. No. We've already got a start." — 2026-09-09

⛔ ANTI-RULINGS — refused, and re-proposed anyway

This section matters most. Every line here has been proposed more than once after being killed.

  1. Per-beat minute allocations in anything shown to Hunter. Refused because a run sheet cannot be locked — every product changes it, so the design re-opened at least four times. "Get rid of the minutes. Get rid of all these things." Last re-proposed 2026-09-08.
  2. Participants placing themselves in the four mental-health/mental-fitness positions. Refused because it is self-diagnosis in a room that was promised nobody has to disclose anything. Last re-proposed 2026-09-08.
  3. Blocking pathways/rewiring as an explanation of mechanism. Refused as over-cautious — the claim is barred, the explanation is not. Last re-proposed 2026-09-08.
  4. A report-suppression floor at any cohort size (n≥20, then n≥10, then n≥5). Refused three times — retired 2026-08-19, again 2026-09-03, again 2026-09-09. "Should be a report no matter the number - just what we can report on changes!" It also meant a buyer could pay full price and receive a delivery confirmation. Last re-proposed 2026-09-09.
  5. Struggle-moment register in the manager session. Refused because the manager room is about high-friction workplace moments, not distress. "I don't think it's about the struggle moments." Last re-proposed 2026-09-09.
  6. Hands up asking a person to disclose their own state — "hands up if you've had a bad day recently." Refused because it manufactures public disclosure in a room promised the opposite. ⚑ Narrowed by Hunter 2026-09-09: a hands-up about shared knowledge or shared experience is NOT refused and is actively wanted — see ruling 17. Last re-proposed 2026-09-08.
  7. Participants building their own Radar in the room. Refused because it costs seven minutes and hands people a blank page. "we're not getting them to get out their phone and spend ten minutes trying to build it." Last re-proposed 2026-09-07.
  8. Butcher's paper, printed prompts, write-on cards, per-person card sets. Refused on cost and retention — "they're probably just gonna chuck it in the bin… that's the truth." Last re-proposed 2026-09-01.
  9. Moving the manager session, the return session or the report outside the price. Refused 2026-08-30 after the exclusions would have put 52–59% of Foundations' costed hours outside the priced product. D-0113.
  10. An eight-response floor, a secret paper ballot, and the TEACH/PRACTICE/IMPLEMENT classification in the return. Refused because "a secret ballot around 'what shall we practise together' signals danger". "We're not trying to capture." — 2026-08-30, D-0114
  11. Excluding a manager from a participant session containing their own reports. Refused twice. "I don't really understand that. I don't think this actually has anything to do with a boss or someone seeing it." Last re-proposed 2026-09-03.
  12. Blocker lists and founder homework before content can ship. Refused: "There shouldn't be eight things or six things that we need to achieve first… Stop it." Recurring.
  13. Leading with caveats instead of the work; reporting "not yet proven" as "cannot be used"; "want me to?" on already-authorised reversible steps. All three named as failures on the same day. "That's what I need with this." — 2026-08-13, L-064
  14. Safeguarding gates enforced by Claude as a prerequisite to delivery. Refused: "Even after what Eimear said - remove the commission and sfeguarding stuff - overly cautious and preventing us progressing." D-0016 is not to be cited as a standing prerequisite. — 2026-08-31, D-0118
  15. Generic wellness taglines and the "X, for Y" shape. Refused 2026-08-02 as non-category-defining; re-proposed repeatedly in copy passes. L-014.
  16. Claiming the loop is novel, or describing the mechanism as "in the same territory as CBT and DBT". Refused — the first does not survive contact with Positive Intelligence; the second "is actually minimising what the other work we've done." — 2026-08-09
  17. A generic safeguarding or claims finding silently rewriting a design Hunter has already ruled on. Refused as the whole reason this file exists: "you're now forgetting everything else that we have." — 2026-09-09

✅ CONTRADICTIONS — ALL SIX CLOSED BY HUNTER, 2026-09-09

Closed the same day they were raised. Three of his answers corrected the recommendation put to him, which is why they were put to him rather than resolved internally.

A · The shift-tool menu — CLOSED, and the recommendation was wrong. Proposed: drop it from the hour, keep it for Essentials and Foundations. Hunter: it stays in the Introduction — shown and spoken through, with worked examples of each tool and why it moves a person from too high or too much to workable. The room still does not perform one. → ruling 29a.

B · Hands up — CLOSED, and the ban was too broad. Hunter: hands up is fine, and beneficial, for recognition — have you heard of this, have you been in a situation like this — because it builds the social norm and makes people feel involved. It is refused only where it asks someone to disclose their own state. → rulings 17 and 113.

C · The community sign-up — CLOSED, and the recommendation was wrong. Proposed: keep it out of the paid hour. Hunter: it goes in every single service. → ruling 29b. ⚠ D-0111 §3 still has the Leadership Community unauthorised for build; that gate is now on the critical path for all three products.

D · "The framework is locked" — CLOSED. Retired. It is stable; changes come from Hunter. → ruling 82.

E · The five skills — CLOSED and extended. Mentioned in every product with why they matter; depth and worked examples in Essentials and Foundations only. → ruling 30. ⛔ Still outstanding, and it is not a decision: four contributors were told the five skills appear in no product. Nobody has told them that reversed.

F · The causal line — WAS NEVER OPEN. Hunter had already ruled on it the same morning, on card 9 of the card set: the arrow goes both ways or it doesn't go, never will deteriorate · protects · preventative · risk factor · mentally unfit · "the research shows", and drop "it's not far-fetched to say that" because it tells the room there is nothing behind it. It was put to him as open in error — a resolved ruling that had not been propagated. → ruling 41 applies.

33 The Quality Checklists

The quality checklists

Hunter, 2026-09-09:

"We've run our agents. We've reviewed it. We've analysed everything. We have ticked every single box of the checklist. Yes, this is now ready. I still haven't reviewed it. So that's a part of the thing that isn't on the checklist."

"If you look at humans — what are the things that make these things great, memorable, can lead to the change? That's what our checklist needs to be built upon."

What this fixes. MFC has 44 executable controls and none of them judges whether any piece of work is any good. A thing can pass every one and still be a session nobody wants to sit in. These checklists ask the other question.

Rule zero — nothing is final until Hunter has read it

This row appears on every session, and it is the last one.

⛔ Has Hunter read this and approved it?

No amount of agent review substitutes for it, and no artefact may be described as final, ready or approved while it reads NO. Hunter, directly: "nothing gets finalised until that happens."

And one row below it will read NO for a long time, deliberately: has this been run with real people? The ledger exists to show the ceiling — once every other box is green, the only thing left is a real room. No further analysis moves it.

Checklist A · An ACTIVITY

Anything a participant does — silent thinking, a physical movement, a paired exchange, a written plan, walking a room. Nine tests. Score each PASS · PARTIAL · FAIL, with a reason.

# Test What a FAIL looks like
A1 Barrier to entry. Can a person do it without standing up, speaking, writing, or being seen to participate? It requires movement, disclosure or a pen with no equivalent offered aloud.
A2 Exposure risk. Can this reveal something about a person they did not choose to reveal — to the facilitator, to a colleague, or to a manager in the room? Choosing a category, a group, or a visible position tells the room something personal.
A3 Mechanism. Is there a real reason this produces the effect claimed, drawn from adjacent established literature and stated as a mechanism, not an outcome? It is an activity because sessions have activities.
A4 Engagement. Will a sceptical adult lean in, or wait it out? It only works for people already bought in.
A5 Dignity. Does this feel like being taken seriously — or like "another bloody activity another organisation is making me do"? It is performative, cute, or asks adults to play.
A6 Thursday value. Does the participant leave with something usable in a real moment, not a nice feeling? The value is entirely inside the room.
A7 Failure mode. When this goes wrong, is there a route the facilitator can actually take — words to say, and somewhere for the person to go if they need it? ⛔ A row that says the route does not exist is a FAIL, not a PASS. A row naming an escalation MFC has not cleared is a FAIL. A row that instructs the facilitator to breach a ruling to recover is a FAIL.
A8 One facilitator. Can one person run it, alone, with 20 people? It needs a second pair of hands MFC does not have.
A9 Accessibility. Does it work seated, silent, and without writing — and is the equivalent offered aloud, before it starts, not on request? ⚡ And does the equivalent survive the whole activity, not just its opening? The equivalent exists on paper but nobody says it. ⛔ Or it is offered at the door and then contradicted by a later instruction — an alternative route that cannot complete the activity is not an alternative route.

⛔ A2 and A9 are gates, not scores. An activity that fails either does not run, whatever else it scores.

Checklist B · A SPOKEN BEAT

Anything the facilitator says that carries an argument. Six tests.

# Test What a FAIL looks like
B1 Cold clarity. Would someone who has never heard any of this follow it, first time, without stopping? It assumes a term, a model or a prior beat.
B2 Curiosity. Does it open a gap the next beat closes — or does it close everything and leave nothing pulling forward? It is complete, correct, and inert.
B3 Recognition. Does a listener see themselves in it, or is it about people in general? It describes a category of person rather than a moment they have had.
B4 Claim safety. K-08 and AG-001: mechanism not outcome, can not will, no causal claim MFC cannot support. An outcome asserted in the present indicative.
B5 His voice. Recognition not persuasion. Not markety. Honest without being apologetic. ⚡ Scored on the words a facilitator actually says — the > quoted lines — never on stage directions, rationale or design notes. It sounds like a brand wrote it. ⛔ Do not score a whole file's punctuation. On 2026-09-10 the corpus held 417 em dashes and only 126 were in spoken text; the manager session, a standing FAIL three passes running, had one. The count rose as the documents got more honest.
B6 Portability. Could someone repeat the point to a colleague that night, in one sentence? It only survives inside the full argument.

Checklist C · A MEASUREMENT COMPONENT

Anything that captures data. Four tests.

# Test What a FAIL looks like
C1 Construct. Does it capture the thing it claims to capture? It measures satisfaction and is reported as change.
C2 Completion. Will people actually finish it, in the conditions it runs in? It assumes a response rate nobody has ever observed.
C3 Privacy. De-identified, no small-cell re-identification, nothing attributable. A number describes a person in a group that size.
C4 Reportability. Can what it produces be said out loud to a buyer within K-08? It generates a figure MFC is not permitted to state.

Checklist D · FLOW — run across a whole session, not a part

Added on Hunter's instruction, 2026-09-09. His words:

"If this was a speech, if this was a conversation — is someone going, yeah, look at the red banana, oh my god bananas, oh my god monkeys? Is there too much jumping around? Is there a case of flow to it?"

# Test What a FAIL looks like
D1 Sequence. Does each beat follow from the one before, or is it a list of good things in an order? Two adjacent beats could swap with no loss.
D2 Curse of knowledge. Is anything explained at a level the audience has not been built up to? A level-five explanation sits beside a level-three one.
D3 Activity fit. Does each activity relate to what was just taught, or is it bolted on? The activity would work equally well anywhere in the session.
D4 One argument. Does the whole session make a single case, or several unrelated ones? It is three good talks in a row.
D5 Load. Is the room asked to do too much, too close together? Two demanding devices back to back with no recovery.

Checklist E · PROPAGATION — run across files, not inside one

⛔ Added 2026-09-10, after the first improvement pass proved every other test blind to this. All twenty-four tests in A–D are within-artefact: they read one file and score it. The four products share one spine, so an edit to the shortest silently breaks the other three and the records that govern them — and on 2026-09-10 that is exactly what happened, within a day of the pattern being named. Not one test could see it.

Run E on every change that touches a shared beat, device, term or ruling. Five tests.

# Test What a FAIL looks like
E1 Orphaned references. After this change, does any other file still name a device, beat or term that no longer exists? A cut device is still referenced in a sibling product, the card set, or a governing record.
E2 Governing records. If the change contradicts 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md, 00-THE-RULINGS.md or a D- record, has that been reconciled or surfaced? The governing record and the product now disagree and nobody said so.
E3 Sibling consistency. Do the four products now give opposite answers to the same question? Three files cut a beat as blocked; the fourth declares the gate invalid and keeps it.
E4 Superseded material marked. Anything this change supersedes carries superseded_by: and a status change in the same change. A file stays on main, fully written, describing a version that no longer exists.
E5 Point-in-time records dated. An analysis or score that describes a prior version is marked as such, not left reading as current. A flow check or assessment is quoted as the current state of a product it no longer describes.

⛔ E1 and E3 are gates. A change that orphans a reference or makes two products contradict each other is not finished, however well it scores on A–D.

⛔ E1 and E4 run across the whole repository, or they do not run. On 2026-09-10 E1 was scored against a hand-picked five-file table in the same pass that made it a gate, and passed — while two live orphans sat outside the list, one of them in the page Hunter reads. A propagation test scoped to the files you already knew about tests nothing. Grep the repo; do not work from a list someone compiled.

⚠ And count what a reference DOES, not that it exists. A file saying "this device was cut" contains the device's name. On 2026-09-10 raw counts of a cut device rose while the defect was being closed. Read the line. A correction is not an orphan.

The anti-gaming rules — read before scoring anything

⛔ Added 2026-09-10, after the first improvement pass cleared eight failures without changing one word a participant would experience.

Rule 1 — Score the participant's experience, not the artefact. A finding closed by deleting the thing is not closed unless the participant is no better off without it. A device moved somewhere that does not exist yet is not fixed, it is homeless — and the score must go DOWN, not up, because yesterday the participant had it and today they do not.

Rule 2 — A record of a route is not a route. This is A7's whole failure. Writing a table row saying what a facilitator would do satisfies nothing if the thing it points at has not been built, cleared, or written. Ask what actually happens to the person in the room.

Rule 3 — A disclosure is not a fix. Naming a problem honestly in a file is worth a great deal and it is not a score. A design that says "this fails and here is why" still fails.

Rule 4 — Verify the changelog, never quote it. A fixer's account of what it changed is a claim, not evidence. On 2026-09-10 a changelog stated five endings had been cut to one; two had gone, and the omitted one had been lengthened in the same pass. That reached the founder as fact. Re-derive every claim from the file.

Rule 5 — A test that cannot be failed, or cannot be passed, is not a test. If a criterion fails 100% of items twice running, or clears without the product changing, the criterion is the defect. Say so in the score. The checklist is under assessment too.

The readiness ledger — one per session

Seven rows. This is what Hunter reads to know where a product actually stands.

Row Means
Built A complete design or script exists.
Checked against the rulings Run against all 124, including the 17 anti-rulings.
Adversarially attacked A fresh context tried to break it, and findings were applied.
Gap-checked against Hunter's own words His captures read against the product for what is absent.
Claims-checked K-08, AG-001 and the advisor register applied to every participant-facing line.
Compass approved The founder lens has said what Hunter would say — see below.
⛔ Hunter has read and approved Nothing is final without this.
Run with real people Expected to read NO. This is the ceiling of what AI review can establish.

How options are presented

Hunter's instruction: three options per activity, and no recommendation from me.

"For each activity you present in Essentials and Foundations, you should give me three options… And I don't want to know the one you recommend."

Each option is scored on four columns, and the fourth is the one nobody writes down:

Column The question
Barrier How easy is it to take part without exposing yourself?
Evidence What actually backs the mechanism?
Engagement Will a sceptical adult lean in?
⚡ Resentment risk How likely is a participant to think: another activity someone is making me do?

Resentment risk decides whether the room leans in or waits it out, and it is the column that is never on a design checklist. Hunter: "if they're not actually open and wanting to learn and practise it, it's not applicable, and it's a waste of our time and their time."

What this is not

These checklists do not establish that anything works. They establish that a thing is well made, safe, in his voice, and worth a participant's time. Whether it produces change is a question only a real room answers, and no row here should ever be read as evidence that it does.

22 The Participant Foundation

The participant foundation

What Hunter ruled, 2026-09-08: "instead of making that the 60 etc — why can't that, but an improved version that we test with our agents, be the foundation for all services — and the manager session is completely different."

The inversion, stated plainly. Until today the 60-minute Introduction was the base and Essentials (90) and Foundations (240) widened it. That is now reversed. There is ONE participant foundation. The 58, the 90 and the 240 are compressions of it. Nothing is added as a product gets longer; things are given back.

The foundation is not a fourth product. Nobody ever delivers "the foundation." It is the complete participant argument, at full depth, from which every participant-facing service is cut.

⛔ The manager session is NOT a compression of this file. It is a separate product with a different audience, a different job and a different organising principle — it teaches the environment, not the practice. It lives in 60-projects/workshop-evidence-informed-adult/16-from-scratch-redesign-v1/03-MANAGER-SESSION-DESIGN.md and must never be derived from, or reconciled against, the movements below.

Why fourteen movements, and not seventeen

The foundation has FOURTEEN movements. They are D-0130's fourteen beats, unchanged in order and in function.

An earlier unfiled proposal claimed seventeen movements and 270 "natural" minutes, with per-movement compression ranks and floors deriving to 56 / 81 / 194. Those seventeen movements and their floors are not reproduced here and are not treated as fact. A-24 refused them as UNAUDITABLE, correctly: no file ever existed to check them against, and the totals they derived to were the totals 02-MERGED §12 already states — which means the derivation was fitted to a known answer rather than producing one.

Where seventeen came from, and why it is not the movement count. Hunter's own talk (15-inputs/hunter-notes/workshop/2026-09-07-founder-the-talk-as-hunter-gives-it.md) is laid out in eighteen numbered steps, not seventeen. Those eighteen are the arc as he happens to say it — and he disowned them as a running order in the same file: "that's the arc of what I've said. Right? It doesn't mean it's the best arc." The capture's own instruction is explicit: "Anyone building from this file must treat the arc as source material, not as a running order."

So: fourteen, because fourteen is the only movement count that exists in a governing record. It is D-0130's ruling, it is built out in 02-MERGED §1, and it is written as spoken words in 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-INTRODUCTION-60.md. Every one of Hunter's eighteen arc steps is carried by one of the fourteen; the mapping is in the table below, and no arc step is orphaned.

The fourteen movements — what each one is FOR

"For" means the job it does to the listener. A movement is not a topic; it is a change of state in the room. If a movement's for is already achieved, the movement is finished, however many minutes remain.

# Movement What it is FOR What breaks without it Hunter's arc step
1 The human, and the promise To have every person in the room recognise themselves before anything is diagnosed. And to remove the single largest source of in-room anxiety — being made to speak — inside the warmth rather than as a disclaimer The room spends the hour privately braced for being asked to share, and hears the rest as a lecture about a deficiency 1
2 The gap, and the car that never learned to brake To convert "I already know this" into "I have never once practised this." The braking image does it: a life getting smaller through an unnamed unpractised skill Nothing that follows has a problem to solve. This is the hook and there is no substitute for it 2
3 The door ⛔ To tell people, before the first thing anyone does, what to do if this gets heavy. Placed here because it must precede the first experience, not follow it A safeguarding floor is missed, and it is missed at the exact moment it becomes needed — (advisor floor, AG-004)
4 The breath. Experience, with no name on it ⛔ To give the room a Stop before the word Stop exists. Experience first, name second. This is the entire close of AG-144 — the first thing a participant does is at minute 6.5, not minute 47 The design returns to its worst recorded failure: content for forty-seven minutes before anyone does anything Hunter's own worked example, addendum
5 What that was, and what mental fitness actually is ⛔ To name what just happened, and only then to define the category. Definitions land because there is now an experience underneath them The definition is abstract, and the hour becomes a talk about a concept 3
6 The four, and the five skills named To place mental health and mental fitness in the four real positions, and to name the five skills with a reason — named, not taught AG-146 breaches (naming something a participant cannot enact) unless "I'm not going to teach you all five in an hour" travels with the names 3
7 Muscle memory. Skills get built To establish, from something everyone already believes, that a mind builds skill the way a body does Movement 8 arrives as an assertion instead of an answer 4
8 The practice site is the life you're already living To remove the time objection entirely: no fifteen minutes a day, the moments are the site. Carries the environment boundary and the manager handoff, once ⛔ The offer becomes another thing to fit in, and the honest limit about environment is never stated 5
9 Stop, Shift, Do — and the unit ⛔ To name the method and the unit of practice, including the State Check (named aloud) and a rep counts when you attempt it, toward what matters There is no method. The counting rule without its direction leaves the rule with no object 6
10 Specificity of practice, and the knowing–doing gap The centre. To establish that generalised training does not transfer to the specific moment, and that the gap is not a missing skill. Carries the honest limit at minute 34, inside the argument The product has no differentiator and no honesty. Losing this loses the reason MFC exists rather than a section 7, 10, 12
11 Run it on a real moment To make the method concrete on moments people recognise. Two scenarios, because one is a trick and two is a pattern. Contains the private thirty seconds of selection The method stays theoretical and nobody has privately chosen anything 11
12 It will miss. Grace, with a number To pre-empt the first failed week. One in three is doing it properly; this is repetition, not a chain The first miss reads as failure and the practice is abandoned before it starts 9
13 The ripple — the peak, deliberately not the end To widen from the individual to the people around them, and to make the mission askable. Ends "and this is how you can help us" The hour is about self-improvement only, and there is no invitation into the movement 13, 14, 15, 16, 18
14 The Radar given. The swap. The flat finish To put an artefact in people's hands that survives the room, stacked onto something already happening — and to end flat, not on a crescendo Nothing exists on Thursday. And if the sixty-second swap goes, D-0008 reopens immediately ⛔ 8, 17

⚑ Beat 14 renamed 2026-09-10 (Checklist E1/E2 — this is the governing record and it was stale). It previously read "The Radar given. Habit stacking. The flat finish." Verified against 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-INTRODUCTION-60.md on 2026-09-10, not against a changelog: habit stacking is no longer a beat of its own in any product. It survives as one spoken line inside the sixty-second swap — "don't let it be a notification… look at it when you're already doing something. The coffee. The drive. The walk in." The purpose column is unchanged and still correct, because stacked onto something already happening is what that line does. What changed is that it is no longer a separate ending. ⛔ The fold-and-hold ritual and the portable sentence handed back are cut outright. ⛔ Contested for the fold-and-hold: D-0131 §4 item 1 (status: decided) restores it and stands until Hunter rules — the former "must not be restored" instruction was an agent overriding a founder decision and is withdrawn, 2026-09-10. See the marking on D-0131. The portable sentence is unaffected by that record.

Hunter's arc steps with no movement of their own: none. Steps 1–18 all land. Steps 3, 7, 11, 12 and 13 are each carried across more than one movement, which is the honest reading of the mapping, not a tidy one-to-one.

The two rules that govern all fourteen at every depth

  1. ⛔ A room cannot perform a Do. Hunter's ruling, 2026-09-08, now written into the hour: the room is told so plainly, and the reps used are ones participants have already done in their own lives — the phone is his named example. No staged Do exercise, at any depth, ever. This binds the 240 as hard as it binds the 58.
  2. Nobody speaks unless they want to. Nothing is asked out loud. Nothing is collected. Nobody writes anything. It is a keynote. Max 20 participants with one facilitator; 30 only with a co-facilitator (AG-131 / AG-160).

The compression rule

Full depth is 194 minutes of content. That is the foundation at its widest articulation — every movement fully worked, delivered as Foundations (240 = 194 content + 40 breaks + 6 buffer).

Compression is narrowing, never removal.

RULE 1 — No movement is ever removed. All fourteen are present at 58, at 90 and at 240. A movement compresses toward its floor; it never reaches zero.

RULE 2 — Order never changes. One shape, one order, one set of words in Hunter's mouth, at every depth. He never has to relearn where he is.

RULE 3 — Nothing is ARGUED at 90 or 240 that is not argued at 58. The argument is the invariant. Depth and practice are what widen.

⚑ AMENDED 2026-09-09 on Hunter's ruling. It previously read "nothing is TAUGHT at 90 or 240 that is not present at 58," and that wording was a live defect. The 58 is a keynote in which nobody writes, speaks or performs anything — so the old rule forbade Foundations from containing rehearsal, pair work, the written Radar, the moment gallery, application studios or toolkit practice: every strong participant device MFC owns. This file already broke it three times in its own text. Hunter's ruling of 2026-09-09 — that the moment gallery "has to be in the foundations" and application studios run "the foundations only" — settles it: a longer product gives the same argument with more depth and with practice the hour cannot carry.

RULE 4 — Compression is monotonic. No movement is ever longer in a shorter product. The one deliberately flat row is movement 3, the door: at 58 and 90 it is the same length, because making it longer turns a reassurance into a warning.

RULE 5 — The never-compress floor is a list, not a percentage. Movements 3, 4, 5, 9, movement 6's "I'm not going to teach you all five in an hour", movement 8's environment boundary and manager handoff, movement 12's one-in-three number, and movement 14's QR plus the sixty-second swap are at their floor already at 58 and cannot be compressed further in any product.

RULE 6 — The buffer is not compressible. It is the thing compression protects.

The three compressions, as the sources state them

Movement 58 (Introduction) 90 (Essentials) 194 (Foundations)
1 The human + promise 2 2 3
2 The gap + braking 3 4 8

The 58 column is today's script, not 02-MERGED §12's table, and the difference is deliberate. Hunter ruled on 2026-09-08 that the Introduction runs 58 minutes of content with a 2-minute buffer (previously 56 + 4). The two minutes went into movement 9, which 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT now runs 23–30 rather than 23–28. Every subsequent movement in the script starts two minutes later than 02-MERGED §12 says. 02-MERGED §12 and §1 are therefore stale on this point and have not been amended — see Open / unaudited, item 2.

The order compression happens in

Predetermined, so it is never a judgement call at minute 44 with a clock running.

At 58 (02-MERGED §5, derived from script word counts at 120–130 wpm, rounded down): C1 movement 13 to two sentences (−2.5) · C2 movement 11 to one scenario, keep the morning one (−2.5) · C3 movement 10's knowing–doing worked examples (−2.5) · C4 movement 8's four places named not worked (−1.5) · C5 movement 7 to two sentences (−1.5). Honest recoverable total: 10.5 minutes. The CPR comparison in movement 2 is marked in the script as the first cut if the room runs long, ahead of C1.

At 90: each cut reverts one movement to exactly its 58-minute duration, which makes double-counting structurally impossible. E1 movement 10 (12→8) · E2 movement 11 (11→7) · E3 movement 13 (8→6) · E4 movement 8 (6→4) · E5 movement 6 (5→3). Recoverable: 14 minutes.

At 240: F1 group practice to one round (M11 36→27) · F2 movement 10's counter-arguments (28→20) · F3 the two participant-chosen scenarios (M11 27→19, stated in composition order after F1) · F4 the reflection rep in M12 (10→4) · F5 the written Radar (M14 16→12) · F6 break 3 absorbed (−10). Recoverable: 45 minutes.

What this file does and does not replace

  • It does not supersede 02-MERGED-DESIGN-ALL-THREE-PRODUCTS.md. That file remains the built-out design — the words, the departures, the leave-behind, the constraints. This file is the structural rule that governs it under the inversion.
  • It does not supersede 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-INTRODUCTION-60.md. Where the two disagree on minutes, the script wins for the 58, because it is what Hunter amended on 2026-09-08.
  • It does not supersede D-0130. The fourteen movements are D-0130's beats.
  • It supersedes nothing. No existing vault file was replaced to write this. The only thing it replaces is an unfiled HTML artifact and chat, neither of which is a vault record — which is precisely the problem Hunter ruled on today.

Open / unaudited — every number in this file that is not grounded

Read this before quoting any figure above.

  1. Every duration in the table is reasoned, never observed. MFC has delivered zero cohorts. No participant has ever sat through any version of this, in any build. This governs all forty-two cells of the compression table.
  2. 02-MERGED §1 and §12 still say 56 + 4 and put movement 9 at five minutes. The script says 58 + 2 and seven minutes. The 90 and 240 columns were derived against the 56 version and have not been re-derived against 58. Whether the 90's monotonicity still holds at movement 9 (58 column now 7, 90 column 8 — it does, by one minute) is checked here; nothing else in those columns has been rechecked. This is a live inconsistency across three files, not a rounding difference.
  3. The 90 and 240 per-movement minutes have no independent basis. They are 02-MERGED §12's widening ladder, asserted as design intent, and no words exist for them — there is no 90-minute script and no 240-minute script. Only the 58 has a written script whose durations can be checked against word counts.
  4. The 194 / 81 figures are internally consistent, not externally validated. They sum, and a total that sums is not a design that works.
  5. The 10.5 / 14 / 45 recoverable totals rest on a 120–130 wpm delivery rate that is itself an estimate. ⛔ THE NEXT CLAUSE WAS FALSE AND IS WITHDRAWN, 2026-09-08. It read "Only the 58's rows were derived from actual script word counts" — they were not. A fresh-context adversarial pass counted the written script directly and an independent recount confirmed it: 4,260 spoken words across all fourteen beats = ~34 minutes at 125 wpm, 38.7 even at a slow 110. With every specified silence added it reaches roughly 36–41 minutes against a 58-minute allocation. To fill 58 minutes the facilitator would have to speak at 73 words per minute; deliberate keynote delivery is 110–130. The per-beat minutes here are design intent at every depth, including the 58 — and this sentence was the one licensing every downstream number, including the 90 and 240 ladders and the recoverable totals in the cut orders. THE DURATION MODEL IS OPEN AND MUST BE REBUILT FROM THE WORDS. Do not quote any figure in this table until it is. (Superseded original text follows.) ~~Only the 58's rows were derived from actual script word counts;~~ the 90's and 240's rows are duration subtractions of the same kind that produced the old C4 defect.
  6. The ~85% of Australians drink coffee figure is unverified and is cut on sourcing (AG-200). It is not used in this file and must not be reintroduced to any movement until registered in 10-sources/.
  7. The hospice-regrets study is cited in Hunter's arc (step 14), is not in 10-sources/, and is cut on the same ground. Movement 13 is written to work without it.
  8. No fresh-context adversarial pass has ever run against the fourteen-beat structure — not when D-0130 created it, not when 02-MERGED built it out, not when the script was written, and not on this file. One should run before any participant hears it.

03 Delivery Script Introduction 60

The hour, as it is said

Register: teaching. Second person, unhedged, analogies doing the work, lands flat. Composed from 16-how-hunter-communicates.md §10, not from committee-transcript sentences.

Marking. [H] = Hunter's own words, from the 2026-09-07 capture or approved script — do not rewrite. [H*] = his words, grammar tidied for speech; the tidy is listed at the foot of this file. [D] = drafted for him to make his own. [BRIDGE] = connective tissue, drafted. ⛔ = never cut. C1–C5 = the cut order, marked where the cut lands.

Four rules that govern every line: nothing is asked out loud about a person's own state · nothing is collected · every question about the participant themselves is asked, held briefly, and answered by him — no answers taken · nobody writes anything.

⚑ Amended by Hunter, 2026-09-09 — the previous flat "no hands taken" was too broad and he said so directly. Hands up is allowed, and wanted, for recognition — have you heard of this, have you been in a situation like this — because it makes people feel involved and builds the social norm: "If I know that you know, that we know together… I think that's actually beneficial." ⛔ Never for disclosure — never hands up if you've had a bad day. The self-directed poll at beat 2 is unchanged: that one they answer to themselves. Rulings 17 and 113.

BEAT 1 · The human, and the promise

Leave-behind already on the chairs. No welcome slide, no agenda, no icebreaker. He starts at zero.

[H]

We all think. We all feel. We all act. We all connect.

And we use those in every part of a life — not just at work. As a parent. As a friend. Playing sport, out for a walk. In a stressful moment, a hard moment, an easy moment, a good one. We depend on those four things constantly. Most of us, most days, without ever once thinking about it.

[D — the no-disclosure promise]

One thing before I go any further, so nobody's sitting there wondering about it for an hour. Nobody in this room is going to be asked to speak. Not to the person next to you, not to a group, not to me. Nothing gets collected. If you say nothing at all for the next hour, you've done this exactly right.

There's a folded sheet in front of you. Leave it for now — there's nothing on it to fill in. It's yours to take home.

⚑ Measured deliveries only: "There's an anonymous one on the way in and one on the way out. It isn't part of the session, it never has your name on it, and it's not the practice." Not said in an unmeasured delivery — it would be false.**

BEAT 2 · The silent poll, the gap, and the car that never learned to brake

[D — the silent poll. From the 25 May live version, hands removed on Hunter's ruling of 2026-09-08: "yes — but get them to answer to themselves." ⛔ NEVER take a show of hands here]

I'm going to ask you something, and I don't want an answer. Not out loud, not a hand up. Just answer it in your own head — you're the only person who's ever going to know what you said.

Most of us move our bodies. We walk, we train, we get outside, we play something. And not really because it prevents anything. We do it for what it gives us. We're better company after it. We sleep. We can keep up with our kids.

Is that true for you?

Three seconds. Nothing is taken. He does not scan the room and never says "hands up" or "who agrees." He answers it himself:

Yeah. Nearly everyone does.

Hold on to that yes, because I'm going to hold you to it for the next hour. Same question, about your mind. Where's the version of that? Where's the training you do for what it gives you?

Three seconds.

There isn't one. Nobody ever sold you the benefit. The mind gets sold to you as something to prevent — and that's where it stops. The upside was never on offer.

[H — the hook]

And here's the thing. We've never actually been taught these skills. Nor have we ever been given a system, or a process, to practise getting better at them in the actual moments of our lives.

[H* — the CPR comparison. Restored 2026-09-08 on Hunter's ruling. ⚑ First cut if the room runs long]

I've done more mental health first aid training than I've done CPR courses. Both are worth doing. Both of those train me to help somebody else. Neither one ever taught me how to run my own head at twenty to four on a Wednesday.

[H — the braking analogy]

Think about it like this. Nobody ever taught us to brake. And we go through life not thinking that we can't brake — ask anyone, yeah, of course I can brake. But we don't really know what braking is. We've heard of it. And honestly, when it comes to it, we struggle. We've never practised it.

[D — the added clause D-0130 requires]

And nobody ever corrected us on it. There was no red pen for this one.

[H]

And here's the thing — nobody walks around saying “I can't brake.” You don't know what you can't do. You just live your life on the skills you already have, and that becomes your norm.

So you take different roads. There are hills you don't go down and trips you don't make, and it isn't a decision — it's just how your life is shaped. And it never once occurs to you that a skill was missing.

Same with your own state, and your own thoughts, in a tricky moment. Nobody thinks I can't regulate. You just adapt around it, and that becomes normal.

So imagine if we could. And imagine if the environment around us actually supported it.

BEAT 3 · The door ⛔ NEVER CUT

[BRIDGE]

Before we go anywhere with that — one thing I'd rather say plainly.

[H — approved script, verbatim]

I'd rather say it plainly than pretend everyone in a room this size is having the same kind of week.

This isn't a clinical workshop. I'm not a psychologist and this isn't treatment. If something's going on for you that's bigger than a rough patch — if you're not okay — the thing that helps is your GP, not me. That's not me passing you off. It's just a different job.

In about a minute I'm going to ask you to do something quiet, on your own, and there'll be a few more of those later. If you don't want to do any of them today, don't. Turn that sheet over and look at the back panel. There's a GP line, there's Lifeline — thirteen eleven, fourteen — and there's triple zero. They're printed there so you don't have to remember them and so you don't have to ask anyone for them.

Straight on. No pause for effect, no lowered voice, no eye-contact sweep. The non-event is the point.**

BEAT 4 · The breath. Experience, with no name on it ⛔ NEVER CUT

[H]

I want you to do something and it takes about ninety seconds. Nobody is watching and nobody is going to ask you about it afterwards.

Close your eyes if you're comfortable doing that — and if you'd rather not, just look down at the table, that works the same. Bring your attention to your breath. Not changing it. Just noticing it going in, and going out.

And don't try to think of anything. Just keep bringing it back to the breath.

Ninety seconds of silence. He does it too — standing still, eyes down, run sheet in hand. He does not scan the room.**

[H*]

Okay. Eyes open.

I'm not going to ask anyone what happened. But I'd guess most of us had the same experience. Our mind wandered. A thought came in. And a lot of us got hooked on it — you were somewhere else for a bit, and then at some point you noticed, and you came back to the breath.

That last part. That coming back. That's the whole thing. You caught it. It was happening, and you noticed while it was still happening, and you came back.

That's what the rest of this hour is about. Not the breathing. The catching.

BEAT 5 · What that was, and what mental fitness actually is ⛔ NEVER CUT

[D — the bridge from beat 4]

So what was that? That was mental fitness, for about one second. Which is the first thing I want you to have: you already do this. Let me tell you what I mean by it, because in most rooms like this, nobody ever does.

(⚑ Online variant: "in most rooms like this" → "in most sessions like this.")

[H — P3a, unchanged]

We all have a body. Physical health is how it's doing. Physical fitness is what it can actually do. Nobody confuses those two.

Same split for the mind, and this is the whole thing.

We define it this way. Mental health is how you're doing. Mental fitness is what you can actually do — how well you think, how you work with what you feel, how you act on what matters, and how you connect, with yourself and with other people.

That's it. That's what the rest of this hour is about. Not how you're doing. What you can do.

[H — the boundary · C6 · ⚑ Spoken form of the is-not half of K-04's locked table — paraphrased for the room, not its verbatim wording. The is half is already carried by the definition above. This is what stops the room mishearing the next fifty minutes]

And let me be straight about what this isn't, because people hear "mental" and fill in the gap themselves.

This isn't therapy, counselling or treatment, and I'm not a clinician. If something in your life needs that, this doesn't replace it — and the two sit alongside each other perfectly well.

It isn't a promise you'll never struggle. Fit people still get sick. What this is for is strengthening what you can reach for when you do.

It isn't one tool that transforms a life. It's reps. That's the whole method and it's deliberately unglamorous.

And it is never a way of telling you that what's hard is your own fault. Some of what makes life hard is the situation, the people around you, what you've been through, or a system that isn't built for you. None of that is a skills problem, and none of it gets blamed on you here.

[H — the four positions]

And those two things are separate, which people find surprising. There are four real positions a person can be in.

You can be struggling, and have skills to draw on. You can be struggling, and have none. You can be doing perfectly well, and have skills. And you can be doing perfectly well, and have none — which is most of us, most of the time, and it's the one nobody talks about.

None of those four is a verdict on you. They're just where you are. And the second one — what you can actually do — is the one that can be practised.

[H — the capacity clause]

One more thing, because it's what people get wrong about themselves at two in the morning. It's a capacity, not perfection. You will miss moments. You'll miss chances to connect, you'll react and regret it. I still do. That isn't this failing — that's what a capacity is. Nobody says physical fitness failed because a fit person got tired.

BEAT 6 · The four, and the five skills named

[BRIDGE]

So if that's what it is — what's it actually made of?

[H — the basis]

In any moment — right now, sitting here — four things are going on at once.

You're thinking. There's something running, even if it's how long is this. You're feeling. Not necessarily dramatic. Bored is a feeling. Fine is a feeling. You're acting. Sitting still is an action. Checking your phone is an action. You're connecting — or not. There are people either side of you and you're doing something about that, including nothing.

That's the whole basis. Thinking, feeling, acting, connecting.

Why does it matter? Two reasons. First, when a moment goes badly it's usually because one of those four ran the show and the other three never got a say. Second — and this is the useful bit — four things means four ways in. When one is jammed, another one usually isn't. You can't always change what you're feeling. You can nearly always change what you're doing.

[H — the five skills. Fifteen seconds. ⛔ The second sentence NEVER CUT]

And underneath those four there are five things we're actually training. Notice. Shift. Choose. Focus. Connect.

And here's why those five. Every moment that goes badly, one of them was the part that failed. You didn't catch it — that's Notice. You caught it and couldn't shift out of it — that's Shift. You shifted and still did the thing you always do — that's Choose. You knew what mattered and couldn't stay on it — that's Focus. Or the whole thing was about somebody else and it went the way it always goes — that's Connect.

Five skills, because there are five ways a moment gets away from you. I'm not going to teach you all five in an hour — but that's what's under the bonnet.

⚑ Fixed 2026-09-10: "workable" was used here and not defined until beat 9. It is now defined where it is first used, at beat 9, and not used before it.

Then straight on. No slide, no definitions, no examples, no practice, and they never come back in the hour. If the fifteen seconds ever has to go, the names and that sentence go together, never the sentence alone.

BEAT 7 · Muscle memory. Skills get built · C5

[D — movement II, named]

So you already do it. Second thing: it can be trained.

[H]

Have you heard of things like muscle memory?

Our muscle doesn't actually have memory. It's our brain. It's our mind. And it works like any other skill — anything we practise, we can get better at.

Nobody thinks that's controversial about a golf swing, or parallel parking, or a language. You did it badly, you did it again, it got easier. Not because you wanted it more. Because you did it more.

[H — how you actually progress. ⚑ K-07's locked pathway, D-0082/D-0089. Named in all three products; worked properly in Essentials and Foundations]

And there are three stages to that, with any skill. We call them Learn It, Build It, Use It.

Learn It is what we're doing right now — you understand what it is and you've seen it once. That's real, and on its own it changes nothing under pressure.

Build It is where the work is. You pick your moments on purpose and you practise in them. Deliberate, a bit clunky, not automatic yet. Almost everything that matters happens in this stage, and it's the one most things skip.

Use It is when it turns up in a moment you didn't plan for, without you reaching for it — it starts showing up on its own. That's what we're aiming at. I'm not going to stand here and tell you an hour gets you there.

⚑ Say the stage names. Do not ask the room to place itself on the pathway — same ruling as the week-placement exercise. C7 compresses this to the three names and one line: "Learn it, build it, use it. The middle one is where the work is, and it's the one everything skips." Recovers 1 min.

[D — the planted question. ⚑ Timing corrected: beat 4 was ten minutes ago, not ninety seconds]

So — if catching a moment is a skill, and you did one about ten minutes ago — where would you practise it?

⚑ C5 cuts the muscle-memory half of this beat to two sentences: "Muscle memory isn't in the muscle, it's the mind. Like any skill — practise it, it gets easier." Recovers 1.5 min. Cut last: cheap in minutes, expensive in logic. ⛔ C5 does not touch Learn It / Build It / Use It — the pathway is in all three products and has its own code, C7.

BEAT 8 · The practice site is the life you're already living · C4

[H]

Here's where I think most of this stuff loses people. You don't need to dedicate fifteen, twenty, thirty minutes a day to this. Most of us don't have it — and the ones who do have it on the good weeks and not the bad ones, and the bad weeks are the ones that matter.

Life is lived in moments. And moments are the practice site. They're already happening. There are dozens of them today and there'll be dozens tomorrow.

What the practice buys you is living those moments with a bit more intention. Catch the moment. Shift. And make the choice that takes you toward what actually matters to you. Not toward what matters to me, or to your manager. Toward yours.

[H — the four places]

And the moments aren't hidden. Yours are already signposted, and there are four places the signpost hides.

People. Who's there when it happens. Who makes it easier, who makes it harder — and honestly, sometimes the same person does both depending on the day. Places. The doorway. The car. The desk. The ward. Times and transitions. The handover. The end of the shift. The twelve steps from the car to the front door. A lot of people find their hardest moments sit at a transition rather than in the middle of something. Objects and screens. The phone. The badge. The keys in your hand.

[D — the Radar, named where it is already being described]

Your cue is already there. There are four places it hides. You've always had them. Nobody ever asked you to look.

[H]

And here's why that beats deciding to try harder. Nobody checks their mirrors because they're disciplined. You check because the mirror is right there, in your eyeline.

It's not you trying harder. It's what's around you.

[D — the planted question. ⛔ Nobody answers, no hands, and he does not come back to it]

So, without telling me: which of those four is yours?

Three seconds. He looks at his run sheet, not the room, and moves straight on.

This is a change of state, not an activity — nothing is performed, so ruling 6 is untouched, and it is recognition rather than disclosure, so ruling 17 is untouched.
