⛔ THE ENVIRONMENT BOUNDARY AND THE MANAGER HANDOFF — said once, here, in this wording. NEVER CUT. NEVER SOFTENED.

[H — DURABLE]

And one thing I'd rather say straight, because it's true and you'd work it out anyway. A skill doesn't replace a bad environment. If you're not sleeping, if there's no support around you, if the conditions are genuinely against you — this is not the answer to that, and I'm not going to pretend it is.

That's exactly why we don't only do this hour. There's a separate session for the people who set how a team actually works — how it's scheduled, what gets noticed, what happens next. That's the other half of it, and it isn't yours to carry from where you're sitting.

BEAT 9 · Stop, Shift, Do. And the unit ⛔ NEVER CUT

[BRIDGE]

So that's where. Third thing — here's how you actually train it. Three steps, and you've already done the first one.

[H* — approved script]

Stop. Stop is not calming down. Stop is noticing that a moment is happening while it's still happening. That's all. You did one at minute seven. It's hard because by the time most of us notice, we've already sent the reply.

Shift. Shift is changing one thing so the moment becomes workable. Not nice. Not calm. Workable — and sometimes calm is the wrong thing to want anyway.

And let me be blunt about calm, because this is where a lot of this stuff loses people. Nobody has ever calmed down just because someone told them to. If your fix needs a quiet room and ten minutes, it will never once happen at twenty to four on a Wednesday. It isn't available. Pretending it is, is why this stuff gets binned.

So what's available? Two doors, both small. Shift your state, or shift your thinking.

A state you're stuck in — tense, flooded, checked out, foggy — isn't a fixed fact about the moment. It's a pattern you fell into, and patterns can be interrupted. And you can interrupt one four ways. I'm going to show you all four, and I'm not going to make you do any of them.

Through your body. The state usually shows up there first — tight shoulders, jaw, shallow breathing. Feet on the floor. One slower breath. Stand up and stretch. Step outside for a minute. Changing something physical can move it, sometimes faster than trying to think your way out.

Through your attention. Your attention can really only hold one thing properly at a time. Name three things you can see. Find the furthest sound you can hear, then the closest. That can make space between you and whatever had hold of you, without you having to solve anything first.

Through your thinking. Sometimes it isn't in your body, it's in how big the problem feels. Zoom out — will this matter in a week. Zoom in — what's the one next thing, not the whole list. Or ask what you'd tell a friend in this spot. A different question doesn't answer itself. It can give your thinking somewhere else to go for a second.

With other people. Text one person. Ask for two minutes. Sit near someone without even talking. Some states are hard to shift alone — not because you're doing it wrong, but because they were never meant to be handled alone.

And every one of them is answering the same question: too much, too little, or workable? Too much, shift down. Too little, shift up. Already workable, there may be nothing here you need.

The point isn't which one. It's that you have one at all — because whichever one you can actually reach in the moment is the right one.

The test is one question: can I do the next thing from here? That's the bar. Not calm. Workable.

And there's a version of that you can ask before you pick a door. We call it the State Check. Is there too much in me right now, too little, or is this workable? That's it. Not what am I feeling — how much. You're not scoring it and I'm never going to ask you for your answer.

Do. The next move, however small. Send it in an hour. Walk over instead of typing. Send the boring version — got it, will look at this after three. Or send exactly what you were going to send anyway, having actually decided to. That last one counts. This isn't about being nicer. It's about the moment having more than one option in it.

Not just decided. Decided toward what actually matters to you in that bit of your life.

⚑ Fixed 2026-09-10: two outcome statements in the four doors above were present indicative ("that makes space", "it gives your thinking somewhere else to go"). Both now read can, matching "can move it" twelve lines up. Ruling 34, K-08, AG-001.

[D — Q1 ruling, Hunter, 2026-09-08. The honest statement. ⛔ NEVER replaced with a staged exercise]

And I'll be straight with you about something most sessions like this fudge. You can't do a Do in this room. You're in a chair. The moment isn't here. Anything I got you to perform right now would be a performance, and you'd know it.

But you've already done thousands of them. Your phone. You've felt the pull to check it, noticed it, and put it down anyway. That's the whole loop — and nobody ever taught it to you. Probably a few times already today.

That's not me catching you out — I'm not watching, and I told you I wouldn't. That's the equipment already being installed. The Do happens out there. That's what it's for — it isn't a gap in the hour.

[H — the unit. The most important sentence in the hour]

And here's the unit. We call it a mental rep. And a rep counts when you attempt it.

Not when it works. When you attempt it. You Stop, you Shift, you Do — the other person still reacts badly, the day is still bad, it changes nothing. That's a completed rep. You did the thing that's trainable.

Same as a learner who stalls at the lights. That lesson still counted. It probably counted more.

BEAT 10 · Specificity of practice, and the knowing–doing gap · the centre of the talk · C3

[BRIDGE]

Now — why practise it there? Why not just go and learn it somewhere quieter and bring it back?

[H — the argument that does the work]

A calf raise builds your calves. A bench press builds your chest. That doesn't mean either one translates into the moment you actually need it.

An athlete doesn't just get strong. They practise the specific skill for match day. Over and over. In something that looks like the real thing.

So — as good as meditation is, as an isolated method — it doesn't mean that tonight, in this moment, you'll catch, shift and do. It might help you catch. It might not help you shift.

What if we practised catching, shifting and doing in the life we're already living?

[H — the knowing–doing gap. ⚑ C3 cuts from here to the end of this block]

Let me put it another way. How many of us have heard of breath work? Nearly everyone. We just did ninety seconds of it.

But doing breath work last week with a practitioner doesn't mean that in this moment, things are going to change. We conceptually understand what we could do. The question is: can we apply it in the moment?

Watching one more episode late at night. The scroll. The food before bed. The conversation that went on past when we should've stopped. And we wake up and think — I shouldn't have done that. Even though I knew better.

That isn't a missing skill. That's the gap between having a skill and applying it in a specific moment.

[H — be kind, be calm]

And here's what we do really well in society. We tell people what we want them to do. Be kind. Be nice. Be calm. Be this, be that.

29 Delivery Script Essentials 90

Essentials, as it is said

Same fourteen beats. Same order. Same words in his mouth. A participant who sat through the Hour in March and Essentials in September recognises every beat and finds it deeper, never different. That is ruling 4 and ruling 5, and it is the only reason this product is affordable to build at all.

What Essentials actually buys, and it is four things.

  1. Time to practise. The Hour shows the shift menu and says plainly that nobody will be made to perform one. Essentials shows it and then has each person use one, silently, on a moment they already lived.
  2. The five skills worked, one example each, and then used as the instrument a participant picks their moment with. In the Hour they are named in fifteen seconds and never return.
  3. The return session, 60 minutes remote, inside the price (D-0113, ruling 69).
  4. Depth in three places the Hour compresses to a sentence: the wider Human Operating System, the four places a cue hides, and low friction against high friction.

Everything else is the Hour.

Marking

[H] Hunter's own words, carried unchanged from 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-INTRODUCTION-60.md. Do not rewrite. [H*] his words, grammar tidied for speech. [D] drafted in the Hour's script and carried. [E] drafted new for Essentials, for Hunter to make his own. [v3] carried across from 39-ESSENTIALS-FINAL-SERVICE-PACK-v3.md, with its line noted. [BRIDGE] connective tissue. ⛔ never cut. E1–E5 the cut order, marked where the cut lands.

Where a beat says CARRIED, the Hour's words for that beat run exactly as written in 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-INTRODUCTION-60.md. They are not reprinted. Reprinting them would create a second copy of Hunter's words that drifts from the first, which is the failure this whole project keeps repeating.

The four rules that govern every line, unchanged from the Hour

Nothing is asked out loud about a person's own state. Nothing is collected. Every question about the participant themselves is asked, held, and answered by him, and no answers are taken. ⛔ Nobody writes anything. Nobody speaks unless they want to. Cap 20 solo, 30 only with a co-facilitator.

Ruling 7 and 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-INTRODUCTION-60.md's own fourth rule bar it, and neither was named. The elicitation below is now held in the head, with nothing written anywhere by anyone.

Hands up is allowed and wanted for recognition — have you heard of this, have you been in a situation like this. Never for disclosure. Ruling 17.

And it isn't just you. Look at what we actually do about this as a society. We wait.

Before that, two questions, and they are for you. Nothing gets written down and nothing gets said. Just hold them in your head.

MOVEMENT II — naming, the category, the skills, muscle memory

BEAT 5 · What that was, and what mental fitness actually is ⛔ NEVER CUT

CARRIED in full — the definition, the is-not boundary, the capacity clause.

[E — the four positions worked, replacing the Hour's single paragraph. Card 9 d2, card 9b d2.]

And those two things are separate, which people find surprising, so let me actually walk it.

You can be struggling, and have skills to draw on. That is the person having a genuinely awful month who still catches themselves before the sentence comes out. Nothing about their month is better. They just have somewhere to stand in it.

You can be struggling, and have none. That is the hardest place to be, and it is the one everything in the mental health world is pointed at, correctly.

You can be doing perfectly well, and have skills. That is a person building while it is calm, which is the only time anybody ever gets to build anything.

And you can be doing perfectly well, and have none. Which is most of us, most of the time. Nothing is wrong. You have simply never been asked to do this under load, and one day you will be.

You can be doing completely fine and still find some of these hard. That is not a contradiction and it is not a warning about you. It is the whole reason a category called fitness exists separately from a category called health.

Let me show you the four ways in on one moment, because I would rather show you than tell you.

An email lands at ten to five and it has a tone in it.

Through feeling, the way in is not to argue with it. Something turned up in your chest. You are not talking it out of the room. But you can notice it arrived, and noticing can change what it does next.

Through acting, the way in is your hands. Stand up. Do not reply yet. Reply at nine tomorrow. This is nearly always the open door, which is why I keep coming back to it.

Through connecting, the way in is somebody else. Walk to a desk. Say the one sentence. Some states are hard to shift alone.

Four doors, one moment. When one is jammed, another one usually is not.

[E — the naming is carried from the Hour verbatim. Then one worked example each. Ruling 30, and the narrowing ruling in 00-THE-RULINGS.md §recoveries Ruling 1.]

Notice. Shift. Choose. Focus. Connect. Five, because there are five ways a moment gets away from you. One of each, so they are not just words. One of these five is more yours than the other four, and you will know which one before I finish the list.

Notice. You get in the car after work and you arrive home with no memory of the drive. Nothing went wrong. You just were not there for any of it. Notice is being there while it is happening.

Shift. You have finished a hard call and the next one starts in ninety seconds. You are going to take the first call into the second one unless you do something with those ninety seconds. Shift is what you do with them.

Choose. You know exactly what you should say. You say the other thing. You knew the whole time. Choose is the gap between knowing and doing, and it is its own skill, not a character flaw.

Focus. You sit down to do the thing that actually matters this week and you are in your inbox within a minute. Focus is not concentration. It is coming back, again, and again, without making a thing of it.

Connect. Someone tells you something and you are already assembling your answer. They can tell. Connect is being on the other side of it for a second longer.

⛔ D-0132 and ruling 70: a report is issued at every cohort size. What scales is what it may contain, never whether it exists. ⚠ A buyer can pay full price and receive a report with very few numbers in it. 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md records that this is stated in 2026-09-04-MEASUREMENT-v5.md and not in the buyer pack. That is a commercial disclosure gap, not a delivery one, and it is not mine to close.

⛔ Essentials has no fieldable measurement instrument. Its return is online and the completion engine is physical. 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md names this the highest-priority build item and it is unresolved here.

The moment gallery — the honest answer

Hunter, 2026-09-09: "if we want to, we'll make time for it in the essentials, but it has to be in the foundations."

My answer: not the full gallery, and here is exactly what it would displace.

The gallery is thirteen minutes in the Foundations budget. Essentials has twenty-three minutes more than the Hour in total. Beat 10 and beat 11 grow by four minutes each; the five skills at beat 6 by two; nothing else grows by more than two.

So thirteen minutes cannot be found in one place. It has to be taken from several, and here is the honest list of what it would actually cost. The proposed cut order recovers about nine minutes without touching beat 11 at all: beat 10's methods passage and the wider operating system, beat 13's worked ripple, beat 8's four places, beat 2's society picture, beat 7's private stage placement. Spend all five and you are still four minutes short, and you have spent the entire compression margin, which means the first time a room runs long there is nothing left to cut and the practice goes by default.

That is the real trade, and it is worse than a single displacement. It is not gallery against one block. It is gallery against every piece of depth Essentials adds outside beat 11, plus the buffer that protects the practice. I would not make that trade. The gallery is thirteen minutes of finding a moment; beat 11 is four minutes of using one. Essentials is the product where they use one.

There is a second reason, and it is a build dependency rather than a judgement. The gallery needs a wall of curated ordinary moments. The moment bank holds 16 verified entries and none is a workplace-manager moment, and the no-invention rule is standing: no facilitator, session or prep step may write a new moment for the wall. The corpus for an Essentials wall does not exist, so even if the time were found the object is not there.

⚑ 16, not 18. 26-RECOVERED-FOUNDATIONS-DEVICES.md says 18, and 90-meta/agent-context-v1/14-moment-examples-bank.md holds M-01 to M-05, M-08 and M-09 to M-18, which is sixteen. M-06 and M-07 are listed as referenced but not captured, under a standing instruction not to reconstruct them and to ask Hunter. The error is inherited from 26 and is corrected here rather than repeated. It makes the gallery's corpus problem worse, not better.

What Essentials runs instead, and it does the gallery's actual job. The gallery exists because asked cold to think of a moment, most people produce either something enormous or nothing at all. The leave-behind already carries printed moments, and beat 11 already points at them: "there are moments printed on the sheet if you'd rather take one than find one, and that's not a lesser version of this." That is the gallery's function, seated, silent, at a cost of zero minutes.

If Hunter wants more than that, the cheapest real version is about two minutes and does not touch beat 11:

[E — the seated gallery, only if he wants it. Goes at the top of beat 11.]

Before we run it. Turn the sheet over and read the moments on the middle panel. Do not pick one yet. Just read them.

Some of them will be nothing like your life. One or two might be irritatingly close.

(Forty seconds of quiet.)

Read them for two different reasons. Find one where the hard part is noticing it is even happening. And find one where the hard part is choosing, where you notice fine and do the other thing anyway. Two moments, two different hard parts.

This is the skill-referenced selection instruction from 26-RECOVERED-FOUNDATIONS-DEVICES.md, verbatim in its logic, made seated and silent. It is the accessibility equivalent that file requires, run as the default rather than as an offer, which also closes the Gate 0.1 failure the original pack carried. It costs about two minutes, taken from beat 13's E2 depth. Foundations still runs the full walk-the-wall version with three moments and three hard parts. Essentials runs two, on the sheet.**

The cut order · and I am proposing a change to it

22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md currently sets E1 to E5 as: E1 beat 10, E2 beat 11, E3 beat 13, E4 beat 8, E5 beat 6, each reverting to its 58-minute length. Recoverable 14 minutes.

⚠ E2 and E5 as written cut the product. Reverting beat 11 to the Hour's version removes the silent shift practice, which is the whole difference between Essentials and the Hour. Reverting beat 6 removes the five worked skills, which is the second one. A cut order whose second and fifth moves delete what the buyer paid for is a defect in the order, not a hard choice. [v3 §10] had already reached the same conclusion in its own terms: moment selection is the only step in the product that carries the stated primary outcome, and a session that never asks where the next rep goes is unlikely to produce one.

Proposed order, marked as a proposal, not silently applied:

Cut What goes Recovers
E1 Beat 10, methods correctly placed and the counter-detail in the wider operating system The four extra components go to one sentence each. Passenger, Engine, Driver stay in full ~3 min
E2 Beat 13, the ripple worked Back to the Hour's version. The turn, the mission and this is how you can help us are untouched ~2 min
E3 Beat 8, the four places worked Back to labels and one example each. ⛔ High friction and low friction stays. ⛔ The environment boundary stays ~2 min
E4 Beat 2, the picture in society and the watching passage Back to the Hour's beat 2 exactly 1 min
E5 Beat 7, the private Learn It, Build It, Use It placement Back to naming the three stages 1 min
Total ~9 min

⚑ Two things about this table that 22's order does better, and I am not hiding them. E4 and E5 are full reversions to the Hour and recover exactly the settings table's delta, one minute each. E1 and E3 are partial — the four extra operating-system components to a sentence each, the four places back to labels — and a partial reversion is the shape that lets the same minute get counted twice, which is precisely the hazard 22's all-or-nothing rule was built to make structurally impossible. The honest reading: E1 and E3 recover approximately three and two minutes, and approximately is doing work in that sentence. If Hunter wants the double-count impossibility back, E1 and E3 become full reversions of beats 10 and 8 and the order recovers about twelve minutes at a higher cost per cut.

⛔ Never cut, at 90: beat 3 the door, beat 4 the breath and the elicitation payoff, beat 5 the definition and the boundary, beat 6's I'm not going to teach you all five in an hour, beat 8's environment boundary and manager handoff, beat 9 in full, beat 10's honest limit, beat 11's practice and the two-moment selection, beat 12's one in three, beat 14's QR and the sixty-second swap.

Do not improvise a cut with the clock running. Recovery row 14.

Facilitator recovery

27-FACILITATOR-RECOVERY.md governs, and every row tagged E applies to this product. Not duplicated here. The rows that matter most in a workplace room, by beat:

Beat 3 onward, row 1, a disclosure of distress. ⛔ Its closing clause is ruled not-a-route and the real escalation procedure is an uncleared draft requiring a qualified clinical reviewer. Beat 4, rows 3 and 4, the silence and "my mind wandered the whole time." Beat 8, rows 8, 9 and 10, the systemic-problem challenge, which is the session's own position and not a concession. Row 18 covers pair or small-group work going wrong, and its remedy is switch to the solo fallback, the facilitator speaks it through, everyone runs it alone — which is already what beat 11 is. There is no row for a room that visibly will not do the silent practice, or for one person who stops halfway and looks around. Row 21, the gallery running long, is Foundations-only in effect, because it funds the overrun from application studios that Essentials does not run. Writing those rows is 27's job and Hunter's ruling, not this file's. Recorded as Open item 13.

If asked whether this has been shown to work, 28-HAS-THIS-BEEN-SHOWN-TO-WORK.md §1a is the ten-second answer and §1b the forty-second one. Not yet. We have not measured a group through this. What is underneath it is well tested, the session on top of it is not, and we will publish when we know. Flat and fast. It is not an apology.

What I took from the orphaned v3 pack, and what I deliberately left

39-ESSENTIALS-FINAL-SERVICE-PACK-v3.md is the only prior beat-by-beat Essentials design that has ever existed. Its numbering is superseded. Its content was never replaced.

Carried across, because it was better than anything written since:

  • The workplace permission and the consequence, not embarrassment distinction (beat 1).
  • The manager-in-the-room instruction: name it, do not pretend the room is flat.
  • The two-moment, skill-referenced selection at beat 11, close to whole, including two moments, two different hard parts, both easy ones and the reasoning that without it the five skills have no downstream consumer.
  • The if-then phone cue as the sanctioned writing surface and all of its boundaries, reused at beat 4's elicitation.
  • The Passenger correction — the Passenger is not the villain — and the ban on the Driver takes back the wheel (beat 10).
  • The State Check boundaries in a workplace: never mandatory, scored, public or performance-based, never a poll, never in the chat.
  • The environment content including the resistant colleague and never convert a contextual problem into mindset (beat 8).
  • The close that refuses "now it's up to you", on v3's reasoning that in a workplace that sentence lets an organisation treat ninety minutes as having discharged an obligation. Beat 14's flat finish already carries this; v3's argument for why is the better argument.
  • The entire online-versus-in-person table ([v3 §7]). It is the only such table MFC has and it is unreplaced. Read it before delivering this online. Cameras off is fine and must be said in the first minute. No chat, no reactions, no polls, no breakouts, no recording.
  • The language corrections table ([v3 §9]), which binds improvised facilitator speech as hard as it binds these scripts.

Deliberately left, and why:

  • The entire R1 to R8 facilitator-cued rep architecture. v3 runs seven reps with required Dos in the room: decide, on purpose, what you are doing next. Ruling 6 bars a staged Do at any depth, ever, and AG-010 bars working a real situation someone offers. The Hour's own beat 9 now says it plainly to the room: you can't do a Do in this room, and anything I got you to perform right now would be a performance, and you'd know it. The rep architecture predates that ruling and does not survive it. What survives is the class of device that is a Stop or a Shift with nothing performed, which is why beat 4's breath and beat 11's silent practice are in and R1 through R8 are out.
  • The seven-beat structure and every minute band inside it. Superseded by D-0131.
  • The claim that the return session and the report are separately purchased. Superseded by D-0113 and ruling 69: everything is inside the price.
  • The Human Operating System at a five-minute hard cap as its own block. It is at beat 10 now, serving the knowing-doing argument, which is where ruling 31 puts it and where card 6's d3 field says explicitly it does not belong at beat 2.
  • The v2 discrimination case that v3 §5 judgement 10a calls its most serious undisclosed subtraction. It is still not restored and I am not restoring it here. It is a ten-minute block that teaches Do separated from outcome and from condition, and v2 called it the thing that stops the personal work becoming self-blame. Ninety minutes cannot carry it without deleting the practice. It belongs in Foundations. Flagging it rather than quietly losing it a second time.
  • The paired listening catch, v3's judgement 5, excluded on the rep criteria and on the no-pair-work rule. Row 18 of the recovery table exists precisely for the case where pair work has started, and this product never starts any.
  • The seven deep skills. Never in any session.

31 Foundations 240 Structure

Foundations, as it goes

⚑ The one sentence this day argues — ADDED 2026-09-10

You leave with one ordinary moment out of your own life, and you spend the afternoon making it survive the version of itself that actually goes wrong.

Why this sentence, and what it settles. The flow check could not write one, because the file was carrying two arguments and subordinating neither: you will learn what to do when this fails, and you will leave with a moment. Both are good. The moment is the object; the failure work is what makes the object worth having. That is the subordination, and it is the only one that makes the back half of the day one thing instead of two. A moment nobody has run against a bad day is a moment that gets abandoned in week one, and a breakpoint map with no moment attached to it is a lecture.

⚑ The alternative was live and is named rather than hidden. The other defensible reading — Foundations is the product where you learn what to do when it fails, and the moment is the worked example — closes with the breakpoint map instead. It was not chosen because ruling 29c makes the moment gallery mandatory here and [v3 §7 guardrail 5] says moment selection carries the stated primary outcome. If Hunter prefers the other reading, the change is one of order, not of content: beat 12 becomes the close and beat 11 becomes the setup.

What each movement does for that sentence

Movement What it does for the sentence Honest reading
I — arrival, the door, the gap, the breath Establishes there is a moment at all, and that catching one is a thing a person can do rather than a thing they know about. Activity 1 makes the room supply the evidence, the breath gives them one catch Serves it.
II — naming, the category, the skills, muscle memory Gives the catch a name and gives the room the three words it will use on its own moment for the next three hours. Notice, Choose and Shift are the filter the gallery runs on Serves it, with one exception. Focus and Connect are taught at beat 6 and never used again in 240 minutes. That is two of five skills that do not serve the sentence, and the honest reading is three working skills and two decorative ones. Recorded, not fixed here.
III — the practice site, the method, the specificity argument Establishes why it has to be a moment of yours and not a technique in general, which is the sentence's whole load-bearing half Serves it. Beat 10 is the centre for exactly this reason.
IV — running it, grace, the ripple, the Radar Selects the moment (gallery), works it (studios, silent shift), then runs it against failure (breakpoint map, rehearsal with options removed) and hands over the thing that survives Thursday Serves it, and this is where the sentence is actually delivered.

What does not serve it, said plainly rather than justified backwards.

  • Activity 4, fold your arms (beat 7). It demonstrates that a less-practised motor pattern feels wrong. It says nothing about anyone's moment, and beat 7 already says the same thing in words. It is left in because cutting it is a design decision beyond this pass, and it is the first thing that should go if the day needs a minute. The assessment's own verdict is that it fails A5 and should be cut. Open item 15.
  • The kids passage and the norms question at beat 13. They serve the ripple, which is the peak, not the sentence. That is legitimate: beat 13 is deliberately the one beat that widens outward. Named so nobody later reverse-engineers a moment-related justification for them.

Same four movements. Same fourteen beats. Same order. Same words in his mouth.

A participant who sat through the Hour in March, Essentials in June and Foundations in September recognises every beat and finds it deeper each time. Never different. That is ruling 4 and ruling 5.

Rule 3 of 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md, as amended 2026-09-09: nothing is argued at 90 or 240 that is not argued at 58. Depth and practice are what widen. That amendment is the entire licence for this file. Everything below either works an argument the Hour already makes, or has the room practise something the Hour has no time for.

What Foundations actually buys, and it is five things

  1. The moment gallery. Mandatory here, and nowhere else in full. Ruling 29c.
  2. Application studios. Foundations only. Ruling 29d. The only small-group device MFC has ever designed that satisfies AG-134 without exposing anyone.
  3. Four separate pieces of practice, against Essentials' one and the Hour's none.
  4. Three spaced unaided retrievals, recovered from the v3 pack, which is the strongest single learning-design feature MFC has ever built and had no successor.
  5. The two arguments only a half day can carry: the breakpoint map, and the case that separates a Do from its outcome so that private work does not turn into self-blame.

Everything else is Essentials, and Essentials is the Hour.

Marking, unchanged from 29-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-ESSENTIALS-90.md

CARRIED the Hour's or Essentials' words for that beat run exactly as written in 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-INTRODUCTION-60.md and 29-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-ESSENTIALS-90.md. They are not reprinted here. Reprinting them makes a second copy of Hunter's words that drifts from the first, which is the failure this project keeps repeating.

[H] Hunter's own words. [E] drafted for Essentials and carried up. [v3] recovered from 40-FOUNDATIONS-FINAL-SERVICE-PACK-v3.md with its section noted. [F] drafted new for Foundations, for Hunter to make his own. ⛔ never cut. ⚡ an activity.

The four rules that govern every beat, unchanged at 240

Nothing is asked out loud about a person's own state. Nothing is collected. Nobody writes anything. Nobody speaks unless they want to. Cap 20 with one facilitator, 30 only with a co-facilitator (AG-131, AG-160, ruling 8).

⛔ The room cannot perform a Do, at any depth, ever (ruling 6, AG-010 HARD). Everything called practice below works a moment the participant already lived, or is a Stop or a Shift with nothing staged and nothing offered by anyone in the room. That rule binds the 240 exactly as hard as it binds the 58, and it is the reason v3's ten-rep architecture is not carried whole.

Hands up is allowed and wanted for recognition (ruling 17): have you heard of this, have you been in a situation like this. Never for a person's own state.

The four routes are offered aloud, not merely permitted, at every block that asks for anything ([v3 §6]): join in, think privately, use an invented example, observe, or say nothing at all. In a half day this has to be said in the first two minutes and then honoured every single time.

MOVEMENT I — arrival, the door, the gap, the breath

BEAT 1 · The human, and the promise

What changes in the room. People stop calculating whether they will be made to speak, and start listening. In a half day this has to happen faster and harder than anywhere else, because four hours of unrelieved exposure anxiety is a different animal from sixty minutes of it.

CARRIED in full from the Hour, plus Essentials' workplace clause and its manager sentence.

What must be said.

[E] The exposure answer, unchanged:

Nothing you think about in here is going to be said out loud, to me or to anyone in this room. There is no going round the table. There is no pairing up. Nobody is reporting back on anything.

[v3 §2, permission block] The half-day addition, and it is the one thing beat 1 gains:

You can join in, think privately, use an invented example, observe, or say nothing at all. Nothing is collected. Nobody is asked to share anything personal, at any point today.

[v3 §2, shape of the day] And the shape, which only exists because the day is long enough to have one:

You'll do things today before I explain them. That's deliberate. And the parts that touch your own life come late, and stay private.

⛔ No personal check-in round, ever. [v3 §2]: a half day creates an expectation of disclosure that must be defeated in the first two minutes, not managed later.

Foundations adds over Essentials: the four routes and the shape of the day, said once, at the front, because a long room needs to know when its own life gets involved and that it is late.

BEAT 3 · The door ⛔ NEVER CUT, AND NEVER LENGTHENED · ⚑ DELIVERED HERE IN FOUNDATIONS, BEFORE BEAT 2

⚑ FIX 2026-09-10 — the door now precedes the day's first experience. In the Hour and Essentials the first thing anyone does is the breath at beat 4, so the door sits at beat 3 and clears it. Foundations is the only product with an activity earlier than that: Activity 1, a private recall of something that was supposed to help you and didn't, inside beat 2. The door was running after it. 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md movement 3 is explicit that the door "must precede the first experience, not follow it," and names what breaks without it: a safeguarding floor missed at the exact moment it becomes needed. The beat keeps its number, because the number is what carries across the three products; only its delivery position in this product moves. Nothing in it is lengthened, added to or reworded — RULE 4 still holds.

What changes in the room. Everyone now knows what to do if this gets heavy, before the first thing anyone does.

CARRIED verbatim. Identical length in all three products, deliberately. RULE 4 of 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md: making the door longer turns a reassurance into a warning. This is the one beat that does not widen at 240. If it takes longer here than it does in the Hour, it has gone wrong.

What must be said, and it is AG-004 (Eimear, HARD) in Hunter's wording:

This isn't therapy and it isn't diagnosis. It's also not a claim that every situation can be solved by an individual responding better. Sometimes what a situation needs is support, safety, time, or something around you to change, and that's real, and it isn't yours alone to carry.

⛔ D-0118 closed D-0016 as a delivery gate. Do not add clinical apparatus to this beat. AG-003 is explicit that inventing clinical issues into a non-clinical educational workshop is the error, not the caution.

Foundations adds over Essentials: nothing. That is the point.

BEAT 2 · The silent poll, the gap, and the car that never learned to brake

What changes in the room. "I already know this" becomes "I have never once practised this," and then becomes "and that is not my fault."

CARRIED in full from the Hour: the poll, the hook, the CPR comparison, the braking analogy, the red pen, the roads you stop taking. Plus Essentials' two additions carried whole: the picture in society, and the watching passage.

What must be said.

[E] The structural version of the gap, which is what stops the room hearing all this as a personal failing:

Nobody would run physical health that way. We do not tell people to wait until their back goes and then hand them a leaflet. We have gyms, and teams, and a park with people running in it on a Tuesday night, and none of that is treatment.

[H] And ruling 52, which is the register of the whole beat:

It's not on you. It has always happened. You have not learned these things, and that's a problem, not a fault.

Foundations widens two things and adds one.

[F card 13 d3] The reactive-only pattern, named. Mental health days, EAPs, a number to call, a poster: things brought in to manage a problem after it exists. Essentials says we wait. Foundations says what we do instead of building, and names it.

[F card 8b d3] The watching passage gets its second half: what a person can choose to pass on differently. Essentials stops at "nobody asked you which was which." Foundations goes one step further, and it is the step that connects beat 2 to beat 13's ripple.

[v3 beat 1] Why the gap stayed open. No school subject, no recognisable venue, no shared vocabulary, no visible unit of practice. ⛔ That is a description of a gap, not a claim that other approaches failed and not a claim that MFC has solved it. Do not disparage any other practice or profession (ruling 38, ruling 39, K-08).

⚡ ACTIVITY 1 · The technique that did not work

[v3 beat 1, carried whole] Foundations only. The first thing anyone in the room does, and it happens before any content, which is AG-144 answered directly. ⚑ The door has already been said (beat 3, delivered above): this activity is the reason it moved, because it asks a person to bring back something that failed them, and that is an experience, not a preamble.

What happens. He asks the room to bring to mind one thing they were once given that was supposed to help and did not.

What participants physically do. Nothing visible. They sit and think for about twenty seconds. Nothing is said, nothing is written, no hands.

What the facilitator does. Says the prompt, says the boundary in the same breath, waits, does not scan the room, and closes it himself:

Think of something you were once given that was supposed to help and didn't. Don't tell me what it was.

then, after the silence:

For a lot of people the technique wasn't the problem. Nobody gave them the process it was supposed to sit inside.

Accessibility equivalent. None needed beyond the standing routes: nothing is written, nothing is said, nobody moves. If nothing comes to mind, that is a complete answer and he says so before the silence starts, not after.

Foundations adds over Essentials: the room supplies its own evidence for the gap before he argues it, instead of being told about it.

BEAT 4 · The breath. Experience, with no name on it ⛔ NEVER CUT

What changes in the room. The room does a Stop before the word Stop exists. Experience first, name second (ruling 9).

CARRIED in full from the Hour, plus Essentials' elicit-before-explain in front of it and its payoff after it.

What must be said. [E] The elicitation, held in the head, nothing written:

Nothing gets written down and nothing gets said. Just hold them in your head.

[H] And the debrief line, which is the single most important sentence in the beat and is spoken exactly, every time:

The rep was not maintaining perfect attention. The rep happened when you caught the drift and came back.

⚡ ACTIVITY 2 · The breath, ninety seconds

[v3 R1, and Hunter's own worked example] Present in all three products. Foundations runs it at ninety seconds, as v3 did, not sixty.

What happens. Ninety seconds of silence, with no name on it. The facilitator says nothing.

What participants physically do. Sit. Bring attention to the breath. When they notice attention has wandered, bring it back. Nothing written, nothing said.

What the facilitator does. Sets it up, does it himself, and ⛔ lets the silence run. Recovery row 3: do not narrate it, do not shorten it, do not fill it. If someone laughs or speaks, continue without comment. Then the debrief line above, unchanged.

Accessibility equivalent. Eyes open or closed, both said aloud. Breath is one option, not a requirement (K-08 rule 6: do not force calming, breathwork, eye closure, disclosure, touch, partner work or public sharing). A participant who prefers to rest attention on a sound in the room instead is doing the same rep and is told so before it starts.

Foundations adds over Essentials: thirty more seconds, which is not a detail. The catch only happens after attention has actually left, and at sixty seconds a portion of the room never gets there.

MOVEMENT II — naming, the category, the skills, muscle memory

⚡ ACTIVITY 3 · The body catch

[v3 R2, carried with its Do removed] Foundations and Essentials.

What happens. A Stop performed on the body, before Shift has ever been defined, followed by an optional Shift with an explicit permission not to.

What participants physically do. Notice where their shoulders are, their jaw, whether they are leaning forward or back. Ten seconds. Then, if they want to, change one thing. Or not.

What the facilitator does. Says it, waits, and says the "or don't" without irony:

Without moving yet, notice where your shoulders are. Your jaw. Whether you're leaning forward or back. Don't fix anything. Just find it. ... Now, if you want to, change one thing. Or don't, that's a real option.

⛔ v3 added a required Do here on 2026-08-31 ("decide, on purpose, what you're doing next"). It is not carried. Ruling 6 bars a staged Do at any depth, and v3's own note concedes that the Do was facilitator-directed and that R2's "occurs without manufacture" rating was already marginal. The "or don't" is what survives, and it is the load-bearing half: it stops Shift being heard as an instruction to calm down, delivered physically before Shift is ever defined.

Accessibility equivalent. A participant who does not want to attend to their body attends to the sound in the room instead, and is told that before it starts. Nobody is watched, nothing is checked.

Foundations adds over Essentials: nothing in the activity itself. The addition is the roles pass on the five skills, above.

[H] Ruling 33, and it is the honest scope of everything:

We can't teach you skills. We can teach you the process. It's up to you to practise that, to build the skills, and then apply it in the life you're living.

[F card 15 d3, and Ruling 3 of the 2026-09-09 recoveries] Pathways as mechanism, said plainly, which the Hour has no room for:

⚡ ACTIVITY 4 · Fold your arms

[v3 beat 4, moved here] Fifteen seconds plus one framing sentence. Present in Foundations and Essentials; here it earns its place at beat 7 rather than beat 10 because this is where repetition is the subject.

What happens. Everyone folds their arms. Then folds them the other way.

What participants physically do. Fold, unfold, refold the wrong way. It feels wrong. That is the whole demonstration.

What the facilitator does. Demonstrates first, then:

That's harder, and it feels wrong, and it isn't wrong. It's just less practised. You've done the first one tens of thousands of times. The difference between them is repetition.

[F card 17b d3] And Foundations runs Learn It, Build It, Use It across all five skills rather than one, plus the honest reason Build It is where almost everything fails:

MOVEMENT III — the practice site, the method, the specificity argument

⚡ ACTIVITY 5 · Where the pressure is in your week

[F card 31 d3] Foundations only. Private, silent, nothing written.

What happens. Immediately after the drawbridge, the room finds its own high-pressure moments so that the low-friction rule has something concrete to be a rule about.

What participants physically do. Sit and think for about twenty seconds. Nothing said, nothing written, no hands.

What the facilitator does. Gives the search a boundary before the silence, says what to do if nothing comes, waits without filling it, and closes it himself with one bank moment said aloud rather than asking anyone for theirs. [v3 beat 4, the three-instance protocol, carried whole]:

Something from this week. Small. Don't go looking for the biggest one. ... If nothing turns up, invent one or use something you saw happen to someone else, it works exactly the same.

BEAT 9 · Stop, Shift, Do. And the unit ⛔ NEVER CUT

What changes in the room. The method gets named, and the unit of practice gets a definition people can count.

CARRIED in full: Stop, Shift, the four shift categories spoken through with examples, the too much / too little / workable question, the State Check named aloud, Do, the honest you cannot do a Do in this room, Essentials' clause distinguishing the Stop and the Shift from the Do, the phone as the rep they have already done, and the unit.

What must be said.

[H] The naming, after they have already done it twice:

Twice in the last twenty minutes you did something. You noticed, that's Stop. Some of you changed something small, and some of you deliberately didn't, that's Shift, and both of those count. And you made a next move on purpose, that's Do.

[H] ⛔ The unit, D-0107, locked:

A rep counts when you attempt it. Not when it works.

[E] ⛔ And the clause that stops the room being told performing is fake and then being asked to perform, which is not optional in any product that contains practice:

That's the Do. The Stop and the Shift are different. So later on I am going to ask you to do one Shift, on a moment that already happened to you, sitting exactly where you are. That one works in here. The Do is the one that only happens out there.

⛔ The four shift categories are the four on the live website (ruling 29e): through your body, through your attention, through your thinking, with other people, all answering too much, too little, or workable. ⚠ K-07 and D-0083 still record Move it / Zoom in or out / Ask a different question / Bring someone in, and the website marks its own wording as a copy trial. A decision record is owed and this is now the third delivered product using the trial wording. Open item 2.

Foundations widens three things.

Too much shifts down, too little shifts up. ⛔ Up is as legitimate as down ([v3 R10]): if you are flat, lifting is a shift. Essentials shows the menu and has the room use one. Foundations works every category and then says what you do when the one you would reach for is not available, which is the case that actually occurs.

[F card 26 d3, and [v3 beat 3, the taxonomy] The full rep taxonomy with an example of each, and this is the depth that makes the whole rest of the day legible:

Type What it is Example Note
Live rep Catch and respond to something happening now M-04, noticing a defensive reaction before it lands, and not biting The only fully live application
Rehearsal rep Imagine a likely moment and mentally run Stop, Shift, Do M-09, the day you are least able to be the parent who listens Real practice. Not a catch.
Reflection rep Revisit a past moment using Stop, Shift, Do M-02, the next episode you knew was the wrong call Real practice. Not a catch.

[v3] ⛔ Said exactly:

All three are worth doing. Only the first is a catch, and calling the others catches would weaken the word.

[v3 beat 3] The attempting-not-achieving standard, restated against the hard cases, which is the part only a half day has room for:

You catch it, you shift, you make the move, and it goes badly anyway. That's still a completed rep. And sometimes you catch it and there is no shift available, and no move that's yours to make. That's also a completed rep. The rep is the catching and the attempt. It has never been the result.

⚡ ACTIVITY 6 · One thing, changed

[v3 R10, carried whole. Shift, isolated] Foundations only. About ninety seconds plus a debrief. This is the first of Foundations' two practice blocks and it exists so that beat 11's work is not the first time anyone has done anything.

What happens. Each person changes exactly one thing about their state or their thinking, and notices what changed, which may be nothing.

What participants physically do. Move something, or ask themselves a different question about how today is going. One thing. Not a sequence, not a routine.

What the facilitator does. Sets the boundary at one, names the up direction explicitly, runs ninety seconds of silence without narrating it, and debriefs in one sentence:

Change exactly one thing about your state or your thinking. One. ... Up is as legitimate as down: if you're flat, lifting is a shift.

then:

That's Shift, isolated. Notice that you did it without needing to feel calm afterwards. Workable, not calm.

⛔ This is a Shift, not a Do. Nothing is staged, nothing is offered by anyone in the room, nothing is said aloud, nothing is collected. ⛔ Never require a specific Shift, and never let Shift be explained as "calm down" (recovery row 11, [v3 §7]). Correct that collectively if it comes up, never by singling anyone out.

Accessibility equivalent. A change in thinking is the equal of a change in the body and is named first, not second, so that a participant who cannot or will not move has the primary route rather than the fallback. Standing up is legitimate and participants are told they may leave the frame if this is running online.

Foundations adds over Essentials: the full shift menu worked in both directions, the rep taxonomy, the hard-case standard, and a first short practice.

What changes in the room. The room stops believing that knowing more would have helped, and starts believing that the specific moment is the only place anything transfers.

CARRIED in full: the calf raise, match day, meditation correctly placed, the knowing-doing gap, be kind be calm, Essentials' methods-correctly-placed passage, and ⛔ the honest limit, inside the argument, never at the end and never as an apology.

[H] The centre of the whole product:

That is the only gap I am claiming. Not that the others do not work.

[E] The wider Human Operating System, and ⛔ the Passenger correction, spoken and not merely intended:

The Passenger is not the villain. Fast reactions are most of what gets you through a day and they keep you safe. The only question is ever whether this one suits this moment.

⛔ Never drawn as a brain. Never a rewiring promise. Never a number of days. "The Driver takes back the wheel" appears nowhere and must not be said ([v3 beat 6a], ruling 31). ⛔ If it starts becoming a taught model with a component list, stop it where it is: a half-explained map is better than a model this product does not teach (recovery row 7).

[F card 19b d3] The full model, in two tiers, worked on the room's own moments. The Hour teaches tier one. Essentials adds the wider four as description. [F card 21 d3] Methods correctly placed, plus the basics of physical health mapped across. ⚡ ACTIVITY 7 · Say it back to one other person

[v3 §5 judgement 13, restoring v2's block 14 teach-back] Foundations only. Pairs, or solo, or to the room. About four minutes.

What happens. Each person explains Stop, Shift and Do in their own words to one other person. Retrieval by producing, which exists nowhere else in any MFC product.

What participants physically do. Turn to the person beside them. One explains the three words and what each one is for. The other listens and then says the one thing they would add. Then they swap. Nothing personal is exchanged. This is about the process, not about anybody's life.

What the facilitator does. Demonstrates the shape in fifteen seconds first. Then listens for one specific error and corrects it to the whole room, never to a person: ⛔ "Shift equals calm down." [v3 §5 judgement 13] records that v2's teach-back was the designated place to catch that error, and that in v3 the catch survives only as a reactive recovery row, which means it now depends on a participant volunteering the mistake. This activity restores the place it gets caught on purpose.

Accessibility equivalent, and it is offered aloud before anyone turns. [v3 §6], four routes, all equal:

You can do this with the person next to you, or say it to yourself in your head, or write nothing and just listen to theirs, or say it to me at the front if you'd rather. All four work.

⛔ If pair work feels unsafe or unwanted once it has started, switch immediately to the solo fallback: the facilitator speaks it through and everyone runs it alone. Do not negotiate it in front of the room (recovery row 18).

⛔ This is not a rep and is never counted as one ([v3 §6]: do not call a rehearsal, plan, teach-back or demonstration a Mental Rep).

Foundations adds over Essentials: the two-tier model run against a moment, the completed physical parallel, and the only place in any MFC product where a participant has to produce the process rather than recognise it.

⏸ BREAK 2 sits here, between movement III and movement IV.

The same join Essentials breaks at, for the same reason: it is the only place a break does not interrupt an argument mid-flight, and it puts the practice on the other side of it with the room refreshed. In Foundations the practice on the other side is forty minutes long, which makes the placement matter more, not less.

MOVEMENT IV — running it, grace, the ripple, the Radar

What changes in the room. People stop hearing about moments and start working on one of their own, and they leave this beat with a specific one selected. [H] Before anything is selected:

A rep counts when you attempt it. Not when it works.

[E] ⛔ And the routes, offered aloud rather than tolerated, every time, because this is the beat where non-participation becomes visible:

⚡ ACTIVITY 8 · The moment gallery ⛔ MANDATORY IN FOUNDATIONS

[v3 beat 7b, and ruling 29c] Hunter, 2026-09-09: "that should never have been lost... it has to be in the foundations." Foundations runs the full three-moment, three-hard-parts version. This is the longest single activity in the day.

What happens. Specific, ordinary moments are posted around the room under five arenas: self, relationships, work, performance, transitions. Participants read the wall and privately note three that connect to them.

What participants physically do. Stand, walk the room, read. Privately hold or note three moments. ⛔ No disclosure. No group formation. Nobody says which arena they stood in longest.

⛔ EXPOSURE FIX, 2026-09-09 — the arenas are not labelled on the wall. The previous design posted moments under five visible headings — self, relationships, work, performance, transitions — which meant standing still under one of them told the room something personal about you, in a room that may contain your manager. A rule about not saying which arena does not solve a problem of being seen choosing one. Ruling 8 promises nothing is asked out loud about a person's own state; this promised it and then made the answer visible.

What changes, and it costs nothing: the moments go up unsorted and unlabelled, in a single mixed sequence around the room, so a person reading any part of the wall could be reading anything. The five arenas remain the curation rule — they are how the set is chosen and balanced — and they are never printed as headings and never named aloud during the walk. The selection instruction below is unchanged, and it already sorts by hard part rather than by life area, which is the sorting that matters.

⚑ The alternative, if Hunter prefers the labelled wall: run the spoken gallery instead (option 8C in 35-THE-OPTIONS.md) — twelve moments read aloud in three groups, nobody stands. It is the only version deliverable today anyway, because the wall's corpus does not exist.

What the facilitator does. Says the selection instruction before anyone stands up, about forty-five seconds, [v3 beat 7b, verbatim]:

As you read, don't just pick three you recognise. Pick them for different reasons. Find one where the hard part is noticing it's even happening, it goes past you every time. Find one where the hard part is choosing, you notice fine, you just do the other thing anyway. And find one where the hard part is shifting, you notice, you know what you'd rather do, and you can't get from one to the other. Three moments, three different hard parts. Still easy ones.

This is what gives the five skills a consumer. Without it they are named at beat 6 and never used again by the beat that decides what the participant actually leaves with. ⚑ Only Notice, Choose and Shift are named. Focus and Connect are deliberately left out: naming a skill the room has never run produces a list, not a filter.

⛔ ACCESSIBILITY EQUIVALENT, and it is offered aloud before anyone stands up. This is a Gate 0.1 requirement and the original v3 pack failed it:

Note them if you want to, or just hold them in your head, either works, and nobody will look at your paper. You can also stay where you are and read from where you're sitting.

A seated route is required as well as a silent one. "Walk the room" is itself a mobility assumption. ⚑ Under this file's fourth rule nobody writes anything, so the default is held in the head and the paper clause is what the v3 pack said; it survives only if Hunter reopens writing. Open item 3.

⛔ Curation, not authorship. No facilitator, session or preparation step may write a new moment for the wall.

⚠ THE GALLERY'S CORPUS DOES NOT EXIST. THIS IS A BUILD DEPENDENCY, NOT A DETAIL.

The wall needs forty to sixty ordinary curated moments. The Moment Bank's verified section holds five entries, M-01 to M-05. 90-meta/agent-context-v1/14-moment-examples-bank.md says so in its own words: "It is currently 5 verified entries against a stated goal of 'a plethora'." 26-RECOVERED-FOUNDATIONS-DEVICES.md says 18 and 29-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-ESSENTIALS-90.md says 16. Both are wrong about the verified set. ⚑ The honest nuance, stated rather than smoothed: a further eleven entries carry a direct Hunter approval under later headings in the same file (M-08 added 2026-08-24; M-09 to M-16 approved 2026-08-25; M-17 and M-18 approved 2026-08-26), and M-06 and M-07 are recorded as referenced but never captured. So the count is five under the file's own "Verified" heading and sixteen if every later Hunter approval is counted. Every reading is far short of forty. And none of the sixteen is a workplace moment. The 608-row radar-widget-v1 ledger is not a substitute: every row reads qualitative_content_review: PENDING, and putting content-unreviewed material on a wall in front of participants is a decision, not a preparation step. Three routes, and none is this file's to pick. (a) Have an accountable human review the forty to sixty selected moments specifically, which is a far smaller job than reviewing 608 and closes the gate for this use. Recommended. (b) Build the wall only from the founder-approved bank, in which case the wall is sixteen moments at most and the gallery needs redesigning around a smaller wall or new moments from Hunter. (c) Accept the corpus because Hunter supplied it, which is a provenance argument answering a review question and does not hold. Under route (b) this is not a dependency, it is a redesign. Foundations still runs, on the asset-free route below, and it is weaker.

⚡ ACTIVITY 9 · The silent shift, on a moment already lived

[E, carried from Essentials whole, and given more room] The beat every product below this one compresses to nothing.

What happens. Each person takes one of their selected moments, puts it back in their head, finds where the catch was, picks one of the four shift categories, and does it, sitting where they are.

What participants physically do. Sit. Think. Then actually do the shift: feet on the floor and one slower breath, or three things they can see and the furthest sound they can hear, or ask themselves the different question, or work out who the person is and what the one sentence would be. A full minute. Eyes down or closed if they prefer.

What the facilitator does. Walks it in four short steps with a silence after each. Does one himself. Does not scan the room, does not narrate, does not comment afterwards. Then the debrief, which is the only thing said, and [E] ⛔ the rehearsal-versus-rep distinction inside it is a carried non-negotiable:

And I want to be accurate about what that was. I set it up, I timed it, and I told you when to start. A mental rep is one you catch yourself, out there, with nobody running it. What we just did is real practice and it is worth doing. It is not a catch. Both count. They are not the same thing.

Accessibility equivalent. The pass, the observe and the invented-moment routes are all said aloud before it starts, not merely permitted. The thinking route and the connecting route need no physical movement at all and are named alongside the body route, not after it.

⛔ This is a Shift, not a Do. The moment is one the participant already lived, nobody offers a live situation, nothing is said aloud, nothing is written, and no facilitator works anybody's real material.

⚡ ACTIVITY 10 · Application studios ⛔ FOUNDATIONS ONLY

[v3 beat 7c, and ruling 29d] Hunter, 2026-09-09: "We could do the application studio. Yes. And the foundations only." This is the small-group practice AG-134 requires, and it is the only device MFC has ever designed that delivers it without exposing anyone.

What happens. The room splits into two by kind of application: managing myself in a moment versus responding to another person. Each group works through a structured sequence on the moment each person selected at the gallery.

⛔ Never a split by life domain. Three reasons: nobody learns anything about your life from which studio you picked; it reliably produces two roughly even groups; and it maps a real difference, because a moment involving another person has a second party's response in it, which changes what Shift and Do can be. A sport / family / work split is exposing and produces uneven groups.

What participants physically do. Move to one side of the room or the other. Sit in threes and fours. Work through four questions on their own selected moment, out loud only as far as they choose: where the catch is · what Shift options exist · what the Do could be · what changes if the first option is gone. The group discusses the question, not each other's lives. Anyone may work a printed scenario from the bank instead of their own moment and this is said aloud at the start.

What the facilitator does. ⛔ Demonstrates one complete worked example at the front first. This is non-negotiable ([v3 beat 7c]): a self-guided studio with no worked model produces vague reflection, which this service explicitly excludes. He works a bank moment, M-01 or M-08, end to end through all four questions, naming two Shift options and then removing the first one. Then he sets both groups running and ⛔ does not circulate to listen in. He is at the front, available, not inside anybody's conversation.

Feeding back to the whole group happens on the scenario, never on a person's own moment: one thing each studio noticed about the kind of moment they worked. AG-134 is satisfied by that, and nothing personal crosses the room.

Accessibility equivalent, offered aloud before the split.

You can stay where you're sitting and work it on your own with the same four questions. You can listen without saying anything. You can use one of the printed situations instead of yours. And if you'd rather not pick a side, sit with either one, nobody is counting.

⛔ Online, there is no split and no breakout rooms ([v3 §4, corrected]). Breakout membership is a host-visible, commonly logged platform record, and the whole in-person rationale is that nobody learns anything about your life from which studio you picked. Online that stops being true. Both studio sequences are issued to everyone and the block runs as one silent self-guided pass. The cost is stated: everyone works material only half of which applies to their moment.

⛔ If the gallery runs long, do not shorten it. Take the time from the studios' second half (recovery row 21). A rushed gallery produces no selected moment and the studios then have nothing to work on.

Foundations adds over Essentials, in one line: the gallery, the studios, and a second full pass of practice on a moment the participant chose rather than one the facilitator supplied.

⚡ ACTIVITY 11 · The breakpoint pass ⛔ FOUNDATIONS ONLY

[v3 beat 6d, recovered as 22 recovery 2 and placed at beat 12] Five named places a rep stops, worked through on fictional situations only. Whole-room, facilitator-led, nothing personal.

What happens. He walks five breakpoints, gives each one a fictional situation, and answers each one the same way: this is still a completed rep, or this is a condition rather than a skill gap.

Breakpoint What to do
The Stop didn't come You noticed afterwards. That's a reflection rep, and it counts.
No workable Shift was available Naming that there wasn't one is a completed rep. Not a failed one.
The Do wasn't clear Waiting, asking, and doing nothing for now are all Dos.
Capacity or safety was the barrier This is a condition, not a skill gap. Support, delay and non-action are complete answers.
There was no opportunity No opportunity and no use are not the same thing.

What participants physically do. Listen. Nothing is asked, nothing is written, nobody is placed anywhere. ⛔ These are places to understand a situation, not grades of a person ([v3 §7 guardrail 9], the anti-hero guardrail). ⛔ Avoid hero narratives. No route here may suggest that courage is the answer or that the person should have pushed through.

What the facilitator does. Uses fictional situations only. Never invites the room to say which breakpoint is theirs. Never asks for hands.

Accessibility equivalent. None required: nothing is asked of anyone. That is by design, and it is why this block sits before the reflection rep rather than after it.

⚡ ACTIVITY 12 · The reflection rep

[v3 R7, carried whole, and ⛔ it can only sit here] About four minutes. Private throughout.

What happens. Each person revisits one ordinary moment from the last week using Stop, Shift, Do.

What participants physically do. Sit and think through three questions, about twenty seconds each. Nothing written, nothing shared, nobody asked what it was.

What the facilitator does. Sets the boundary and the escape hatch in the same breath, then asks the three questions slowly, then names exactly what it was:

Think of one ordinary moment from the last week. Not a big one, a small one. If nothing comes, invent one, or use something you saw happen to someone else. It works exactly the same. Nothing to write, nothing to share, and nobody will ask what it was.

then: "Where was the Stop? Was there one?" · "What could the Shift have been, and was one even available?" · "What was the Do, and what else could it have been?"

then, exactly:

That was a reflection rep. It's real practice and it's worth doing. It is not a catch, a catch is when you get it live, in the moment. Both count; they're not the same thing.

⛔ It can only sit after the breakpoint pass. [v3 §5 judgement 4]: without that permission arriving first, a participant looking back at a moment they missed reads it as personal failure. Do not fill the silence and do not ask for hands afterwards.

Accessibility equivalent. Invented moment, someone else's moment, or nothing at all, all named before the silence starts.

What happens. He asks the eight questions slowly, one at a time, with real silence between them. The room answers them in their own heads against the moment they selected at the gallery, worked at the studios, shifted at activity 9 and rehearsed against failure at activity 15.

What the facilitator does. Reads the eight, in this order, and says before starting that nothing is written and nobody will be asked:

My moment — the specific, recurring, ordinary one. What I might catch — the tell. A body sensation, a thought, an urge, a phrase. Stop — where in the moment the catch is realistically possible. Why two Shift options and not eight: a menu of eight is a menu nobody retrieves under load. Why "if I miss it" is on the list: missing it is what will actually happen first, and a plan with no answer for the first thing that happens gets abandoned. Why the fields belong late and not at beat 4: [v3] a plan written before the person has experienced a rep failing is a plan for a person who doesn't exist yet — and by this point the rep has failed on purpose three times at activity 15.
