The three unaided retrievals

Recovered from [v3 §1], which called spaced retrieval under variation v2's strongest single design feature. It has no successor anywhere in the current build.

# Where Anchor
1 Opens beat 11, immediately after break 2 Two beats and a break after the naming at beat 9
2 Opens beat 12, after break 3 After the day's longest working beat
3 The final act of beat 14, the last thing that happens in the room After the close

Protocol, identical each time, carried verbatim from [v3 §1]. Hide or turn the Stop – Shift – Do visual before asking. Five silent seconds. Pass or answer. ⛔ Do not count responses. Re-show only after the opportunity, then the fixed three-sentence correction:

Stop notices; Shift creates space or perspective when available; Do is an intentional next move.

⛔ Silence is a permitted answer, every time. Do not press, do not count, do not re-ask (recovery row 19).

⚠ The spacing is genuinely shorter than v3's and much shorter than v2's, and I am not claiming otherwise. v2 ran 155 minutes across two breaks between the first two; v3 ran 95 across one. This file's retrievals 1 and 2 sit one beat apart, which is the shortest interval of any version. The cause is structural and is the same one v3 recorded: the fourteen-beat spine fixes where beat openings are, retrievals can only sit at openings, and beats 9 and 10 are where the naming and the centre are. Two honest options, both Hunter's call. Either accept the short interval, which still buys three retrievals against Essentials' one; or move retrieval 2 to the opening of beat 13 and accept that retrievals 2 and 3 then sit closer together instead. I chose the first because beat 12 is where grace lives, and a retrieval that fails at beat 12 is caught by the beat that follows it.

Plus the running retrieval, from beat 9 onward: every rep debrief is spoken in the three words, and every beat from 10 to 14 opens by asking the room for the three words before he says them. That is roughly thirteen retrieval events across the day, at a few seconds each. ⛔ Do not count answers, do not correct individuals, do not press a silent room.

The Rep Plan — in or out, and on what authority

It was gated in [v3 §8 conflict 1] pending a Hunter decision, and 26-RECOVERED-FOUNDATIONS-DEVICES.md lists it as still orphaned. Here is the ruling this file takes, stated rather than slipped in.

⚑ REVISED 2026-09-10. OUT of the room entirely. ON the premade leave-behind. The previous ruling was in as spoken content, out as a written sheet, and it produced a block that failed on value: the fields were read aloud, answered silently, and kept by nobody. The fields were never the problem; the surface was. They now travel on the one surface this design already permits, printed and premade, and the eight minutes go back to the day. The two authorities below are unchanged and still hold — this revision changes which of the two available asset-free routes is taken, not the reasoning about the sheet.

The authority for keeping the content: the eight fields are the strongest single piece of downstream design MFC owns, 26 names them as worth recovering, and nothing in any ruling bars a facilitator from asking eight questions out loud.

The authority for dropping the sheet — ⚑ corrected 2026-09-10, and it is ONE record, not three. Anti-ruling 115 (butcher's paper, printed prompts, write-on cards and per-person card sets, refused on cost and on retention) is unscoped and refuses the sheet on its own. ⛔ The other two do not reach it, verified from the primary sources: ruling 23's printed-prompts clause is "No printed prompts in the hour" (00-THE-RULINGS.md:49) and Foundations is four hours; and D-0112 §1 expressly permits separate participant-owned written artefacts ("Not affected: the Radar worksheet (A4, substantive, already theirs to keep)", "Butcher's paper stays exactly as already designed for in-session writing"). The fourth standing rule of the Hour and Essentials, nobody writes anything, carried by 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-INTRODUCTION-60.md, is a separate rule — ⚑ and this file previously asserted it "is not scoped by product." Ruling 7 scopes it by product in its own words ("If it's in the sixty minute, we're not pulling out a butcher's sheet"), so it is stated here as a practice the products have held, not as an unscoped rule. 29-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-ESSENTIALS-90.md withdrew the participant's own phone as a writing surface on exactly this reasoning, and taking the opposite view one product later would be the drift this whole project exists to stop.

The decision Hunter could make, and the case for it, because he should see it rather than have it buried. D-0112 explicitly preserves "the Radar worksheet (A4, substantive, already theirs to keep)" as a separate participant-owned written artefact. On that reading a separate Rep Plan sheet is the same class of object D-0112 already permits, because it is only the leave-behind that must stay premade and unwritten, and there is no conflict at all. v3 called that the leading option and I think v3 was right about the reading. What stops me adopting it is not D-0112, it is the nobody-writes-anything rule, which is a separate rule and which no product has yet been permitted to break. If Hunter reopens writing for Foundations, the sheet comes back with its full boundaries intact: never collected, never photographed, never seen by a manager, never read aloud, never referenced in any report, never read over a shoulder, and a participant who does not write is not asked why.

What is lost by printing it rather than writing it: the plan is not specified to this participant's moment on paper — the prompts are identical for everyone and the personalisation stays in their head. That is a real cost and it is the cost the writing rule imposes, not an accident of this design. It is a smaller cost than the previous route's, which kept neither the specification nor the object.

What I took from the orphaned v3 pack, and what I deliberately left

40-FOUNDATIONS-FINAL-SERVICE-PACK-v3.md is the only prior beat-by-beat Foundations design that has ever existed. Its beat numbering is superseded by D-0131. Its content was never replaced.

Carried across, because it was better than anything written since:

  • The moment gallery in full, its five arenas, its skill-referenced selection instruction, its no-disclosure rule, its curation-not-authorship rule, and ⛔ both accessibility routes, seated and silent, which are Gate 0.1 requirements the original pack failed and which survive here.
  • The application studios, their split by kind of application, the three reasons for it, and the non-negotiable worked demonstration first.
  • The three spaced unaided retrievals and their exact protocol.
  • The breakpoint map, and the anti-hero guardrail that travels with it.
  • The Rep Plan's eight fields, including "If I miss it" and its answer — ⚑ carried onto the premade leave-behind rather than spoken in the room, 2026-09-10.
  • R8's extended form, run three times with options removed.
  • R10 as Shift isolated, including up is as legitimate as down.
  • R7 as the reflection rep, and ⛔ its positional constraint: it can only sit after the breakpoint pass has granted permission.
  • R2's body catch minus its required Do, and the "or don't" that is its load-bearing half.
  • The arise-together correction, taught explicitly, with no diagram.
  • The full rep taxonomy and its "calling the others catches would weaken the word" line.
  • The attempting-not-achieving standard against the hard cases.
  • The Passenger correction, and the ban on the Driver takes back the wheel.
  • The permission block, the shape-of-the-day line, and the no-personal-check-in-round rule.
  • The facilitator's visual specification: ⛔ one surface, three words, Stop – Shift – Do, nothing else. No definitions, no icons, no arrows, no cycle diagram. An arrow or a loop teaches a sequence this design explicitly refuses to teach. It must be turnable or coverable in under two seconds, because all three retrieval protocols depend on hiding it before asking. Foundations alone has one further surface, the four shift categories, shown only while they are being taught and removed afterwards, and never visible during a retrieval. ⚠ Neither asset exists as a produced item. They are dependencies, not descriptions.
  • The entire in-person versus online table. ⛔ Read it before delivering this online. Cameras off is fine and must be said in the first minute. No chat, no reactions, no polls, no breakouts, no recording. Real screens-off breaks. Foundations is the product whose online version is materially weakest and that is stated rather than glossed.

Deliberately left, and why:

  • The ten-rep architecture, as a count and as a spine. R3 the time catch, R4 the reaction catch, R5 the scepticism catch and R6 the transition catch all terminate in a facilitator-cued "decide, on purpose, what you're doing next." Ruling 6 bars a staged Do at any depth, ever, and AG-010 (HARD) bars working a situation someone offers. v3's own notes concede that R2's Do was a marginal pass on "occurs without manufacture" and that R5 was the weakest rep in the set. What survives is the class of device that is a Stop, a Shift, a reflection or a rehearsal with nothing staged, which is why five of the ten are here and the count is gone. ⛔ Do not restore the count. A rep total is exactly the number a funder will misread (recovery row 23).
  • The seven-beat structure and every minute band inside it. Superseded by D-0131.
  • The 270-minute product length. Foundations is 240 (22, 02-MERGED). v3's 270 predates it.
  • "Foundations is where you find out what happens when the process doesn't work" as the product's one-sentence identity. It is a good sentence and it is now only half true: the breakpoint map survives, and the moment gallery and studios make Foundations equally the product where you leave with a moment. Recorded rather than silently dropped.
  • The seven deep skills. Never in any session, in any product.
  • The organisational plan block. See immediately below.

⚠ The organisational plan — card 43 against ruling 28, and it is a third of the session

23-THE-CARD-SET.html card 43, d3: "Foundations only, and it can be a third of the session. This is the thing 240 minutes exists to make room for."

Three current records say otherwise. Ruling 28: "Foundations' differentiator this cycle is the deepest individual teaching, not organisational readiness. Route B stays built and gated but is not a marketed differentiator" (D-0110). Ruling 29: Route B is agreement, not live design, selecting from options worked out with managers beforehand, never invented in the room. [v3 §6]: organisational diagnosis lives nowhere**; any collective commitment or shared team experiment lives in the organisational engagement, not in these 270 minutes.

This file follows the rulings and the card is not built. Under the standing rule that anything matching an anti-ruling is refused before it is written, a block that has a room agreeing collective commitments at minute 200 is recovery row 22's exact scenario. What Foundations carries instead is description: the norms passages at beats 8 and 13, which say what environments reward and what they could, and stop there.

⛔ This is the single largest live disagreement in the Foundations design and it is Hunter's call, not mine. The card set is a published artifact with no vault record and is one of the four files 22 lists as carrying no supersession marking. If Hunter rules for the card, Foundations gains a block worth roughly a third of the session and ruling 28 and D-0110 both need amending in the same breath. Do not let it arrive by drift.

Facilitator recovery

27-FACILITATOR-RECOVERY.md governs, and every row tagged F applies. Not duplicated here. The rows that matter most in a half day, by beat:

Beat 3 onward, row 1, a disclosure of distress. ⛔ Its closing clause is ruled not-a-route by checklist item 18 (HARD), and the real escalation procedure is an uncleared draft requiring a qualified clinical reviewer. Beat 4, rows 3 and 4, the silence and "my mind wandered the whole time." Beat 8, rows 8, 9 and 10, the systemic-problem challenge, which is the session's own position and not a concession. Beat 9, rows 11 and 12, calm-as-the-only-shift, and "what should my State Check answer be." Beat 10, row 7, the operating system becoming a taught model. Beat 11, rows 17, 18 and 21, a scenario resembling a live dispute, pair or group work going wrong once it has started, and the gallery running long. Beat 14, rows 19, 20 and 22, silence at the retrieval, a host proposing a shared team version, and the late-session consent problem.

⛔ Five gaps bear directly on Foundations and I am not inventing rows to fill them (27 §5):

  1. No co-facilitator protocol exists anywhere. A 30-person room is permitted only with a second person and nothing says what that person does. 27 calls this the largest single gap in the set and it is the largest one here too, because Foundations is the product with the most movement, the most group work, and the longest exposure.
  2. Nobody can leave the room with a participant who walks out distressed. The one recorded attempt was found physically impossible for a solo facilitator and was never replaced.
  3. A manager naming a specific employee in a participant room. The manager session has the line; Foundations has nothing, and a manager sits in this room too (ruling 27, ruling 72).
  4. A hostile or disengaged room. Every silence row assumes willing quiet. None assumes refusal, and a half day gives refusal four hours to set.
  5. The facilitator's own error, caught by the room. No recovery line exists, and it is the one failure certain to occur in a first cohort.

If asked whether this has been shown to work, 28-HAS-THIS-BEEN-SHOWN-TO-WORK.md §1a is the ten-second answer and §1b the forty-second one. Not yet. We have not measured a group through this. What is underneath it is well tested, the session on top of it is not, and we will publish when we know. Flat and fast. It is not an apology.

The return session and the report

Inside the price, not an extension, not separately quoted (D-0113, ruling 69). Foundations runs the same return session Essentials does: 60 minutes, remote, a check-in and not a classification exercise (D-0114, ruling 24). No branching, no modules, no thresholds, no response floor, no paper-slip vote. Its four-beat shape is drafted in 29-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-ESSENTIALS-90.md and is not duplicated here.

⚠ Numbering. 22's recovery table places the return session at beat 15 and the spine has fourteen beats. It is a second session, not a fifteenth beat. Recorded rather than reconciled.

A report is issued at every cohort size (D-0132, ruling 70). What scales is what it may contain, never whether it exists. ⚠ A buyer can pay full price and receive a report with very few numbers in it, and that is stated in 2026-09-04-MEASUREMENT-v5.md and not in the buyer pack. A commercial disclosure gap, not a delivery one.

Item 1 and item 3 are Hunter's call on a contradiction between two of his own records. 30 Manager Session V2

The manager session, v2

⚠ Read this before the design

No real manager has read or sat through any version of this session — v1 or v2. The "manager panel" cited throughout 03-MANAGER-SESSION-DESIGN.md was AI-simulated: a reader panel run inside the design session that produced that file. It is not manager research, not advisor testimony and not committee evidence.

This does not block the build. It is the largest open risk on the product and it is closed by one real manager reading it, not by any further internal review. It must not be hidden, and it must not be softened into "tested with a panel."

MFC has delivered zero cohorts. Every beat below is reasoned, not observed.

1 · What this session is

A planning session with an intention. Hunter, 2026-09-09:

"It needs to be unique. It's going to feel like — oh, this is interesting. And we have to come in and there's an intention. We're coming in to plan this, we're doing this, and this is what we're wanting to be implemented at the end."

Three properties follow, and they are the whole product:

  1. High-friction workplace moments, not struggle moments (ruling 50). The participant hour's emotional register is wrong for this room. Nothing here is about how anyone is coping.
  2. The environment a manager creates, and what behaviours get rewarded (ruling 25). Hunter: "They're creating the environment, the setting, what's rewarded, what's not… for eight hours of their day, in their life. And that's why it's important."
  3. A working block where managers build something for their own team, in the room (ruling 26). This is the centre of the hour, not a closing exercise.

The double-up question, answered

Managers attend a participant session first (D-0123: the seat is counted and charged; no exclusion rule, and the session runs identically if their own reports are present). So the hour must be an addition, not a repeat.

It is, and the answer comes from inside the framework rather than being asserted. ⚑ This paragraph is design rationale and is NOT spoken in any room, changed 2026-09-10 — beat 3 used to say it out loud, and the Human Operating System is Essentials-and-above content that an Introduction buyer's managers have never been taught. K-07's Human Operating System has seven parts. Six of them sit inside a person. One — Environment — is the only one that is largely not.

⚠ Stated precisely, because ruling 41 binds it. K-07 defines Environment as "the people, places, cues, pressures and supports around you." It does not say who builds it, and v2 must not put that sentence in K-07's mouth. The 6/1 arithmetic is K-07's. That a manager is one of those people, and sets some of those places, cues and pressures, is beat 6's own demonstration — shown in the room, from the room, never asserted as framework. A team can only ever work on the inside of its own moments. A manager works on the outside of thirty other people's. That is a different job, and nobody else in the building has it.

⛔ Withdrawn: "same framework, different unit." It implies a team has mental fitness, which MFC cannot support and which invites "so what's our team score?"

⛔ Never "Manager Radar" or "Team Radar" (ruling 65). K-07 refuses it directly — "not one Radar per role." The manager's construct already exists in K-07 and had never been used: enabling conditions ⚠ (K-07 files it as Stage-3 Deepening content that "has not itself been simplified for a first explanation". v2 makes it a core construct in a one-hour room; the spoken form below is that simplification, written here and not yet approved) — "what must be available, permitted, modelled or changed around the person for the next move to be realistic." Spoken form drops the label entirely: "what has to be true around someone for the next move to be realistic."

⚠ Three of the four "this is an addition" arguments require managers to have attended the participant session. Nothing in the buyer pack or the pricing model requires that attendance. Open, carried from v1, unchanged.

2 · The load-bearing argument

Not an analogy. Arithmetic, in the room.

You answer the nine p.m. email in four minutes. You answer the Tuesday lunchtime one on Thursday. Nobody ever said a word about when to send things. And everybody now knows when to send things.

You are already rewarding behaviour. You just aren't choosing which.

This replaces v1's driving / times-tables / bins set, which Hunter cut: "I don't know what this is. How is that carrying a whole product?" It needs no analogy, it is in his own register, and — unlike the cut set — it generates the working block rather than merely preceding it. It also puts ruling 25's named subject, rewarding the behaviours you want to see, at the centre where it belongs.

3 · The spine — four movements, twelve beats

No minutes (rulings 1, 2). Beats widen; order never changes. Duration is a property of a beat in a product, not of the spine.

⚠ This is a separate spine, and ruling 3 does not reach it. Ruling 3 fixes the participant spine at four movements over fourteen beats (D-0131), and its movements are the participant hour's own ("Is this me?", "Can it change?"). Ruling 25 says the manager session is a separate product and never a compression of the participant foundation, so it carries its own spine. Twelve beats here is not a violation of fourteen there — but ruling 3 as written is unqualified, and this qualification is the system's reading, not Hunter's. If he wants one spine across all four products, this file is what changes.

Movement A — What this hour is, and what it isn't

Beat 1 · The frame. This is a planning session. You will leave with something for your own team that you intend to implement. Nothing is collected and nobody is asked to speak (ruling 8).

⚑ WRITTEN 2026-09-10. This beat previously had no spoken words at all — it described what the frame was and left the facilitator to invent the first thing the room hears.

"This is a planning hour. It isn't a workshop and it isn't a wellbeing session. By the end of it you'll have one thing, for your own team, that you actually intend to do next week.

Nothing you come up with in here is collected. I don't see it, nobody reports on it, and there's no going round the table. You don't have to say anything for the whole hour if you don't want to.

You're in this room because you're not just doing your own week. You're setting the conditions everybody else's week happens inside, and nobody else in the building has that job."

⚠ The third paragraph is the beat's only forward-leaning claim and it is deliberately small. It sets up beat 3 and beat 4 without borrowing their arguments, and it says nothing about what a manager causes.

Beat 2 · The scope rule, said to their face. ⚠ Placed here deliberately, before any friction example is named. Compliance requirement carried from the held version: the register change from struggle to workplace friction reduces clinical exposure and increases legal and industrial exposure, because "high-friction workplace moments" sits close to the descriptive language of the psychosocial hazards in the WHS regulations, and what a manager names in the room may concern a live grievance. The scope rule must arrive first, not as a mid-hour correction.

Carried forward in full and unweakened (ruling 46; claim-boundary load-bearing):

"One boundary, because otherwise this hour gets used for the wrong thing.

If the real problem is workload, or staffing, or safety, or one specific person behaving badly, that is not a habit, and I'm not going to let us turn it into one. Nothing in this hour fixes it and pretending otherwise would be the wrong thing to do with it. Those go through whatever your organisation actually has for them.

And to be plain about what this isn't: it's not a hazard assessment, it doesn't tell you whether anything here is safe or unsafe, and it doesn't discharge anything you owe anybody. There's a free government tool for that side of it and it's better at it than I am.

And the honest version of the same boundary, because it's the one that matters most and it's the reason you're in this room rather than just them. A skill doesn't replace a bad environment. If the conditions are genuinely against your people, no amount of noticing a moment fixes that, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. What you can move is the part that's ordinary, and that's most of the week.

The four levers are for the ordinary week. That's genuinely most of it, and it's not nothing."

(Delivery note carried from v1: in a community group, club or volunteer setting, cut the government-tool sentence and keep the boundary.)

Two additions required by the register change, both new in v2:

  • The named-matter exclusion, said aloud. "If a moment you're thinking of is about one named person, or it's already in a formal process, don't use it here. Pick a different one. This hour isn't the place for it and I'm not the person for it."
  • The no-record rule, said aloud rather than merely being true. "Nothing you write goes anywhere. I don't see it, we don't collect it, it isn't reported to anyone, and there's no record of this session beyond that you attended." It was already true under D-0112; a manager weighing whether to name something real needs to hear it, not to have it be quietly the case.

⛔ AG-011 / AG-012: never call Stop / Shift / Do a WHS control, here or anywhere. The negative scope is stated in this beat, repeated at beat 11, and repeated in the thirty-second upward pitch at beat 12. Both register entries are pending-approval; no grading exists and none may be asserted.

Beat 3 · The double-up answer.

⚑ REWRITTEN 2026-09-10 — the six-of-seven arithmetic is cut from the spoken beat. It rested the single most sceptical moment in the hour on K-07's Human Operating System, which is Essentials-and-above content. A manager whose organisation bought the Introduction has never heard of it, so for that buyer the beat was arithmetic on a model that does not exist. And the same point arrives two beats later, at level three, when the room looks at itself (beat 5) and then at the nine p.m. email (beat 4). The abstraction is cut and the demonstration carries it, which is this whole product's own preference stated in §1: shown in the room, from the room, never asserted as framework.

"Some of you are sitting there thinking you've just done this. You have, and this isn't that.

Everything in that session happened inside one person's own head. That's where it has to happen, and it's real. But not one thing in it was about the conditions those moments happen in, because nobody in that room could change them.

You can. That's the difference, and that's the whole hour."

Your team can do Learn It without you. They cannot do Build It without you, because Build It is the part that's visible and slow, and you're the one who decides what slow costs around here.

⚠ K-07's 6/1 arithmetic stays in §1 as design rationale and is not spoken in any room. It is why the beat is true; it is not how the beat is delivered.

Learn It / Build It / Use It is the spine of the manager's version of the argument. The five skills are named with why they matter and are not taught here (ruling 30). "We can't teach you skills. We can teach you the process" (ruling 33) applies to this room exactly as to the participant room.

Movement B — You are already rewarding behaviour

Beat 4 · The arithmetic. §2 above. The nine p.m. email and the Tuesday lunchtime one. Ends on: you are already rewarding behaviour, you just aren't choosing which.

Beat 5 · The room as an environment. Carried forward verbatim (Hunter kept this explicitly):

"Look at this room for a second. Actually look. Chairs in rows facing me. Phones face up. That's an environment doing its job, and it isn't neutral. It's telling everyone in here how to behave, and it's working. Nobody voted for it. I set it up in four minutes."

Beat 6 · The four levers. Carried forward. The four cue locations read back as things the manager controls — people; places; objects and screens; times and transitions — including, load-bearing:

"People. For everyone who works for you, you are on that list. You're one of the people who's there when it happens. Some days you make it easier and some days you make it harder, and it's usually the same you."

And carried with it, because it is what stops the beat becoming guilt: "plenty of you don't decide any of it… that band isn't yours. That's a fact about your job, not a failing. Cross it off and use the other three."

⚠ Terminology. These are not "the Radar's four hiding places" and not a Radar of any kind. They are a cue-location device living in the workshop design layer, appearing in no foundations record. The manager's construct is enabling conditions (§1).

Beat 7 · The reward boundary. The one instruction in this product that most needs to be right.

"You're going to reward something this week whether you mean to or not. So choose it. Reward what somebody does in the shared work. They left a gap in the agenda, they came back to a decision instead of firing off the reply, they said the thing later instead of in the moment. That's visible, it's about the work, and everyone can see the same thing you saw.

Never reward evidence that a person is practising. Not who's using it, not who's got a list, not who's doing their reps. And never reward a state. Not who seems calmer, not who looks like they're handling it better. The second you do either of those, you've made it a performance, and the people who most need the three seconds are the ones who'll stop taking them."

⛔ This boundary is CONSTRUCTED, NOT AUTHORISED — and must be recorded as such wherever it is used. A sweep of all 379 entries in 50-authority/advisor-guidance-register/REGISTER.md — re-counted against the live register on 2026-09-09, correcting the stale figure of 326 that the held version and several other files still carry — found zero entries on reward, observation or monitoring. The two near-misses are AG-069 (webinar ROI) and AG-331 (brand recognition), neither on point. There is no advisor position behind this line. It is MFC's own reasoning, written by the system, and it is the riskiest instruction in the product because it tells a manager what to notice about their staff.

The one question that converts it into a HARD ruling, for Eimear Quigley (clinical psychologist, committee):

"In a workplace session we tell managers to reward what someone does in the shared work, and never to reward evidence that a person is practising or any change in how they seem. Is that the right boundary, and is there anything in it that would make a manager more likely to start reading their staff rather than less?"

One question, one answer, and the line stops being constructed. Until it is asked, this beat is delivered as designed and disclosed as unauthorised — it is not blocked, and it is not presented as ruled.

Movement C — The moment bank and the moves

Beat 8 · The friction moments. Given, never a blank page (AG-147). See §4 for the bank and for what was cut out of it.

⚑ WRITTEN 2026-09-10. This beat previously had no spoken words — it named the requirement and handed over a table.

"I'm not going to ask you to think of something from nothing. That's the part that never works, and it's not because people can't think.

Here are six that come up in nearly every team I've been in. Read them, and find the one that's most like your week. If none of them is yours, take the closest one and change it in your head until it is.

One. Not a list. The whole thing after this runs on one."

⛔ The six are read or shown, never expanded into examples of who they happen to. The moment is a piece of the week's structure, never a person in it.

Beat 9 · The move menu, sorted by the four levers. Each move is a change to a condition, never a change to a person. Every one is something a manager does, that someone else would see.

⚑ WRITTEN 2026-09-10. This beat previously had no spoken words — three tables and no line to carry them.

"Two lists, and then I'll shut up and you'll build the thing.

First, moves. Every one of these is a change to a condition, not a change to a person. That's on purpose and it's the rule the whole hour runs on.

Second, the sentence. This is the part nobody's ever been asked to write, and it's the only part of your plan another human ever hears. It's about the work. Never about how somebody seems.

You're taking one from each. One move, one sentence. One is the whole exercise."

Read aloud twice, and on the leave-behind's move panel — a spoken menu alone is a weaker prompt than a printed one (AG-147), and v1 already recorded that as a known weakness.

Lever Moves
Times and transitions Put a gap between two things that currently touch. Move the hardest conversation off the end of a Friday. Stop taking updates in the last five minutes. Give the question before the meeting rather than in it.
Objects and screens Schedule-send anything written after hours. Say once, out loud, what your own out-of-hours message does and does not mean. Take one recurring thing off the channel that pings.
Places Make one route to contribute that isn't speaking first in front of everyone. Find somewhere a handover can happen that isn't in a doorway with someone waiting. Make your door a real door, or stop calling it open.
People Say out loud, once, that taking a few seconds before answering is fine here — and then be the one who does it in front of them. Stop being the first voice in the round.

⛔ Every move above is a condition. If a proposed move names a person, counts anybody's anything, or depends on watching how someone seems, it is not a move — it fails the fifth test at beat 10 and it breaches beat 7's boundary. This applies to F6 without exception (§4).

The five notice stems — given, because the notice is the part nobody has ever been asked to write and the part AG-147 most applies to. Each is about the shared work and none is about a person's practice or state:

  1. "That's a better way round than what I asked for."
  2. "You came back to that instead of firing off the reply. That's the one I want."
  3. "You left a gap in that agenda on purpose, didn't you. Keep doing that."
  4. "You said the thing later instead of in the moment and it landed better. Noted."
  5. "I noticed nobody had to speak first there. That was you."

Three worked example plans, so nobody is composing the shape and the content at once:

Moment Move Notice
The stand-up round-the-table where everyone hears how long you took (F1) I stop going in the same order, and I stop being the first voice "I noticed nobody had to speak first there. That was you."
Messages I send that land in someone's evening (F3) Anything I write after six gets schedule-sent for the morning "You came back to that instead of firing off the reply. That's the one I want."
The hardest conversation on a Friday afternoon (F4) It moves to Tuesday morning, and there is a gap after it "You left a gap in that agenda on purpose, didn't you. Keep doing that."

Movement D — Build it, in the room

Beat 10 · The working block — the moment, the move, and the notice. The centre of the product (ruling 26).

Three parts:

  1. The moment — which recurring bit of your week you're changing.
  2. The move — what you will do differently that somebody would actually see.
  3. The notice — what you'll say out loud, once, when you see someone else do it.

The third part is what Hunter said was missing everywhere, and it is the only part of the plan another human hears. It is also where beat 7's boundary does its work: the notice is said about the shared work, never about a person's practice and never about their state.

⚑ THE SPOKEN ROUTE, WRITTEN 2026-09-10, AND IT IS SAID BEFORE ANYONE PICKS UP A PEN. The whole block was written, the only opt-out in it was the pair reading, and a manager who cannot write comfortably or would rather not had no stated route through the centre of the product. Every other MFC product carries a head-held default; this one is the product whose output is a written artefact, which is exactly why the route has to be said out loud rather than assumed.

"Write it or don't. If you'd rather keep it in your head, keep it in your head. It's three things, and it's three things either way: the moment, the move, and the sentence. Say them to yourself until you can say them without thinking. Nobody's checking your page and nobody's collecting it."

⚠ Anti-ruling 115, named here rather than left unnamed. It refuses "butcher's paper, printed prompts, write-on cards, per-person card sets", and this block runs on a per-person write-on sheet. This file previously argued only that D-0112 does not reach in-session writing, which is a different record, while its sibling file used 115 to strip a written sheet out of Foundations on the same day. Two products, one day, opposite conclusions on one anti-ruling. The spoken route above closes the accessibility gate either way — nobody is now excluded from the centre of the product by not writing — but whether managers may be handed a sheet at all is a ruling, and it is Hunter's. Recorded as open item 10, not resolved here.

The facilitator builds his own first, badly, and repairs it in front of them. That is what unblocks the page — not encouragement, and not a better prompt. It is the same principle as ruling 29d's non-negotiable worked demonstration in the application studios.

Then the five tests. Managers apply these to their own draft:

Test The question
The diary test Is there an actual recurring slot in your week this lands in?
The bad-Tuesday test Would you still do it on your worst day of the month?
The permission test Do you actually control this, or does someone above you?
The witness test Would anyone on your team notice you'd done it without being told?
The no-names-no-numbers test Does it name a person, or count anybody's anything? If so, rewrite it.

Then, if they want to, a pair reads it with one job: tell them which of the five they'd fail.

⚠ The opt-out is written into the beat, not assumed. Spoken: "If you'd rather not show anyone, don't. Run the five yourself. It works either way and nobody's checking." Ruling 8 — nobody speaks unless they want to — binds this room exactly as it binds the participant room, and a sheet a manager has just written about their own team is the single most likely thing they would decline to show. The tests, not facilitator attention and not the pair, are what makes this scale to twenty.

Beat 11 · The three closes. Carried forward. Nothing was said out loud and nothing is collected; it will miss, and remembering late is still a rep; and the don't —

"Third, about your team, and it's the only thing I'll ask of you, and it's a don't. When they come back they'll have written one sentence on their own phone. Don't go looking for it. If they bring it up, ask how it's going, that's a normal conversation. But don't ask what they wrote, don't ask to see it, and don't open with it. That's the one thing that would undo the whole thing.

And I'll give you the reason rather than just the rule, because the rule on its own won't survive a week. From where you're sitting, "how did that go?" is a friendly question. From where they're sitting it's their manager asking. There's about one beat between that and "what did you put?", and they know it before you do."

And the safety line, carried forward verbatim. Safeguarding load-bearing (ruling 47):

⚠ "Panel eight" is v1's leave-behind panel number. v2 has not yet specified the leave-behind's panels, so it is carried here exactly as spoken and must be re-pointed at the actual referral panel before delivery (ruling 23: one consolidated leave-behind). Do not drop the pointer in order to fix the number — a safeguarding line that names no route is worse than one that names the wrong panel.

"And one thing that isn't true, which matters more than any of this. If someone on your team goes quiet, or slow, or flat, that is not them doing this. Don't read anything as a technique. This is one sentence on a phone; it doesn't change how anybody looks. If you're worried about someone, then you're worried about someone, and that's the same route it's always been. Panel eight, and whatever your organisation has. Nothing in this hour is a reason to wait and see."

Beat 12 · Thirty seconds upward, and the door out. The line a manager gives their own boss, capped so it cannot become a claim, with the non-discharge repeated.

⚑ WRITTEN 2026-09-10, AND THIS IS THE LAST THING ANYONE HEARS. The beat previously had no spoken words, which meant the session's final words did not exist — and §5 records the AG-011 / AG-012 negative scope as "stated at beat 2, beat 11 and beat 12", so a compliance control was recorded as being carried by a line nobody had written. It is written now, and it is the load-bearing sentence in the middle paragraph.

"Last thing, and it's for the conversation you'll have on the way out of here.

Somebody above you is going to ask what this was. Here's the whole answer, and don't add to it: we spent an hour on the ordinary friction in our week, and I've picked one thing I'm changing and one thing I'll say out loud when I see somebody else do it. That's it. It's small on purpose.

And be straight about what it isn't, because this is the bit that gets people into trouble. This is not a safety control. It isn't a hazard assessment, it doesn't tell anyone whether anything here is safe or unsafe, and it doesn't discharge one thing this organisation owes anybody. If it gets written up as any of those, that's wrong, and you're the person standing closest to it.

[The community line goes here. See the note below: it says what exists on the day, and nothing that doesn't.]

That's the hour. One moment, one move, one sentence."

⛔ The negative-scope paragraph is AG-011 / AG-012 and is never compressed into a clause, never moved earlier to save time, and never softened because the room is in a good mood at the end. Both register entries are pending-approval; no grading exists and none may be asserted.

⚠ The community line is left as a bracket deliberately. It cannot be written until it is known whether the page resolves on the day, and writing a plausible sentence now is how a sign-up ends up pointing at nothing. This is a real dependency, not an omission. The Leadership Community sign-up goes in every service (ruling 29b) and is not blocked — see the reconciled note below, which is now stated in these words in all four products.

⚠ ⚑ RECONCILED ACROSS ALL FOUR PRODUCTS, 2026-09-10 — this beat is IN, and it is not cut. CLAUDE.md §4a applied and shown, rather than each product deciding for itself. Ruling 29b is Hunter, 2026-09-09, correcting a proposal to keep the sign-up out of the paid hour: "I think that should be in every single service that we do." D-0111 §3's build gate has no external basis — no regulator, licence, contract or qualified human asked for it. It is MFC's own caution, so the ruling is the better evidence and the internal gate is not enforced meanwhile.

⛔ The one real constraint is practical, not a gate. The beat must promise nothing that does not exist on the day: no frequency, no format, no description of what a person gets. If a destination resolves on the day it is named; if it does not, the beat says what is coming and how to hear about it, and the leave-behind carries nothing. The wording above is written to survive both cases.

⛔ ONE OPEN QUESTION, AND IT IS HUNTER'S — recorded identically in all four products and resolved by no agent: does D-0111 §3's not authorised for build stand, or is it retired by ruling 29b? Until he answers, the beat runs as written above. Recommendation: follow the ruling.

⚑ Why this note exists. Until 2026-09-10 the Hour, Essentials and Foundations each marked this ⛔ BLOCKING and cut the beat, while 30-MANAGER-SESSION-v2.md lines 463–469 ruled the opposite and put the sign-up in. Four products, one day, opposite rulings on the same question — Checklist E3, which is a gate. This is now the single position and it is stated in all four files in these words.

4 · The moment bank for beat 8 — and the three that were cut

90-meta/agent-context-v1/14-moment-examples-bank.md lists 18 entries but records only 5 as verified, against a stated goal of "a plethora" — and not one workplace-manager moment at any status. Its standing rule: no skill or session may invent a new moment. The held version's eight friction moments included three inventions.

⚠ And the bank's own last application of that rule went the other way, which v2's first draft did not surface. When an audit flagged M-09 to M-16 as invented, Hunter ruled: "the invented parent[s] [and] sport [moments], that's okay. Please revert that back." The governing precedent for "an AI invented a moment" is therefore ask Hunter, not cut it. Cutting three prompts unilaterally on a rule whose own precedent points the other way is one-directional caution (L-084).

So they are held, not deleted, and the ask is one line. ⛔ They do not go in a room until Hunter answers. The hour runs on the six sourced prompts meanwhile, which is enough for AG-147.

⛔ HELD — invented, not derivable from any approved MFC script. One question to Hunter: "Three manager friction moments were written by the system rather than taken from anything you've said — the meeting that runs over, the decision made above you, and 'got a sec?' for the eleventh time. You kept the invented parent and sport moments last time. Same call here, or do you want these to come from a real manager?"

# Held moment Why it is held
1 The meeting that runs over No source. Plausible, which is exactly the problem (14-moment-examples-bank standing rule; onboarding §2a Q3). Lowest risk of the three.
2 The decision made above you No source, and it is the one most likely to pull the room toward grievance material the scope rule has just excluded.
3 "Got a sec?" for the eleventh time No source, and person-shaped — it makes a colleague the friction. ⛔ This one does not come back even if Hunter approves the other two, unless it is reframed onto the structure the way F6 was. It is the same defect F6 had.

✅ KEPT — each derived from language already approved and spoken in MFC's own manager script (03-MANAGER-SESSION-DESIGN.md, M6 and M7, which Hunter read and did not reject):

# Friction moment Lever Source line
F1 The stand-up where you go round the table and everyone can hear how long you took times and transitions M6 diagnostic, spoken verbatim
F2 A handover with somebody physically waiting behind you places M6 diagnostic, spoken verbatim
F3 The message you send that lands on somebody's screen in their evening objects and screens M6 four levers, spoken verbatim
F4 The hardest conversation put in the last twenty minutes of a Friday times and transitions M6 four levers, spoken verbatim
F5 There being nowhere to stand that isn't in front of everyone places M6 four levers, spoken verbatim
F6 Your own three-second decision about a silence in a meeting people reframed; see below

Six prompts run the hour. Six satisfies AG-147 — nobody is facing a blank page — and it is better than eight with three MFC cannot source. Anything Hunter approves or a real manager supplies goes into the moment bank first and into this table second, in that order.

⛔ F6 — the reframe that is not optional

Hunter's brief named "the person who's gone quiet in stand-ups." As written, that invites a manager to read a quiet person as a signal — colliding head-on with beat 11's safety line (a quiet, slow or flat employee is not a technique), with beat 7's reward boundary, and with the participant hour's promise that nobody is asked to notice anything about anybody.

It stays reframed onto the structure. The friction is the manager's own three-second decision about the silence, and every legitimate move is structural — how the round-the-table works, whether there is a way to contribute that isn't speaking first, whether the question was askable cold. No move under F6 may be about the person.

This is a claim-limits question, not a design choice. The person-shaped version does not get reintroduced by anyone, at any point, for any reason.

5 · What binds everything a manager hears

  • K-08 — the claims boundary, in every line of this hour. Can, not will (ruling 34). Organisational outcomes are target-and-cite, never assertion (ruling 40). Nothing may be said about the framework that has not been said and approved (ruling 41).
  • AG-001 — binds every claim made to a manager. Managers hear organisational language more readily than participants do, which makes this room the easiest place to drift.
  • AG-011 / AG-012 — ⛔ Stop / Shift / Do is never a WHS control. Stated at beat 2, beat 11 and beat 12. ⚑ The beat 12 statement was recorded here before it existed as a line; it is now written into that beat verbatim, 2026-09-10. Both entries are pending-approval; no grading exists.
  • Ruling 36 — where the environment is the real problem, MFC is not the answer and says so.
  • Ruling 45 — no external statistic enters this room without a registered source.
  • 28-HAS-THIS-BEEN-SHOWN-TO-WORK.md — the scripted answer, and it is asked in this room too, in its buyer register. The ten-second version stands unchanged: "Not yet. We haven't measured a group through this. What's underneath it is well tested; the hour on top of it isn't. We'll publish when we know." And per P35, the manager session is deliberately not measured — say so, and say why: what each manager writes is private, on their own phone, and collecting it would produce the version people write to be collected.

The recovery file needs a manager-spine column, and does not have one.

27 Facilitator Recovery

Facilitator recovery — when the room goes wrong

What this is. The scripted responses that let one person run the room alone. Thirty-seven situation rows and ten standing guardrails. Rows 1-23 are recovered from five orphaned source files and re-anchored to the fourteen-beat spine. Rows 24-37 were written on 2026-09-10 to cover the four activities that put a participant inside a real difficult moment and had no scripted recovery at all, plus the hostile room and the facilitator's own error. They are marked ⚑ and are new writing, not recovery.

How to read a row. Beat is where the situation arises under the current spine. Product says where the row can actually happen — the Introduction is a keynote in which nobody writes, speaks on demand, or performs anything (rulings 7, 8), so rows that assume an exercise is running belong only to Essentials and Foundations. Flag marks a row that breaks a current ruling or carries an unresolved dependency. A flagged row is still carried. It is not dropped and it is not silently kept.

Row numbers are stable identifiers, not reading order. Rows 1-23 keep the numbers they were recovered under, because other files cite them (31-FOUNDATIONS-240-STRUCTURE.md cites row 23 by number). New rows 24-37 were appended to whichever movement table their beat belongs to, so the numbering runs out of sequence down the page. Nothing was renumbered.

Product codes: I Introduction (The Mental Fitness Hour) · E Essentials · F Foundations.

1 · The one thing to fix before any of this is used

Four rows below end with "follow the host's approved support process if one exists."

41-EVERY-WORKSHOP-CHECKLIST-v1.md item 18 (HARD) rules on that exact wording:

"A recovery line that defers to 'the host's approved process if one exists' is not a route."

It is carried verbatim anyway, because it is what the facilitator currently has and deleting it leaves nothing. But it is not a route, and this file does not turn it into one. The real procedure exists as 14-build-readiness-and-expert-lens-v1/04-escalation-and-distress-response-procedures-DRAFT.md, whose own frontmatter says it is draft-not-cleared-requires-qualified-clinical-and-legal-review. Its open questions to a clinical reviewer include the exact scripted wording for the in-the-moment check-in — the words that would replace the deferral line. That draft is the missing object, and only a qualified human closes it. Not this file, and not an agent.

2 · Standing guardrails — true at every beat, in every product

Carried verbatim from 40-...-v3.md §7 items 1-10 (which themselves carry 07-FOUNDATIONS-FACILITATOR-PACKET-v1.md).

  1. Keep private reflection private. No person needs to explain a choice or a barrier.
  2. Do not call a rehearsal, plan, teach-back or demonstration a Mental Rep.
  3. Do not imply more practice guarantees access, success or wellbeing.
  4. Do not sell or score team components as part of Foundations' routine value.
  5. If time compresses: see row 9. (Change marked: the original item 5 named specific reps and minute-band protections belonging to the retired eleven-part run sheet. The current compression authority is 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md's C1-C5 / E1-E5 / F1-F6 orders.)
  6. Never require a specific Shift; never let Shift be explained as "calm down."
  7. Never say practice will make a new pattern feel natural.
  8. Do not read, collect, photograph or comment on any participant's written work. (Change marked: original said "any participant's Rep Plan." The Rep Plan is Foundations-only and is gated on the D-0112 conflict; the guardrail is broader than the artefact and is stated at its real scope.)
  9. Breakpoints are places to understand a situation, not grades of a person. Fictional situations only.
  10. Avoid hero narratives. Support, delay and non-action are complete answers.

3 · The recovery rows

Movement I — arrival, the gap, the door, the breath (beats 1-4)

# Situation Response Beat Product Flag
1 A participant discloses distress or an unsafe situation Thank them briefly; do not invite detail or group advice. Name that safety or support may be the next appropriate step; follow the host's approved support process if one exists. Beat 3 onward — product-general I E F ⛔ §1 above. The closing clause is ruled not-a-route by checklist item 18 (HARD).
2 The room is silent at a recognition question "You do not need to respond — quiet recognition is enough." Continue. Do not count or record. Beats 2, 6 I E F Now explicitly permitted: ruling 17 allows hands up for recognition ("have you heard of this", "do you recognise this"), never for a person's own state.
3 The silence becomes uncomfortable Let it run. Do not narrate, shorten or fill it. If someone laughs or speaks, continue without comment. Beat 4 I E F ⚑ Change marked: original read "the sixty seconds of silence." 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT now runs ninety seconds. No duration carried (ruling 1).
4 "My mind wandered the whole time / I couldn't do it" "That's the rep. The wandering isn't the failure — catching it is the whole thing." The wandering is the precondition for the rep, not its failure. Beat 4 I E F —
24 Someone answers "the technique that did not work" out loud, names a person, or names their employer "Don't tell me what it was — that one's yours." Say it once, do not repeat it, do not respond to the content, and go straight to your own closing line. Do not thank them for sharing and do not build on what they said — either turns a private prompt into a shared one. Beat 2 (Foundations activity 1) F ⚠ This activity currently runs BEFORE the safety door at beat 3. The row recovers the moment either way; whether a private prompt about a past disappointment may precede the door is a ruling, not a recovery — see gap 10.
25 "Nothing came to mind", at the technique prompt or at any private prompt "That's a complete answer. Nothing to fix." Move on at the same pace. Do not offer a substitute prompt to the room to rescue it — the boundary already permits nothing. Beat 2 onward — every private prompt E F Consistent with ruling 8. The nothing-comes route is said before the silence starts in the design; this row is for when it is asked after.
26 A hostile or disengaged room — arms folded, phones down or out, nobody responding to anything, including recognition prompts Do not name it, do not ask what is wrong, and do not ask the room to try harder. Drop every recognition prompt for the next beat and keep teaching. Say once, flatly, without apology: "You don't have to do any of this out loud. Nothing here gets collected and nobody gets asked anything." Then continue at normal pace to the next private device. If it is still cold at the next beat, keep delivering the content and finish the session. Product-general, from beat 1 I E F ⚑ New row, 2026-09-10 — closes gap 8. Every other silence row assumed willing quiet. Deliberate limit: a solo facilitator cannot convert a hostile room, and this row does not pretend to. What it protects is that refusal costs nothing and is never read aloud (ruling 8, guardrail 1). A room that is hostile because of something in the organisation is not a facilitation problem and is not this row's to solve (rulings 46, 47).

Movement II — naming, the category, the skills, muscle memory (beats 5-7)

# Situation Response Beat Product Flag
5 Someone challenges the distinction from mindfulness or therapy Agree that many practices support in-the-moment awareness; state that this session offers one simple language and process and is not competing with care or other practices. Beat 5 I E F —
6 The room unpicks the skills-to-basis mapping Agree it doesn't line up neatly — two skills work across all four, three sit inside them. Do not defend a tidier version. Beat 6 I E F —
7 The Human Operating System starts becoming a taught model Stop it at its budgeted length regardless of where you are. A half-explained map is better than a model this product does not teach. Beat 10 (tier one is taught in the hour, ruling 31) I E F ⛔ Ruling 1. Original read "Stop it at five minutes." Minute removed; the instruction is unchanged.

Movement III — the practice site, the method, the specificity argument (beats 8-10)

# Situation Response Beat Product Flag
8 A participant says the process ignores systemic problems / real problems Agree. Individual choices do not replace fair conditions, safety or support. Return to the boundary sentence and to the environment content. This is the session's own position, not a concession. Beat 8 I E F ⚑ Change marked: originals said "return to the minute-two / minute-three boundary" and "beat 6" under the retired numbering. Re-anchored to beat 8, which now carries the environment boundary.
9 "So I just have to cope better" "No — the opposite. We said early on this isn't a promise you can solve conditions alone. What we practised is what's available to you inside the moment, which is a different question from whether the conditions are right." Beat 8 I E F ⚑ Change marked: "we said in minute three" → "we said early on" (ruling 1).
10 Anything converting a contextual problem into "mindset" Name the condition as a condition. The environment boundary exists for this. Beat 8 I E F —
11 Someone offers "calm down" as the only Shift "Calm might be welcome, but it isn't the requirement. The goal is workable enough for this moment." Correct collectively, never singling anyone out. Beat 9 I E F ⚑ Ruling 29e: the shift tools are now the four on the live website (body / attention / thinking / other people), and K-07/D-0083 still record the older names. The correction line itself is unaffected; the menu it points at is unresolved.
12 Someone asks what their State Check answer should be "There's no should, and I'm not going to ask anyone for theirs. It's a question you ask yourself." Beat 9 I E F Consistent with ruling 8 — nothing is asked out loud about a person's own state.
13 The visual fails Teach verbally; ask for the three words at close regardless. Beats 5, 9, 14 I E F —
14 Discussion runs long Take the cuts in the predetermined order for the product being delivered. Do not improvise a cut with the clock running. Product-general I E F ⛔ Ruling 1 and ruling 3. The original rows carried per-product cut orders naming retired beat numbers and minute values. They are not carried. The current authority is 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md: C1-C5 at 58, E1-E5 at 90, F1-F6 at 240, with the never-compress floor in RULE 5.
27 A participant is visibly distressed during the silent shift Do not stop the room and do not go to them mid-silence — both make them the subject of the room. Let the minute finish as written. Say the debrief as written, then release the room to the break or the next beat, and be near the door rather than at the front. If they come to you, row 1 governs from there. Beat 9 (Foundations activity 9) · beat 11 (Essentials) E F ⛔ §1 governs. This row deliberately stops at "be available". MFC's own escalation threshold and the words for a private check-in are open items requiring qualified clinical input (04-escalation-and-distress-response-procedures-DRAFT.md); nothing here invents them. Distress beyond a person needing a moment routes to GP, Lifeline 13 11 14, or 000 per AG-004.
28 Someone cannot find a moment, or freezes, during the silent shift Nothing in the moment — do not approach, do not check. The routes are already said aloud before the silence starts; say them again at the top of the silence rather than to the person: "If nothing comes, invent one, or use something you saw happen to someone else. It works exactly the same." Then the silence runs full length regardless. Beat 9 (F activity 9) · beat 11 (E) E F ⚑ New row. Depends on the pass / observe / invented-moment routes being spoken before the minute starts, which is a design non-negotiable, not a recovery option.
29 Someone starts talking to a neighbour during the silent shift Do not shush, do not look at them, do not restart. Keep your own eyes down and let the minute run. At the next natural boundary, to the whole room: "One thing about that one — it only works in your own head. Nothing gets said out loud." Never addressed to the pair. Beat 9 (F activity 9) · beat 11 (E) E F ⚑ New row. Correct collectively, never singling anyone out — same rule as row 11.
30 A manager or host asks afterwards what people picked "I don't know, and I didn't ask. That one's private by design — that's why people actually do it." Do not soften it into a partial answer, do not describe the room, do not say what you saw. If pressed: "I can tell you what we practised. I can't tell you what anyone chose." Beat 9 onward, and after the session E F Ruling 8 and guardrail 8. Ruling 47: managers are told not to go looking for what their team wrote. Row 15 covers the same demand made during the room; this covers it made after.
31 The room will not engage with the silent shift at all — nobody settles, movement and noise throughout Run it anyway, at full length, exactly as scripted. Do not shorten it, do not swap it for discussion, and do not comment on the room afterwards. Then the debrief as written and move on. A minute that half the room used is the beat working. Beat 9 (F activity 9) · beat 11 (E) E F ⚑ New row. Deliberate: there is no rescue here that does not breach ruling 8 or guardrail 1. The only recovery available to a solo facilitator is to let it be optional and keep going, and this row says that rather than inventing a save.

Movement IV — running it, grace, the ripple, the Radar (beats 11-14)

# Situation Response Beat Product Flag
15 A manager asks participants to share their situations "We keep this private by design. Let's work with a fictional example instead." Do not negotiate. Beat 11 I E F —
16 Someone asks whether checking their phone means they failed "No. Choosing to check it can be a completely intentional Do. The rep is noticing there was a choice." Beat 11 I E F The phone is Hunter's own named example of a rep participants have already done (ruling 6).
17 A scenario resembles a live dispute in the room Stop, switch to the recorded fallback scenario, no discussion. Beat 11 I E F Depends on the S1-S6 bank and its avoid/switch triggers, 04-PACKET-OPERATIONS-SPEC-v1.md — listed in 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md as a recovery-owed device.
18 Pair or small-group work feels unsafe or unwanted once it has started Switch immediately to the solo fallback: the facilitator speaks it through, everyone runs the catch alone. Do not negotiate it in front of the room. Beat 11 E F Cannot arise in the Introduction — no pair work exists there (ruling 7).
19 The room is silent at the unaided retrieval Do not press, do not count, do not re-ask. Re-show and give the three-sentence correction. Silence is a permitted answer. Beat 14 I E F —
20 A manager or host proposes building a shared team version in the room "That's a separate piece of work with its own conversation, and this isn't the session to decide it." Return to the beat you were on. Beat 14 I E F ⛔ Ruling 65. The original row's label read "proposes building a Team Radar." "Team Radar" and "Manager Radar" are banned terms; the manager's construct is enabling conditions. The situation label is reworded; the spoken response never contained the phrase.
21 The moment gallery runs long Do not shorten it below its budgeted length. Take the time from the application studios' second half, not from the gallery — a rushed gallery produces no selected moment, and the beat that follows has nothing to work on. Beat 11 F, and E where time is made ⛔ Ruling 1. Original read "below twelve minutes." Minute removed. Gallery and studios reinstated by rulings 29c and 29d.
22 The room tires and the obvious next move looks like building something together Do not. Consent obtained late in a long session, in front of colleagues, in a room with momentum, is not consent. Foundations may say the team version exists. It may not start one. Beat 14 F Carried from 40-...-v3.md §7's preamble, not its table. Same ruling-65 terminology correction as row 20.
23 The facilitator's own reps in the room are being counted as evidence In-session reps are cued — facilitator-prompted and facilitator-timed. A Mental Rep is self-initiated and cannot happen in the room. In-session rep counts must never appear in external, funder or measurement material. Product-general I E F K-08. Carried from 35-...-v2.md's terminology block, which is the only place it is stated as a facilitator instruction rather than a design note.
32 The reflection rep surfaces something heavy — a participant goes quiet, tearful, or leaves the room Do not follow the questions with a fourth one, do not ask for hands, do not check on the person in front of the room. Close the beat exactly as written — "that was a reflection rep… both count" — and go to the break early if one is near. Be near the door, not at the front. If they come to you, row 1 governs. Beat 12 (Foundations activity 12) F ⛔ §1 and gap 2 both govern. A solo facilitator cannot leave the room with a participant — that was found physically impossible in the 2026-08-15 panel and was never replaced. This row does not pretend otherwise. It positions the facilitator where the person can reach him and stops there.
33 Someone says the reflection rep made them feel worse about the moment they picked "That's the part we put the breakpoint map before this for. Looking back and seeing you missed it isn't a failure — noticing afterwards is a reflection rep, and it counts." Say it to the room, not to the person. Never say it will feel different next time. Beat 12 F K-08, AG-001 — names what the rep is, promises nothing about how anyone will feel. Depends on the breakpoint pass having run first, which is a positional non-negotiable.
34 The Rep Plan's eight questions land on an exhausted room — visible drop-off, people stop tracking Slow down and cut, do not speed up. Say: "If you only hold three of these, hold these three — the moment, the catch, the cue." Then run those three at full pace with the pauses intact and drop the rest. Do not re-ask the room to concentrate and do not apologise for the length. Beat 14 (Foundations activity 14) F This is 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md's F5 compression taken deliberately rather than improvised — which is row 14's rule applied here. ⛔ Nothing written, nothing collected, nothing said, in the cut version as in the full one.
35 The rehearsal rep's third pass lands as futility — "so if the Do isn't available either, what was the point?" "That's the answer, not the problem. If the move isn't available, you still stopped and you still chose — that's a completed rep. The rep isn't the outcome, it's the catch." Then continue to the next pass or the close without discussion. Beat 14 (Foundations activity 15) F D-0107: a rep counts by attempt, not by outcome. This is the beat's own point, not a save — running it with options removed is the entire reason it runs three times.
36 The facilitator makes an error and the room catches it — a wrong number, a contradiction, a mis-said definition, the wrong slide Say it plainly and immediately, then keep going: "You're right, I got that wrong. [The correct version.] Thanks." Do not explain how it happened, do not apologise twice, do not offer to check and come back unless it is a number. If it is an external number and you cannot source it live, row 37 governs. Product-general, any beat I E F ⚑ New row, 2026-09-10 — closes gap 9, "the one failure certain to occur in a first cohort." Deliberate register: correction is a one-line move, because a facilitator visibly rattled by his own error costs the room more than the error did.
37 The room disputes an external statistic and it cannot be sourced in the moment "Fair question. I'm not going to defend a number I can't source standing here — I'll send the source with the follow-up." Drop the number for the rest of the session and teach the point without it. Then actually send it, or correct it, in the follow-up. Product-general, any beat I E F ⚑ New row. Ruling 45: every external number carries a registered source. This row also closes gap 5. It creates a real follow-up obligation on the facilitator — the recovery is not complete in the room.

⚑ Row 34 was briefly dead and is live again, 2026-09-10 (second pass). It was written the same day another fixer cut the Rep Plan block from 31-FOUNDATIONS-240-STRUCTURE.md — two edits to one object with neither reading the other (38-THE-RESCORE.md WORSE-5). The block has been restored to the room because the leave-behind it was moved to cannot carry it — ⚑ and the authority for that is one record, not three (corrected 2026-09-10): anti-ruling 115, which refuses printed prompts and is unscoped. D-0112 has no §4 (verified against the record: its sections are 1 and 2), the eight-panel limit is 05-LEAVE-BEHIND-PRINT-SPEC.md §1's own rule, and ruling 23's printed-prompts clause is scoped "in the hour" while Foundations is four hours. Row 34 applies as written. Do not delete it.

4 · Adjacent material — what was found and what was not

The brief asked specifically whether an escalation route, a serious-disclosure response, a nobody-speaks response, or a co-facilitator protocol went missing with these tables.

Thing Found? Where it actually is
A serious-disclosure response Yes — row 1, in all three v3 packs and both v1 packets, wording unchanged across every version. Recovered. But its escalation clause is ruled not-a-route (§1).
An escalation route Partly, and it is not cleared. 14-build-readiness-and-expert-lens-v1/04-escalation-and-distress-response-procedures-DRAFT.md. Four sections drafted; the scripted wording for pausing the room and for the private check-in is explicitly left open for a qualified clinical reviewer, and the crisis contact block is empty. D-0013 competency 10 remains unverifiable until it is closed.
A "what if nobody speaks" response Yes — rows 2 and 19. Recovered. Stronger than expected: silence is a permitted answer at every retrieval, and quiet recognition is sufficient at every recognition prompt.
A co-facilitator protocol No. It does not exist anywhere. Searched 15-current-service-definition-v1/, 12-evidence-first-rebuild/, 16-from-scratch-redesign-v1/, 14-build-readiness-and-expert-lens-v1/ and the advisor register. What exists is the cap — 20 solo, 30 only with a co-facilitator (AG-131, AG-160, ruling 8) — and one open question in the uncleared escalation draft asking whether a second person should be mandatory at every size. There is no division of labour, no handover line, no who-follows-the-person-out rule. This is the largest single gap in the set.

Also found, already live and not duplicated here: 03-MANAGER-SESSION-DESIGN.md §6a carries two manager-room recovery moves — a leader names an individual and a leader makes a speech about the organisation's commitment to wellbeing. They are in the manager product and stay there.

5 · Coverage gaps — listed, not filled

Each of these was a room failure with no scripted response anywhere in the recovered corpus. Three are now closed by rows written on 2026-09-10 and are marked CLOSED with the row that closed them. The rest stay open and are not invented into rows.

  1. No co-facilitator protocol at all (§4). A 30-person room is permitted only with a second person, and nothing says what that person does.
  2. Nobody can leave the room with the participant. The one recorded attempt at this — the "meet them at the door and hold them outside" line in 120-RETURN-SESSION-DESIGN.md §5.5 — was found in the 2026-08-15 panel to be physically impossible for one facilitator (Cole, Compass F8). It was never replaced. If someone walks out distressed mid-beat, the solo facilitator has no instruction.
  3. A manager naming a specific employee in a participant room. The manager session has the line ("Sarah's not here to agree with the description"); Essentials and Foundations have nothing, and a manager sits in those rooms too (ruling 27, ruling 72). Adopting it across is a ruling, not a recovery — it is Hunter's call, not this file's.
  4. A participant challenges the evidence base directly — "has this been shown to work?" There is no scripted answer, in any pack, to the single most likely hard question in a room of adults. MFC has delivered zero cohorts and K-08 binds the reply.
  5. ~~The room disputes a statistic.~~ CLOSED by row 37 (2026-09-10). Ruling 45 still binds: the row drops the number rather than defending it, and creates a real follow-up obligation.
  6. The Leadership Community sign-up is asked about and does not exist yet. Ruling 29b puts the sign-up in every service; D-0111 §3 still records the Community as not authorised for build. A participant asking "what is it?" has no answer written.
  7. Technology fails beyond the visual. Row 13 covers the slide. Nothing covers the QR code, the digital Introduction's platform, or the leave-behind not arriving.
  8. ~~A hostile or disengaged room~~ — CLOSED by row 26 (2026-09-10), with a stated limit: the row protects the participants' right to refuse and keeps the session running. It does not claim a solo facilitator can convert a hostile room, because he cannot.
  9. ~~The facilitator makes an error and the room catches it.~~ CLOSED by row 36 (2026-09-10).
  10. ⚠ NEW, found while writing row 24. Foundations activity 1 — the technique that did not work — currently runs at beat 2, BEFORE the safety door at beat 3. It asks every person in the room to bring to mind a past disappointment before anything has been said about what is private, what is optional and where to go if something lands hard. Row 24 recovers the moment either way. Whether the door moves in front of it, or the activity moves behind the door, is a ruling and it is Hunter's call — it is not this file's to make. Beat 3 is marked never cut and never lengthened, which is a further constraint on any fix.
  11. The private check-in itself. Rows 27 and 32 both stop at "be near the door and be available." What is actually said to a distressed participant one-to-one, and the threshold at which MFC does more than that, remain open items requiring qualified clinical input and are not written here. This is §1 restated at the two beats where it now bites hardest.

6 · What was checked, and what was not

Checked against 00-THE-RULINGS.md: ruling 1 (no minutes), 3 (four movements over fourteen beats), 6 (the room cannot perform a Do), 7 (keynote), 8 (nothing asked out loud, group cap), 17 (hands up for recognition, never disclosure), 29c/29d/29e (gallery, studios, shift tools), 46 and 47 (manager scope, the quiet employee), 65 (banned Radar terminology), and K-08 across every spoken line.

No row breaks ruling 6. Nothing in this file has the room perform a Do; row 16 concerns a rep a participant has already done in their own life, which is exactly Hunter's named example.

No row breaks ruling 8. Rows 2, 12 and 19 all defend the opposite — nothing is asked out loud about a person's own state, and silence is always a permitted answer.

No spoken line in this file makes an outcome claim. Row 4's "that's the rep" names an attempt, which is D-0107's locked definition — a rep counts by attempt, not by outcome. Row 23 is the K-08 guardrail itself.

Not checked: whether the rulings 46 and 47 manager lines need participant-room equivalents (gap 3 — a ruling, not a recovery). Not licensed: anything in §1 and gaps 2, 10 and 11. The escalation wording, the internal escalation threshold, the walk-out response, and whether the safety door moves in front of Foundations activity 1 are not agent decisions. The first three require a qualified clinical reviewer; the fourth is Hunter's. No number of agent passes supplies either.

Rows 24-37, added 2026-09-10, were checked line by line against the same set. No new row asks a person what they picked, calls on an individual, converts a private device into a shared one, reads a person's state aloud, or promises anything about how a participant will feel (K-08, AG-001). Rows 27, 31, 32 and 26 each stop short of a rescue that would breach one of those, and say so in place of pretending to a recovery. Independent check: not yet performed on the new rows.
