26 Recovered Foundations Devices

Two devices, recovered

Hunter, 2026-09-09, on being shown they were lost: "The moment gallery, we need to implement… this is the thing. Right? That should never have been lost. That should be… if we want to, we'll make time for it in the essentials, but it has to be in the foundations. We could do the application studio. Yes. And the foundations only."

Device Introduction Essentials Foundations
Moment gallery No If time allows — Hunter's words: "if we want to, we'll make time for it" ⛔ Mandatory
Application studios No No ⛔ Foundations only

⚑ This required amending 22-THE-PARTICIPANT-FOUNDATION.md's Rule 3, which as written forbade Foundations from containing anything absent from the 58-minute keynote — and therefore forbade both of these. Rule 3 now reads argued, not taught. Depth and practice are what widen.

1 · The moment gallery

Specific, ordinary moments posted around the room under five arenas — self, relationships, work, performance, transitions. Participants walk the room and privately note three that connect to them. Thirteen minutes in the v3 Foundations budget.

⛔ No disclosure. No group formation. Nobody says which arena they stood in longest.

Why a gallery and not a discussion — the sharpest rationale in the corpus:

Asked cold to "think of a moment in your life," most people produce either something enormous or nothing at all. A wall of ordinary pre-written moments makes the ordinary ones visible and gives permission for the small.

Choosing a life category out loud is exposing, group sizes come out uneven, and the domains overlap anyway.

The skill-referenced selection instruction, spoken before the room stands up, about 45 seconds:

"As you read, don't just pick three you recognise. Pick them for different reasons. Find one where the hard part is noticing it's even happening — it goes past you every time. Find one where the hard part is choosing — you notice fine, you just do the other thing anyway. And find one where the hard part is shifting — you notice, you know what you'd rather do, and you can't get from one to the other. Three moments, three different hard parts. Still easy ones."

This is what gives the five skills a consumer. Without it they are named, practised twice, and never used again by the beat that decides what the participant actually leaves with. Foundations runs the three-skill version; Essentials would run two (Notice and Choose). Focus and Connect are deliberately not named here — Focus is trained elsewhere and Connect is practised in no product, and naming a skill the room has never run produces a list, not a filter.

⛔ The accessibility equivalent must be offered aloud before anyone stands up. It is a Gate 0.1 requirement, and the original pack failed it:

"Note them if you want to, or just hold them in your head — either works, and nobody will look at your paper. You can also stay where you are and read from where you're sitting."

A seated route is required as well as a silent one — "walk the room" is itself a mobility assumption.

⛔ Curation, not authorship. No facilitator, session or preparation step may write a new moment for the wall (14-moment-examples-bank.md standing no-invention rule). The bank holds 18 verified entries and none is a workplace-manager moment — the corpus for the wall is unresolved and is a real build dependency, not a detail.

2 · Application studios — Foundations only

The room splits by kind of application, never by life domain: managing myself in a moment versus responding to another person. Twelve minutes.

Three reasons for this split and not a domain split: 1. Nobody learns anything about your life from which studio you picked. 2. It reliably produces two roughly even groups. 3. It maps a real difference — a moment involving another person has a second party's response in it, which changes what Shift and Do can be.

A domain split (sport / family / work) is exposing and produces uneven groups.

⛔ With one facilitator, both run as structured self-guided studios — after the facilitator demonstrates one complete worked example at the front. This is non-negotiable: a self-guided studio with no worked model produces vague reflection, which this service explicitly excludes.

Each guide walks the participant through their own selected moment: where the catch is, what Shift options exist, what the Do could be, and what changes if the first option is gone.

This is the only small-group device MFC has ever designed that satisfies AG-134 (Eimear Quigley: the workshop must be experiential, small-group practice feeding back to the whole group) without exposing any individual. That is why losing it mattered.

Still orphaned, not recovered here

The same sweep found more, and Hunter has not ruled on these:

  • The two facilitator recovery tables — ~23 scripted rows for a room going wrong ("My mind wandered the whole time → That's the rep."). The single largest lost body of material, and what lets one person run a room alone. Recommended as the next recovery.
  • The Rep Plan's eight fields, including "If I miss it" — "a plan written before the person has experienced a rep failing is a plan for a person who doesn't exist yet." ⚠ Was gated pending a Hunter decision in the original pack.
  • Context-neutral framing — an approved decision with a verbatim spoken passage, zero occurrences in the current build.
  • The anti-hero guardrail — "These are places to understand a situation, not grades of a person."

28 Has This Been Shown To Work

"Has this been shown to work?"

The likeliest hard question in any room of adults, and MFC had no scripted answer to it. Found by the facilitator recovery sweep, 2026-09-09, absent from every facilitator pack MFC has ever written. A participant asks it with four minutes left; a buyer asks it in writing. Same answer, three lengths.

The position underneath all of it. MFC has zero delivered cohorts and no outcome evidence of any kind. The mechanism it is built on — repeated practice against a real cue, which may make useful patterns more familiar and easier to reach (P9) — draws on established work in adjacent literatures (P5). MFC's own programme has not been shown to produce it. Those are two different claims and the entire answer is built on keeping them apart (K-09; P21).

1 · The spoken answer

1a · Ten seconds — a participant, hand up, four minutes left

Not yet. We haven't measured a group through this. What's underneath it is well tested; the hour on top of it isn't. We'll publish when we know.

P19 + P21 + P20, compressed. Use this in the room unless the person wants more.

1b · Forty seconds — the standing version

Four beats. Learn the shape, not the words.

[1 — answer the question first] Not yet. We haven't delivered a measured cohort. We have no results to show you and we're not going to invent any.

[2 — what has been shown] What has been shown is the thing underneath it. Our approach draws together established psychological science — attention, state regulation, values-based action — into a practical, teachable model. Practising a skill against a real cue, in the moment you'd actually use it. That isn't ours and it isn't new. What we've done is build an hour on top of it.

[3 — the line that must not be softened] So what the research validates is the mechanisms we've built on. That's a different claim, and you should hold us to the difference.

[4 — turn it into the ask] Proof comes from measurement across cohorts, or it doesn't come at all — and we'll publish either way.

Beat Traces to
1 P19 (AG-001; said once, AG-028 — as the invitation, not the apology)
2 P5 (verbatim spine, K-08 "may safely say") + P3 + ruling 39, which is conceded first and unprompted rather than defended
3 P21. 13-...-value-proposition marks this sentence as one that must not be softened. Any drift to "backed by research" or "evidence-based programme" breaks K-08.
4 P20

Why beat 2 carries the room. It is the only beat that gives a sceptic something to hold, and conceding that the loop isn't novel before anyone extracts it is what makes beats 3 and 4 land as confidence rather than hedging.

Register. Beat 1 is flat and fast — it is not an apology and must not be delivered as one ("I don't want us to shoot ourselves in the foot… be precise, be powerful."). Same register as beat 10 of 03-DELIVERY-SCRIPT-INTRODUCTION-60.md: "It's an hour, and I think it lands. That doesn't guarantee it leads to behaviour change, and it can't."

1c · ⛔ The fifth beat that is NOT usable today — naming the mechanism literature

There is a tempting extra beat naming if-then planning. Do not use it yet.

The registered source (Sheeran, Listrom & Gollwitzer 2024, 642 tests, 10-sources/2026-09-03-sheeran-listrom-gollwitzer-2024-...md) permits exactly one public sentence — "Choosing a few specific moments ahead of time draws on decades of research on if-then planning" — and only once the record is confirmed. It is status: draft, approval_status: awaiting-specialist, confirmed_by: "". Registered (ruling 45) and confirmed are different gates.

⛔ And the record states the evidence is for implementation intentions in goal pursuit and is untested for "notice a moment and do a mental rep." So "that's the family we're in" is barred outright, now and after confirmation. ⛔ No effect size, percentage or "X times more likely" on any public surface until a full-text read — the record is abstract-level, secondary-sourced, and carries an unverified flag of substantial publication bias.

Status: UNSUPPORTED, not usable. Unblocking it is head-of-research work: confirm the record.

2 · The buyer one-liner

"We can't show you outcomes — we have no delivered cohorts, and we won't invent any. What we can show you is the research behind the mechanism, and measurement designed in from the first session rather than bolted on."

P19 + P21 + P22. One sentence, two clauses, ends on what the buyer gets.

3 · The follow-ups

3.1 · "So you're saying it might not work?"

[H] It can, not will. There are skills that can, not will, improve how you navigate life's moments — and I'd rather say that than the other thing.

Where it genuinely doesn't reach: a skill doesn't replace a bad environment. If the conditions are against you, this is not the answer to that.

What we're aiming at is that more ordinary moments have more than one option in them. That's the target.

P30 (the "can, not will" construction is Hunter's own — preserve it exactly) · P14 · P7.

⚑ One boundary, not five. P14 is the falsifiable one and it is what buys the credibility; P4 (capacity is not perfection) belongs in the room during the talk, not stacked here. AG-028, and AG-003/AG-233 — Eimear has twice found MFC over-reading caution. Over-hedging is a defect, not diligence (L-084). ⛔ Do not add "it's not a magic trick", "it is not a promise", or any sentence asserting your own trustworthiness — beat 3 already does that work without saying so, and defending against an accusation nobody made is the tell of a weak position.

⚠ If the person presses, the correct move is a diagnostic question, not reassurance: where did it break — did you catch it, did you have something to shift with, did you know what to do instead? (13-...-claim-limits Layer 2.)

3.2 · "What evidence do you have?"

[H] Two kinds, and they're not the same kind, so let me separate them.

There's the research behind the mechanisms — memory and retrieval, habit formation, planning, emotion regulation. We're evidence-informed and evidence-aligned, and those are the two words I'll use. We hold a working library of it, and we'll show you any of it.

Then there's evidence that our programme does what we say. We have none of that. Zero cohorts. And it's the only kind that could settle it.

So: measurement across cohorts, and we publish either way.

P6 (evidence-informed and evidence-aligned — these two words and no stronger ones) · P21 · P19 · P20 · K-09's four evidence roles in plain language.

⚑ "A working library, and we'll show you any of it" is the founder's own form and deliberately carries no number. ⛔ Do not say a count out loud. (For the record: 10-sources/ holds 138 records as of 2026-09-09, up from the 118 verified 2026-08-09 — which is why a spoken figure goes stale and gets a facilitator caught.)

Named registered mechanism sources if asked: Tulving & Pearlstone 1966; Sheppes et al. 2011; Roediger & Karpicke 2006; Lally et al. 2010; Burgler et al. 2026; Sheeran, Listrom & Gollwitzer 2024. ⚠ All are draft/awaiting-specialist. Say "registered in our source library", never "established findings" about any one of them, and ⛔ never describe any of them as proving an MFC component (K-09, representative-source role).

3.3 · Buyer: "How will I know it worked?"

[H] You'll get a written report, and I'll tell you now exactly what it can and can't tell you.

We measure comprehension before and after the session, and attempted reps at three weeks. That tells you whether it landed and whether people are reaching for it. It does not tell you behaviour changed over months. Nobody can tell you that from a workshop, and we won't.

You get a report whatever the number responds — what changes is what it can carry. With ten or more, numbers. Below that, at the moment, a report about the session and the design rather than about the people, and I'll tell you that up front. Never anything attributable to a person, and never broken down by team, shift, site or role.

Measurement is designed in from the first session rather than bolted on.

P23 · P24 · P22 · ⚑ D-0132 (2026-09-09, Hunter, canonical: true).

⚠ P25 is now partly stale and this page does not rely on it. D-0132 retired the report-suppression floor: "There is no report-suppression floor. Every cohort that buys a measured product receives a written report." It supersedes D-0121's sub-five clause and P25's final sentence. P25 still needs updating at source in 11-PERMITTED-CLAIMS.md — head-of-research work, flagged not done. ⛔ The five-to-nine "kinds of moment" tier is NOT YET IN FORCE (gated on Debra Fidler and Eimear Quigley, 06 §3.0.8) — which is why the spoken line above says "below ten, a report about the session" and does not offer kinds of moment at four respondents.

⚑ Product-scoping, not optional (D-0120, D-0121): - Introduction — pre/post only. No three-week measure and no Form C. Drop that clause. - Essentials / Small Team Essentials / Foundations — the paragraph above applies in full. - The manager session is deliberately not measured (P35). Say so and say why: what each manager writes is private, on their own phone, and collecting it would produce the version that sounds good.

⚠ Unresolved and surfaced rather than reconciled (CLAUDE.md §4): P24 calls the Introduction artefact "a delivery and comprehension record, not a report", while D-0121 §2 rules "A written report goes to every product — Introduction, Small Team Essentials, Essentials and Foundations." These may reconcile, since P24 was rewritten under D-0121, but a facilitator holding both can be caught. Until it is settled, describe the Introduction artefact by what it contains — recognition before and after a 60-minute session — rather than by either label.

3.4 · "So we'd be your first?" / "Are we paying to be your test case?"

The hardest question in the set, and the direct consequence of beat 1.

[H] Among the first, yes. I'm not going to dress that up. What you're buying is the workshop — the design, the hour, the return session, the manager session, the report. All of that is built and priced on the work in it, not on a discount for being early.

What you'd also be is one of the places this gets measured properly, which is the part I actually want. Proof comes from measurement across cohorts, or it doesn't come at all — and we'll publish either way.

P20 · P32 (the return session, report and manager session are inside the price, not extensions).

⛔ Do not offer a discount, a pilot rate or a "founding cohort" price. D-0122 §4 settled this: solving for a discount that holds per head at the benchmark "comes out at zero on both products." The commercial route around zero evidence is not price — it is the measurement design, which is what §3.3 sells. ⛔ And do not say "you'd be helping us" — that inverts who is buying what.

3.5 · "Can I speak to someone who's done it?" / "How many have you run?"

[H] Not yet — there's nobody to put you in front of, and I'd rather say that than find you someone who once came to a talk. When there are cohorts, you'll get the report, not a testimonial.

P19 · P20. ⚑ This is why the anecdote ban in §4 does not leave the facilitator empty: the replacement for a reference is the report, and it is a better artefact. There is also a principled reason, worth giving if the buyer is technical: individual testimony can never be MFC's proof, because the model is structured so no single individual outcome could disconfirm it (13-...-claim-limits). Aggregate measurement is the only thing that can.

3.6 · "Can you send me the evidence in writing?"

[H] Yes. I'll send what we hold and what it does and doesn't cover.

⚠ AG-018 (Gina, HARD) requires the evidence summary to be published for consumers. ⛔ Do not send a source record or an internal file. Until a published summary exists, send only what is already cleared for external use and say so. This is a real gap: there is no buyer-facing evidence one-pager, and this answer is writing a cheque nothing currently cashes.

3.7 · The don't-know exit — sanctioned, use it

[H] I don't want to guess at that. Let me come back to you in writing.

⚑ This exists because a prohibition list with no exit fails live. The pressure that produces every banned sentence in §4 is a facilitator with no permitted answer. This is the permitted answer. Using it costs nothing; guessing costs the room.

4 · ⛔ Never say, in answer to this question

⛔ Never Say instead Why
"We've had great feedback" / "people say it changed things for them" / any anecdote from a run, a talk or a conversation. P19, then beat 2, then §3.5 An outcome claim with no cohort behind it (AG-001). Reaching for a story here is the single most damaging available move.
"The research shows this works." P21 Collapses the two claims the whole answer exists to separate.
"Evidence-based" / "backed by research" / "proven" / "validated" / "clinically approved." P6 Strengthens evidence-informed into validation MFC does not have. Zero cohorts, and K-08's red lines are themselves unapproved.
"Content without an environment doesn't survive contact with real life." P15 ⛔ A causal claim no source supports. Named in CLAUDE.md §2 specifically. Fleming 2024 is cross-sectional. See §6 — still live in a founder-voice file.
"The evidence disconfirms individual training" / "resilience training makes people worse." P15 Same. Breaches K-08.
"Anyone who tells you their hour changes behaviour is making it up." P19, P20 The most tempting sentence in this whole script, and it is a comparative effectiveness claim from an organisation with zero cohorts. P37 permits comparative evidence talk only when specific, non-selective, and carrying MFC's own limit in the same sentence. A general swipe at a category is not that.
"We've done 120,000 mental reps." P19 Ruling 48. That figure is participation in a 2025 campaign — never evidence of practice or behaviour change, and in answer to this question it reads as exactly that.
Any statistic not registered in 10-sources/ — one in five, nine in ten, $X billion in lost productivity. Or a registered one whose record is unconfirmed. Nothing AG-001, D-0130, ruling 45. Gina's paired warning about AI-sourced statistics that do not survive checking. P27's target-and-cite formula is not usable today — no comparable study is registered.
"It'll show up in engagement / turnover / absenteeism" — including softened to "helps with." P7 D-0104. "Helps with" is the assertion wearing a coat.
"You will catch more moments" / "your people will…" P8, P30 Can, not will. The most common way a permitted sentence gets strengthened live.
"It's designed by a clinical psychologist." P1, P28 Eimear advises; she did not design the product.
"We've seen people's wellbeing improve when they use it." P29, P7 ⛔ AG-008, HARD: any association between skill enactment and wellbeing is correlation only and must never be reported as MFC causing the change. This still applies once cohort data exists — it is not a placeholder for the zero-evidence period.
Repeating the limit three or four times across one answer. Say it once AG-028; AG-003/AG-233. Over-hedging is a defect, not caution (L-084). Beat 1 carries it; beats 2–4 must not re-carry it.

5 · Is the honest answer commercially weak? — the plain verdict

In a written procurement comparison, yes, demonstrably. In a room, the reasoning says no — but that half is a hypothesis, not a finding, and this page cannot evidence it.

  • In a tender or a side-by-side against a vendor willing to overclaim, MFC loses, and no drafting fixes it. A buyer scoring "evidence of outcomes" on a rubric marks MFC zero, correctly. That is a real, permanent-until-cohorts commercial cost of AG-001, and MFC should carry it knowingly rather than discover it in a lost bid.
  • In front of adults, the reasoning is that a checkable concession beats an unfalsifiable claim, and that conceding ruling 39 unprompted converts the weakest moment into the most credible one. ⚠ That is a judgement this page cannot support. Zero cohorts means this script has never met an actual sceptic. The first deliveries settle it.
  • The only real mitigation is a delivered measured cohort. ⛔ Filling P27 would not fix the procurement problem — target-and-cite produces a cited target, not outcome evidence, and scores zero on the same rubric. It is a partial improvement, not the answer, and it is currently blocked anyway.
  • Price is not the route either. D-0122 §4 found a defensible early-adopter discount comes out at zero on both products. What MFC has to sell against zero evidence is the measurement design itself (§3.3) — which is genuinely unusual and is the strongest commercial asset in this whole answer.
  • AG-292 is only half answered. Gina's point is that a buyer who cannot see the potential benefit will not buy. §3.3 gives a concrete deliverable and P7 gives the target. Neither is a benefit statement. Whether that is enough is Gina's call, not this page's.

6 · What I could not license

  1. Not compliance clearance. K-08's red lines are themselves unapproved (BD-01 to BD-08 pending). Eimear has not seen this script. Neither has Gina.
  2. ⚑ Live conflict, found while drafting. 90-meta/agent-context-v1/13-founder-voice-v2-value-proposition.md line 108, inside its worked funder script, reads: "The evidence is clear that content without an environment does not survive contact with real life." That exact sentence is prohibited by CLAUDE.md §2 and 11-PERMITTED-CLAIMS.md §2. ⚠ Do not confuse it with line 82 — "We tried that ourselves and found what everyone finds: it does not survive contact with real life" — which is about a fifteen-minutes-a-day habit, is not the prohibited claim, and must not be struck. A facilitator reading that file for register will pick line 108 up. Marking it at source is head-of-framework / head-of-research work, not this page's to overwrite.
  3. P25 is stale against D-0132 and P27 is empty. Both need fixing in 11-PERMITTED-CLAIMS.md. This page routes around them rather than quietly restating them.
  4. There is no buyer-facing evidence summary, so §3.6 promises something that does not exist in cleared form. AG-018 requires one. Named, not solved.
  5. Never tested in a room. The traces are checkable; the delivery is not yet evidenced.

7 · The independent pass — what it changed

One adversarial check, 2026-09-09. Ten defects, nine applied. The material ones: the draft stated the ungated five-to-nine reporting tier as live to a buyer and had missed D-0132, decided the same day; the fifth beat used an unconfirmed source record in a form that record explicitly forbids; the header and beat 2 both strengthened P9/P5 into claims MFC cannot make; and §3.1 carried the limit five times inside one hundred words, in a document whose own §4 bans exactly that. Four missing follow-ups (§3.4–3.7) and the ten-second participant form (§1a) were also added.

One recommendation rejected on evidence. The check proposed offering a founding/case-study cohort at a discount as the commercial route around zero evidence. D-0122 §4 settles that a defensible discount comes out at zero on both products. Recorded in §5 as ruled out, not omitted.

00 Current Workshop Service Definition 2026 08 29

⚠ This navigation file is superseded. Do not use it to find the current definition.

It carried status: current_internal_definition — the strongest claim in this folder — while pointing at service packs two generations old. It was the first file anyone opened, and it was sending them to the wrong place.

The current definition is 37-WORKSHOP-NARRATIVE-SPINE-v2.md and the v3 packs 38/39/40 in this folder, as improved and merged on 2026-09-01 (commit 6bdc74a). 42-ARC-AT-A-GLANCE-v1.md is the delivery-readable view of it.

A from-scratch redesign exists and is a candidate, not the definition: 16-from-scratch-redesign-v1/02-MERGED-DESIGN-ALL-THREE-PRODUCTS.md. It becomes the definition only when Hunter approves it, at which point this folder's packs get marked superseded in turn. Until then they remain live, because retiring a current definition in favour of an unapproved candidate would leave MFC with no definition at all.

Everything below is retained as the 29 August record. It is history, not status.

For the current measurement decision, read 27-MEASUREMENT-FOUNDER-REVIEW-v3.md first. It is the separate 8-minute interface for approving, amending or pausing the measured-service baseline.

Status in one sentence

The current internal definitions are the controlled service packs for Introduction, Essentials and Foundations, with their facilitator packets and the shared Operations specification; the former HTML decks and package are legacy source material and must not define a workshop without a deliberate rebuild to the current packs.

What is current

Service Current definition Product boundary
60-minute Introduction 01-INTRODUCTION-FINAL-SERVICE-PACK-v1.md + 05-INTRODUCTION-FACILITATOR-PACKET-v1.md + 04-PACKET-OPERATIONS-SPEC-v1.md Broad public first encounter. No required material, writing, QR, data or follow-up.
90-minute Essentials 02-ESSENTIALS-FINAL-SERVICE-PACK-v1.md + 06-ESSENTIALS-FACILITATOR-PACKET-v1.md + 04-PACKET-OPERATIONS-SPEC-v1.md Team-context workshop: tailored examples and deeper guided practice; no inflated culture/change claim.

For every workshop question, open this folder first. A live deck, facilitator guide or participant material is current only if it is explicitly reconciled to this three-part definition.

What the 90/100 means

Each service core scores 90/100 for internal artefact quality only. The separate measurement-forms candidate is not given a product-effectiveness score: it is a reviewer-ready proposed evaluation system, not a fielded service or an evidence-of-effectiveness claim. The score assesses what can be made and checked now: definition, sequence, learning jobs, transfer design, measurement logic, accessibility/claim safeguards and evidence traceability. It does not claim participant effectiveness, real-world use, delivery readiness, clinical/legal/privacy clearance, partner readiness or founder approval.

The score is deliberately capped at 90 until new internal work is done: independent challenge of material uncertainty, terminology, retrieval/bridge alternatives, whole-journey access/adverse effects, and blind source/alternative review. Those are product-improvement tasks, not later external testing gates.

01 Introduction Final Service Pack V1

MFC final service pack — Introduction v1

Product: 60-minute broad adult public first encounter
Core boundary: no required participant material, writing, QR, data, follow-up or real-world-use claim.
Normative exact-content companions: facilitator packet v1 and Operations spec v1. Score v6 is audit evidence only.

Final slide-by-slide sequence

Slide Time Participant experience Exact learning job Facilitator instruction
1 0–2 arrive/observe permission “You can join in, think privately, use a fictional example or listen.”
2 2–5 understand scope non-clinical/no-blame boundary Name support, safety and context; no disclosure invitation.
3 5–8 recognise ordinary moment 1 Fictional message reaction.
4 8–12 recognise ordinary moment 2 Fictional conversation/scrolling alternative; quiet recognition only.
5 12–16 reframe difficulty is learned/contextual, not a defect State that access varies with capacity, safety, time and relationships.
6 16–20 distinguish mental health / mental fitness boundary No diagnosis or outcome claim.
7 20–23 understand Stop Notice the moment; not “calm down.”
8 23–27 understand Shift Available space/perspective; optional, including support/distance.
9 27–31 understand Do + worked message Use the packet’s fictional upsetting-message example; outcome does not decide whether it counts.
10 31–41 guided recall distinguish process/context/action Fixed prompt: “You are about to walk into a conversation you are already dreading. You notice your body tightening and your mind rushing ahead.” Prompt Stop, then Shift, then Do; gentle correction only.
11 41–52 guided rehearsal safe fictional application Use S5; switch to S1 if trigger applies; call it guided rehearsal, never a Mental Rep.
12 52–57 future bridge no obligation A moment may arise or not; support/delay/non-action remain valid.
13 57–60 unaided retrieval/close recall core language Hide visual; five silent seconds; reveal/correct only afterwards.

Participant-facing non-negotiables

  • No participant writes, identifies themselves, shares a personal moment or completes a form.
  • S5 is the default rehearsal; S1 is the explicit safe switch.
  • The session ends in the room. Nothing needs downloading, taking home or reporting.

Final product claim

“A one-hour, human first encounter that gives people a simple language for noticing an everyday moment and choosing what to do next when it is useful.”

Not: treatment, a wellbeing intervention, proof of use, a team/culture programme, or a follow-up service.

04 Packet Operations Spec V1

MFC packet operations specification v1

Retrieval protocols

Product/beat Protocol
Introduction 31–41 This is guided recall/discrimination, not unaided retrieval: facilitator prompts each process word and corrects collectively.
Introduction 57–60 Before asking, hide/turn the Stop–Shift–Do visual. Say: “Take five quiet seconds. You may think privately, pass, or answer when ready: what are the three words?” After responses, re-show and state the correction: “Stop notices; Shift creates space or perspective when available; Do is an intentional next move.” Do not count responses.
Essentials 86–90 Hide/turn visual and allow five silent seconds before collective answer. Re-show only after a pass/answer opportunity. Correct with the same three-sentence wording above.
Foundations 45–55 No card/visual visible. Five quiet seconds, then private recall or pass. Only then show a neutral fictional card and ask for process application. The first part is unaided retrieval; card use is guided rehearsal.
Foundations 210–230 No visual/card visible. Present only the opening line of a scenario, allow silent retrieval of the process, then reveal constraint text and work through discrimination. This is a second, context-distal unaided retrieval followed by guided discrimination.

Host preparation and accessibility record

Complete for every delivery candidate, without collecting participant health information: agenda available in advance; read-aloud/visual alternative; large-print/plain-text availability; language/interpreter requirement and competent provider; seating/quiet/pass route; sensory/movement needs; device-free delivery; mixed-seniority/pair-work caution; and named facilitator switch route. “No materials” means no required participant worksheet, device, writing or data burden; optional accessibility aids are permitted.

Scenario selection record

For Essentials choose 2 IDs; for Foundations choose 3 IDs and one fallback. For Introduction use S5 unless its avoid/switch trigger is present, then use S1. Record: setting, chosen IDs, avoided IDs/reason, alternative scenario, live-conflict/grievance switch trigger, and whether paired work is suitable. If a scenario resembles a live dispute, stop and switch to the fallback without discussion.

ID Plain-text scenario Read-aloud equivalent Avoid/switch trigger
S1 Message Stage 1: “A message changes a task you thought was settled.” Stage 2: “You are tired, unsure what it means, and feel the urge to reply immediately.” Read each stage exactly when revealed. identifiable recent message/incident
S2 Tension Stage 1: “A comment is misunderstood in a conversation.” Stage 2: “The conversation becomes tense and other people are present.” Read each stage exactly when revealed. live team conflict
S3 Capacity Stage 1: “A task is added when capacity is already stretched.” Stage 2: “The work cannot all be completed in the available time.” Read each stage exactly when revealed. prompts disclosure of workload dispute
S4 Speaking up Stage 1: “A practical concern needs raising.” Stage 2: “The usual meeting is cancelled and there is a power difference.” Read each stage exactly when revealed. active grievance/disciplinary matter
S5 Public moment Stage 1: “In a public place, someone reacts sharply.” Stage 2: “You notice tension and are unsure whether engaging is safe.” Read each stage exactly when revealed. threat/violence or culturally loaded incident
S6 Household Stage 1: “A household conversation is tense.” Stage 2: “Everyone is tired and the situation does not feel ready to resolve.” Read each stage exactly when revealed. domestic safety concern

All cards are delivered as the text above, on screen/large print/read aloud as needed. No hidden card asset is required.

Foundations default deterministic selection record

For the frozen v1 core packet: F06 (85–100) = S2, F07 (100–115) = S3, F10 (185–210) = S4 with Stage 1 then Stage 2 reveal, fallback S1. A named-host tailoring record may replace these IDs only if it writes the same ordered mapping and fallback before the session; it may not alter the mechanism or switch rule.

05 Introduction Facilitator Packet V1

MFC Introduction — 60-minute facilitator packet v1

Status: internal product candidate; standard service, no materials and no routine participant data
Audience: broad adult public audience; adapt examples, not the core mechanism
Product job: a human first encounter that makes MFC’s category and simple process recognisable, memorable and worth voluntarily trying later.

Required companion: use MFC-PACKET-OPERATIONS-SPEC-v1.md for the 57–60 hidden-visual retrieval protocol, accessibility/host preparation, and the Introduction scenario switch rule. “No materials” means no required participant worksheet, writing, device or routine data—not no optional accessibility aid.

Non-negotiables

  • No forms, worksheets, QR codes, mandatory phone tasks, personal cards, attendee identifiers or expected follow-up.
  • People may pass, observe or use a fictional example. Do not invite public disclosure.
  • A guided activity is called guided rehearsal. A Mental Rep occurs only in a naturally occurring real-world moment and is not claimed here.
  • Do not diagnose, promise wellbeing change, suggest another practice is inadequate, or frame a constraint as someone’s failure.

Materials and room set-up

Facilitator, a visible three-word slide or board (Stop – Shift – Do), timer and optional accessible verbal description of the slide. The product must work if the visual aid fails.

0:00–0:05 — welcome and permission

Say:

Thanks for being here. This is a conversation about the ordinary moments where life asks something of us—at home, at work, in our heads, or with other people. You never need to share a personal story here. You can join in, think quietly, use an invented example, or simply listen.

This is not therapy, diagnosis, or a claim that every difficult situation can be solved by an individual response. Some situations need support, time, safety, or change around us. Today is about having one small process available in moments where it is useful.

Facilitator check: pace slowly; do not ask “who is struggling?”

0:05–0:12 — recognise the kind of moment

Say:

Think of a small, recognisable moment: you see a message and feel a reaction before you reply; you notice you have been scrolling longer than you meant to; someone says something in a conversation and you can feel yourself closing off. Nothing dramatic needs to be happening for a moment to matter.

You do not need to tell anyone which example fits. Just notice whether you recognise the kind of moment.

Optional room interaction: “A nod or a quiet hand-up if this kind of thing sounds familiar.” Do not count or record responses.

Recovery route: if the room is silent, say: “You do not need to respond—quiet recognition is enough.” Continue.

0:12–0:20 — reframe without blame

Say:

We are often expected to handle these moments as though we should already know how. But people learn ways of responding through guidance, observation, experience and practice—and what is available to us changes with stress, safety, time, relationships and the situation itself.

Mental health is about how we are doing. Mental fitness is about what we are able to do in life’s everyday moments. They connect, but they are not the same thing. Needing more options or practice is not evidence that someone is broken.

Do not say: “Nobody taught us this,” “everyone can learn this,” or anything that implies equal control/capacity.

0:20–0:31 — teach Stop–Shift–Do

Display or say the three words one at a time.

Say:

MFC uses a simple process: Stop – Shift – Do.

Stop is the chance to notice that a moment is happening. It might be before, during, or after it. It does not mean freezing, being calm, or getting it right.

Shift is anything that gives you a little more space or perspective when one is available: a breath, a pause, a different question, stepping away, talking to someone, or deciding this is not a moment to handle alone. It is an option, not a rule.

Do is choosing a next move with intention—something that fits what matters in that moment. It may be speaking, waiting, asking for help, leaving, coming back later, or doing nothing for now.

The result does not decide whether the attempt counted. You can make an intentional next move and still have a difficult outcome.

Worked fictional example:

You receive a message that lands badly and your first impulse is to reply immediately. Stop: you notice the pull to react. Shift: perhaps you put the phone down, read it again later, or ask what you need before replying. Do: you choose whether to respond now, wait, ask a question, or speak to someone. The best move depends on the situation; the point is having a moment to choose.

0:31–0:41 — collective retrieval and discrimination

Scenario: “You are about to walk into a conversation you are already dreading. You notice your body tightening and your mind rushing ahead.”

Ask, one at a time:

  1. “What is the first word in the process?” Pause five seconds. Confirm: “Stop—notice the moment.”
  2. “What might Shift mean here?” Accept several answers; add: “It could also be recognising that you need support or that now is not the right time.”
  3. “What could Do look like?” Accept multiple safe, context-sensitive examples.

Correct gently: if someone says “calm down” as the only answer, say: “Calm might be welcome, but it is not the requirement. The process is about having an intentional next move available.”

0:41–0:52 — shared guided rehearsal

Set-up:

We will do one rehearsal together. It is not a test and you do not need to use a personal example. Think privately, use this situation, or simply listen.

Scenario: use S5 Stage 1 then Stage 2 from the Operations specification. If that public-moment scenario could resemble a recent threat, violence or culturally loaded incident, switch to S1 Message, keep it fictional, and use the same rehearsal sequence.

Guide slowly:

  1. “Where might you notice the moment? That is Stop.” Pause.
  2. “What are a few different ways someone might create a little space, if it is safe and available? That is Shift.” Invite two or three possibilities, including “move away” or “do nothing for now.”
  3. “What could an intentional next move be? That is Do.” Invite alternatives; affirm that safety, leaving, asking for support or not engaging can all be appropriate.

Close the rehearsal:

That was a guided rehearsal in a shared scenario. It is not a Mental Rep. A Mental Rep is when a real moment occurs in your life and you catch it and choose what you do next with intention.

0:52–0:57 — future bridge with no obligation

Say:

If a moment that matters shows up after today, you might notice it and see whether Stop, Shift or Do gives you one more option. If no moment shows up, if the process does not come to mind, or if the situation calls for support rather than action, that is information—not a failure.

You do not need to make a promise, choose a target or report anything back. The point is simply that this language is now available if it is useful.

0:57–1:00 — unaided recap and close

Ask: “Without looking, what are the three words?” Allow the room to answer collectively.

Say:

Stop—notice the moment. Shift—create some space or perspective if it is available. Do—choose an intentional next move. Mental fitness is not about controlling every outcome. It is about having more chance to notice and choose in the everyday moments that matter.

Thank you for thinking with us.

Facilitator recovery rules

If this happens Do this
A participant discloses distress or an unsafe situation Thank them briefly; do not invite detail or group advice. Acknowledge that safety/support may be the next appropriate step; follow the host’s approved support process if one exists.
Someone challenges the distinction from mindfulness/therapy Agree that many practices can support in-the-moment awareness; state that this session offers one simple language/process and is not competing with care or other practices.
Discussion runs long Protect the rehearsal and close. Shorten examples before removing the core retrieval/rehearsal beats.
The visual fails Teach verbally; ask for the three words again at close.

Internal build checklist

  • [x] timed 60-minute flow
  • [x] exact facilitator language
  • [x] no-material/no-data boundary
  • [x] fictional/shared scenarios and pass route
  • [x] outcome-independent, T2/T4-correct language
  • [x] recovery rules
  • [ ] alternative scenario bank
  • [ ] accessibility/plain-language internal audit
  • [ ] independent internal critique and rescore

06 Essentials Facilitator Packet V1

MFC Essentials — 90-minute facilitator packet v1

Status: internal product candidate; team-context learning service
Core boundary: no participant data, return contact or manager component is required for this 90-minute product. Those are separate optional modules.
Product job: contextual, private, practical learning—not a team-culture intervention.

Required companion: use MFC-PACKET-OPERATIONS-SPEC-v1.md for host/access preparation, S1–S6 scenario selection and the 86–90 verbal-or-hidden-visual retrieval protocol. Its S-ID scenario text is the sole canonical scenario source.

Before the session — tailoring record

Record only: setting/sector, common non-sensitive work rhythms, accessibility and language needs, words/examples to avoid, power/seniority mix, and two fictional scenarios relevant to the setting. Do not ask a host to identify individual problems or collect health information.

Facilitator rules

People may pass, observe, choose a hypothetical scenario, or keep reflection private. No one shares a personal situation with a manager or colleague by design. A classroom attempt is guided rehearsal, not a Mental Rep. In unsafe, discriminatory, coercive or clinical situations, support, protection, delay or leaving may be the appropriate next move.

Run sheet and exact core language

Time Facilitator move Participant route Non-negotiable correction
0–8 Welcome: “We are working with ordinary moments in a team context. No disclosure is required. This is not therapy, performance management, or a promise that individuals can solve workplace conditions alone.” listen/pass No baseline form in the core session.
8–18 Use two tailored but fictional examples. Ask: “What makes this a moment rather than a personality, diagnosis or performance label?” Then explain that access varies with capacity, safety, workload, relationship and environment. quiet reflection or whole-room responses Never convert a contextual problem into “mindset.”
18–31 Teach Stop–Shift–Do using a neutral example: an unexpected change to a priority creates a quick reaction. Stop: notice the moment. Shift: create space/perspective if available (pause, question, seek support, defer). Do: choose a next move aligned with what matters. “The outcome does not decide whether an intentional attempt counted.” listen, then recall each word Shift is an option, not a demand to calm down.
31–42 Shared discrimination case: “A deadline moves; someone says, ‘Just deal with it.’” Ask: “What is the moment? What might be a next move? What condition/support is separate from either?” fictional whole-group analysis Correctly separate moment, action and context.
42–56 Paired/small-group fictional rehearsal using the recorded selected S-ID 1, with Stage 1 then Stage 2 reveal where the Operations specification supplies one. Ask each group to name more than one safe Stop/Shift/Do route. join, observe or work silently No personal storytelling; no best answer.
56–68 Private translation: “You may privately think of a future, recent, or invented moment. What might help you notice it? What is one possible next move? What is an alternative if that move is unavailable?” private/paperless thought only No collection or invitation to share. A plan is not a rep.
68–78 Conditions rehearsal using the recorded selected S-ID 2. Ask: “What changes in the conditions? What routes remain possible? When might support, delay or non-action be appropriate?” shared or paired fictional analysis Do not imply courage is the only answer.
78–86 Future bridge: “A moment may appear; it may not. You may remember this process or not. Those are not moral scores. If it is useful, you have one more language for noticing and choosing. If a situation needs support or change around you, that matters too.” listen/private thought No pledge, commitment card or manager-visible artefact.
86–90 Ask unaided: “What are the three words?” Close: “A guided rehearsal is something we did here. A Mental Rep is a real-world moment where someone catches the moment and intentionally chooses what they do next.” collective recall Keep the distinction exact.

Core scenario source

Select exactly two canonical S-IDs under the companion operations specification. Record selection, avoided scenario/reason and fallback before the session. Do not attach a scenario to an assumed identity, hierarchy or diagnosis.

Facilitator recovery routes

Situation Response
A manager asks participants to share their situations “We keep this private by design. Let’s work with the fictional case instead.”
A participant says the process ignores systemic problems Agree that individual choices do not replace fair conditions, safety or support; return to the distinction between an available next move and a responsibility to fix the system.
Pair work feels unsafe or unwanted Switch immediately to silent individual or whole-group fictional analysis.
Timing slips Keep 18–31, one fictional rehearsal and 86–90. Shorten the number of examples, not privacy/scope language.

Optional modules explicitly outside the 90-minute score packet

  • Immediate learning/experience module: only after consent, outside teaching time, using MFC-OPTIONAL-MEASUREMENT-MODULES-v1.md.
  • Week-3 return: only if separately purchased/specified; not an assumed part of Essentials.
  • Manager session: a separate product/component with its own contract and no inference about participant outcomes.

07 Foundations Facilitator Packet V1

MFC Foundations — half-day facilitator packet v1

Status: internal product candidate; deepest individual-teaching service
Routine scope: individual learning in a group setting. It is not a culture, manager or environment-readiness intervention.

Required companion: use MFC-PACKET-OPERATIONS-SPEC-v1.md for host/access preparation, canonical S-ID scenarios, staged-reveal retrieval text, scenario selection and fallback rules. The companion replaces the shorthand A–D card table below.

Core promise

Foundations provides the shared Stop–Shift–Do spine at a slower pace and adds retrieval under variation, private translation, fallback planning and non-blaming troubleshooting. The added time must not become extra explanation, group confession, organisational diagnosis or vague reflection.

Detailed run sheet

Time Block and script direction Distinct individual-learning value Fallback/guardrail
0–15 Welcome, permission, scope. State: “You may pass, observe or use a fictional situation. This is not a demand to solve every hard situation yourself.” Name support/safety boundary. shared safety and product scope No personal check-in round.
15–30 Recognition: offer three ordinary fictional moments; distinguish moment from story, trait or outcome. corrects category errors before teaching If examples do not fit, invite a neutral invented example.
30–45 Teach Stop–Shift–Do exactly as in Essentials, with two contrasting worked examples. Say: “Shift may be a pause, support, distance, a question or recognising that this is not yours to solve alone.” permits slower conceptual correction Never require a specific Shift.
45–55 Individual unaided retrieval: participants silently recall the three words, then teach them back with a fictional card or in pairs. makes retrieval visible Observe/pass route; do not score participants.
55–70 Discrimination drill: identify the moment, distinguish a next move from an outcome, and name a context/support condition. distinguishes the constructs that later measurement must not collapse Use whole group if paired work is unwelcome.
70–85 Break pacing —
85–100 Scenario rehearsal A: conversation tension. Generate more than one Stop/Shift/Do route. variation in a relational moment Safety/leave/support are valid routes.
100–115 Scenario rehearsal B: overload/competing priorities. Generate routes where the first intended move is unavailable. flexibility, not repetition No advice about workload as personal failure.
115–130 Private translation: future/recent/hypothetical moment; silently name first and fallback next moves. relevance with privacy No sharing or collection.
130–145 Pair or solo explanation: explain the process using a neutral example. Receive facilitator correction. retrieval plus teach-back Use prompt cards; pass allowed.
145–165 Break pacing —
165–185 Breakpoint map: not noticed / no workable Shift / move unclear / capacity or safety barrier / no opportunity. State: “These are places to understand the situation, not grades of the person.” non-blaming diagnosis Participants can analyse fictional situations only.
185–210 Troubleshooting rehearsal: scenario cards where an obvious action is unsafe, unavailable or inappropriate; choose another route, support, delay or non-action. explicitly practises context-sensitive flexibility Avoid hero narratives.
210–230 Integration: spaced unaided retrieval then a neutral case in which participants identify process, context and outcome separately. consolidates precise language Correct drift openly and briefly.
230–245 Future bridge: optional private cue; distinguish intention, opportunity and a real-world event. “No opportunity and no use are not the same.” protects later interpretation No required commitment/return.
245–270 Close: repeat core distinction and boundaries; invite support where needed. consolidation and safe close No routine form or day-21 contact embedded.

Scenario source

Select three canonical S-IDs and a fallback under the companion operations specification. Use its exact staged-reveal text for F10. No separate A–D card asset exists.

Facilitation guardrails

  1. Keep private reflection private; no person needs to explain a choice or barrier.
  2. Do not call a rehearsal, plan or teach-back a Mental Rep.
  3. Do not imply that more practice guarantees access, success or wellbeing.
  4. Do not sell or score Route B/team components as part of Foundations’ routine value.
  5. If time compresses, remove one scenario or shorten debrief; retain retrieval, variation, breakpoint distinction and scope close.

Optional components outside this core

  • Day-21 learning return: a separately specified hypothesis, not a default proof of transfer.
  • Manager session/Route B: separate products/components, excluded from participant-core claims and score.

90 Independent Final Service Pack Review

Independent exact-flow re-review — final service packs

Decision: PASS. The three final service packs, when used with their expressly named facilitator packet and Operations specification, now form an internally complete controlled definition of the three current MFC services. The packs are the entry points; the named companions remain normative for the exact scripts, scenario text and retrieval procedures. The legacy HTML decks remain rebuild inputs only.

This is a source-fidelity and internal product-definition decision. Participant testing, delivery, governance, production rendering, approval and field outcomes were not assessed and have not been used as deductions.

Scope and authority read

Artefacts read in full Review role Status
Three final service packs v1 Candidate entry-point definitions. Artefacts under review
Three facilitator packets v1 and MFC-PACKET-OPERATIONS-SPEC-v1.md Exact timing, script, scenario and retrieval content. Normative controlled companions
MFC-FINAL-SERVICE-PACK-SECTION-CHECK-v2.md, ...CROSS-CHECK-v2.md, MFC-LEGACY-DECK-DISPOSITION-v1.md Claimed checks and legacy source rule. Supporting verification records

work/terra-raw-slide-divergence-audit.md Material-beat mapping for all three legacy HTML decks. Independent supporting audit
Current Hunter direction as reconciled in MFC-PRODUCT-ARCHITECTURE-AND-OUTCOME-CONTRACTS.md Two-lane architecture, product jobs, boundaries and T2/T4 rule. Controlling direction / decision reconciliation

The score v6 artifact is correctly presented as audit evidence, not a product-content authority, in each service pack (Introduction, Essentials and Foundations line 5).

Re-test of the five prior acceptance tests

Prior acceptance test Result Direct evidence
1. Introduction has the 20–31 worked message, 31–41 dreading-conversation retrieval, and S5/S1 only at 41–52. PASS Service pack lines 17–23 now places the worked upsetting-message example at 27–31, the exact dreading-conversation prompt at 31–41, and S5/S1 only at 41–52. These match the facilitator packet’s 20–31 (:52–70), 31–41 (:72–82) and 41–52 (:84–100) blocks.
2. Essentials has the fixed 31–42 case, uses selected S-IDs only in their rehearsal blocks, and uses the single Operations close. PASS Pack lines 20–25 restores the exact deadline/“Just deal with it” case, records S-ID 1 at 42–56 and S-ID 2 at 68–78, and specifies hide/turn → five seconds → pass/answer → reveal/correct. This matches the packet :24–29 and Operations :9, 17–30. No E-A/E-B or verbal-only alternative remains in the service pack.
3. Foundations distinguishes both retrieval protocols, preserves S4 Stage 1→Stage 2, applies the selection rule, and uses pair-or-solo teach-back. PASS Pack line 14 gives the first no-card/visual, five-second private/pass protocol; lines 17–18 and 23 give the S2/S3/S4 defaults, S1 fallback and recorded substitution rule; line 20 is pair-or-solo; lines 23–25 distinguish S4 troubleshooting, then the separate second unaided retrieval, then intention/opportunity/event. Operations :10–11, 34 supplies the exact silent-retrieval and staged-reveal detail.
4. The source hierarchy is clear: packet + Operations are normative; scores/checks are audit evidence only. PASS All three packs line 5 label their companions “Normative exact-content companions” and label v6 audit evidence only. Cross-check v2 line 14 and legacy disposition line 11 repeat the controlled-triad rule.
5. Fresh checks reproduce the same jobs, boundaries and sequences without the legacy HTML. PASS Section check v2 lines 5–11 gives each product’s timed source-faithful sequence and names the packet/Operations companion; cross-check v2 lines 5–14 reconfirms jobs, T2/T4, participation, data boundary and marginal value; legacy disposition lines 3–11 keeps HTML non-controlling.

Product-level result

Service Result Current definitional job and boundary verified
Introduction 60 PASS Broad adult public first encounter; no required materials, writing, data, follow-up or real-world-use claim; collective guided rehearsal is not a Mental Rep.
Essentials 90 PASS Contextual team learning at standard depth; private/fictional/pass participation; no manager-visible personal material, return, measurement or team/culture promise in the core.
Foundations 270 PASS Deepest individual-teaching service; added time earns retrieval variation, private translation, non-blaming breakpoint work and troubleshooting; no Route B, manager or culture component in the core.

Three required checks

Check Result Basis
Section-by-section check v2 PASS Its stated sequence agrees with the repaired packs and the named exact-content companions.
Cross-pack check v2 PASS The two-lane portfolio is differentiated without product-boundary, T2/T4 or scope drift.
Legacy-deck disposition PASS It correctly treats all three HTML decks as legacy and now names the service-pack + packet + Operations triad as the sole rebuild source. The raw audit has a complete material-beat map for each deck.

Closure of the prior major findings

  • Introduction: no longer routes the 31–41 guided recall through S1/S5; it restores the worked fictional message.
  • Essentials: no longer replaces the fixed discrimination case with a selected case, invents E-A/E-B, or permits a standalone verbal-only close.
  • Foundations: no longer inserts a private retrieval between S4 stages or adds whole-room teach-back; it restores first-retrieval, default-substitution and intention language.
  • Change control: the score is no longer styled as a content control, and the controlled triad is now explicit in the packs, cross-check and legacy disposition.

Minor maintenance observation — non-blocking

MFC-ESSENTIALS-90-FACILITATOR-PACKET-v1.md:7 still calls the companion an “86–90 verbal-or-hidden-visual retrieval protocol.” The governing Operations row (MFC-PACKET-OPERATIONS-SPEC-v1.md:9) and corrected service-pack row (MFC-FINAL-SERVICE-PACK-ESSENTIALS-v1.md:25) make the actual protocol unambiguous: hide/turn the visual, wait five seconds, then reveal/correct. Rename the packet-header phrase to “hidden-visual retrieval protocol” in its next controlled revision to remove an avoidable shorthand ambiguity. It does not alter the current controlled flow and is not a condition of this PASS.

Conclusion

Yes. The corrected set can be presented internally as the single current definition of Introduction, Essentials and Foundations as a controlled triad: final service pack (entry point) + named facilitator packet + Operations specification (normative exact content). It is not accurate to describe any one summary file in isolation as the entire service definition, and it remains incorrect to represent the legacy HTML decks as current services.

No conclusion is made here about participant response, testing, delivery, production rebuild quality or governance approval.
