19 Half Day Deck Preflight And Assurance

Half-Day Foundations slide deck — preflight, rationale and assurance

Lifecycle correction, 2026-08-13: this record establishes source fidelity, package coherence and local artifact assurance. It is not a design-intelligence review and does not establish that the education-led architecture or 80-screen implementation is optimal. The current lifecycle is internal candidate until the option comparison, staged specialist challenge and rationale work in 23-half-day-design-intelligence-and-founder-finalisation.md are completed and applied. Hunter has not approved this build as final.

Scope and honest sequence

This governs the single current Half-Day deck candidate. It does not create another workshop or a parallel architecture. The first 38-screen assembly was built from the older 44:56 storyboard without first proving source authority, learning architecture, language fidelity or projection readability. A later 64-screen correction improved those defects but still used the wrong arc. It is preserved in archive/slide-deck-practice-heavy-64-slide-superseded.html and is explicitly not current.

The current candidate was reconstructed from the later education-led operational package. Its 80 screens are an output of the teaching and interaction sequence, not a quota. This record is honest that artifact-specific preflight occurred only after the original build failed.

Source precedence and conflict resolution

  1. Product identity and container: D-0094, then D-0098.
  2. Current workshop-product amendments: D-0091.
  3. Current operational Half-Day arc, timings and room plan: workshop-package.html.
  4. Locked public wording and framework boundaries: K-04, K-05, K-07, K-08.
  5. Founder/Gina communication controls: 13-founder-voice-v2-explaining-mental-fitness.md, 15-copywriting-craft-fundamentals.md, 05-brand-voice-and-language.md, D-0046, D-0047.
  6. Current delivery operations: 20-half-day-foundations-facilitator-guide-current.md and 21-half-day-foundations-participant-materials-current.md.
  7. Reusable production constraints: 13-contrast-asset-spec-and-readability-pass.md and the still-valid locked wording/specifications inside the older participant-material source.

14-DRAFT-recut-arc-education-led.md is historical provenance for Hunter's rejection and the education-led rationale; D-0091 and workshop-package.html contain the later operational state. Files 01-three-hour-design.md, 10-facilitator-guide-3hour.md and the storyboard/timings in 11-participant-materials-and-storyboard.md retain the founder-rejected 44:56 arc. They remain readable as history and as sources of reusable copy, but they may not drive current sequence, timing, slide count or delivery.

Evidence corpus map

Source Classification Use in this pass

D-0091 USED IN FULL Current applied-rep and shared-Radar amendments.
workshop-package.html CURRENT OPERATIONAL SOURCE 113:67/63:37 education-led arc and room plan.

Decision-rationale matrix

Choice Decision Rationale
Overall count 80 screens, reopenable Count follows the jobs below, including the now-explicit post-instruction Form 2 handoff. No optimum count is claimed; rehearsal or independent review may change it.
Founder/Gina opening Recognition, physical parallel, human learning gap, then mechanism Uses the approved human premise and removes curse-of-knowledge compression before MFC terms appear.
Moments spectrum Two screens Preserves Gina-endorsed difficult/ordinary/joyful range without projecting a paragraph.
Five public skills Five screens Keeps each locked sentence legible and gives every skill equal weight.
Stop–Shift–Do corrections Three screens The corrections are part of the teaching, not a disclaimer; colour is paired with word, shape and fixed position.
Retrieval drill Ten prompts Preserves one-prompt-at-a-time mapping, reversal, pace and correction retrieval instead of merely showing answers.
Human Operating System Intro, Driver, Passenger, Engine, question The current package teaches three parts only. It is explicitly a teaching model, not a brain map or diagnosis.
State Check Question, three states, private check Keeps it separate from Stop–Shift–Do, anchors “for this moment,” uses no colour scale and protects privacy.
Mental rep Definition, recognition, immediate applied rep Education lands before experience; the room does a small rep before the second break.
Block Three Easy-moment rationale, shifts, contrast, Radar, cue, lapse/return Follows the current education-led transfer sequence. A shared/team Radar appears only if a separately approved question was actually collected; routine D-0100 Form 1 does not contain that item.
Measurement close Form 2 at 3:30-3:34, after the instructional close Makes the approved immediate post-session measure operational without distorting the 113:67 instructional balance. Only the exact cohort-frozen approved form may be used.
Visual system Restrained text-led projection The facilitator, participant activity and room wall are the medium; decoration must not compete with retrieval or privacy.

Founder and Gina language control

The candidate preserves the locked definition, expansion, five skill sentences, Stop–Shift–Do meaning, State Check question, mental-rep definition, Passenger line and Radar prompt. It uses Hunter's physical-health/fitness parallel and his mechanism order. It restores Gina-endorsed anchors: “No one is born knowing how to handle every human moment,” skills learned through guidance/observation/experience/practice/repetition, and the difficult/ordinary/joyful moments spectrum.

Shared-human explanations prefer we/us; direct exercises use you. “Workable” is glossed where it is first taught. The deck avoids production labels, the seven deeper skill names, unexplained proper-nounification and deficit language. One language change made during assurance replaced “feelings are valid” with the more precise and inclusive “feelings can carry information about what matters to us; they are not instructions.” This does not claim that Gina independently reviewed the deck.

Professional lens coverage

Lens What actually ran Status and limit
Learning/behaviour design Current operational arc, prior executed specialist work and integrated package review Internal pass with conditions; no fresh independent specialist review of this 80-screen artifact or its unified guide/materials.
Communications/founder language Locked corpus, Founder Voice V2, Gina baseline and copywriting controls checked against on-screen copy Internal pass; no claim of Gina, Hunter or A-08 approval.
Accessibility/technical All 80 screens rendered in Chrome at 1280×720 and 390×844 in both supported light and dark themes; overflow, bounds and desktop projected-text size checked Passed local digital render; real projector, room-distance, washout and assistive-technology testing remain open.
Safeguarding/privacy Disclosure, opt-out, private State Check/Radar and source conflicts screened Fail-closed. Butcher-paper/privacy, distress/referral wording and qualified-human gates remain open.
Brand/creative Existing restrained MFC system applied and all frames visually inspected Internal visual pass only; no fresh Alysse/creative approval.

Agent Steward need test: no new persistent agent is justified. The responsibilities already exist; the recurring defect is failure to invoke source-precedence, preflight and artifact-assurance at the right time. The smallest sufficient intervention is the enforced preflight plus live candidate validator, wired into the existing controls.

Accessibility and technical checks

  • 80/80 screens render in light and dark themes with no detected desktop or mobile clipping, scroll overflow, out-of-bounds text or console errors.
  • Participant-visible desktop projection text is at least 32 CSS px; the delivery-gate copy is not a participant screen.
  • Core text/background contrast ranges from 5.27:1 to 15.71:1 across the two themes for the tokens used by participant text and the internal gate warning.
  • Colour is accompanied by word, shape and position for Stop–Shift–Do.
  • Keyboard navigation supports arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End and space; P toggles presenter chrome.
  • The deck fails closed until “Open internal review deck” is deliberately activated.
  • All 80 desktop frames were inspected in refreshed contact sheets after the automated pass.
  • The only console error is an optional missing favicon.ico; no deck behaviour depends on it.

Important unresolved questions the deck cannot close

  1. The current participant materials are controlled copy, not yet approved print-ready artwork.
  2. The butcher-paper exercise versus anonymous/private collection remains a safeguarding and facilitation trade-off requiring qualified review and rehearsal.
  3. The qualified distress/referral wording is still a visible placeholder; the participant support card therefore remains blocked.
  4. Forms 1, 2 and 3 must be approved and frozen for a cohort; collection, storage, aggregation and deletion must be operationally proved.
  5. Shared/team Radar may run only if a separately approved team question was actually collected. Routine D-0100 Form 1 does not supply it.
  6. Room configuration, materials staging, facilitator load and the full timed sequence require rehearsal; projector and assistive-technology checks remain open.
  7. The Introduction deck and 90-Minute Essentials remain separate open product work; this package does not imply they exist.
  8. Qualified safeguarding, clinical-governance, privacy/legal, insurer and host review—and real participant testing—remain outside AI authority.

Safeguarding and approval boundary

The deck displays a full-screen not cleared for participant delivery gate. The unresolved distress/referral placeholder remains visible during internal review and is never fabricated. Clinical-governance, legal/privacy, insurer, host, accessibility and real-participant approval remain outside AI authority.

Verdict

PASS WITH CONDITIONS — single unified internal package candidate. The arc, deck, current guide and participant-material copy now agree under the live package verifier. This permits internal review and rehearsal; it does not establish delivery readiness. The package is not independently specialist-reviewed, not qualified-human-approved, not fully produced, not projector/room-tested, not participant-tested and not cleared for delivery.

The strongest next step is a fresh independent review of the unified package followed by a full timed rehearsal. Only findings from those checks—not an arbitrary slide quota—should drive further deck changes.

20 Half Day Foundations Facilitator Guide Current

⚑ POINTER ADDED 2026-09-08 — read before assuming this file is dead. This document carries the experience-design pass Hunter commissioned on 2026-08-19/20. It was not carried into the 2026-09-01 from-scratch rebuild, and because that rebuild wrote new files rather than editing these, git records no deletion and nothing here was ever marked superseded. D-0130 recorded the loss seven days later; the 2026-09-08 archaeology pass recovered the contents. D-0131 restores the fold-and-hold ritual, Priya the running character, and the misreads-performed-wrongly comedy beat from this file. This file is therefore a live source, not a superseded draft. Do not delete it and do not rebuild from scratch without reading it.

Experience-design redesign pass, 2026-08-19–20 — read before the rest of this document

Per Hunter's direct decision, the same experience-design treatment applied to Essentials (130) is applied here across the session's full arc, not just the opening: (1) engineered peak — the "same moment twice" beat (2:52–3:04) is directed as the session's deliberate high point, with genuine performance commitment and a held silence before discussion. (2) The close (3:27–3:30) is now deliberately weighted alongside it — per the peak-end research this pass is built on, both the peak and the ending carry disproportionate weight in what's actually remembered, so both now get genuine warmth rather than a brisk wrap-up. (3) Consent/disclosure tone rewritten across the full arc, substance unchanged and re-verified — the 0:00–0:07 opening and the 3:22–3:27 lapse-normalising beat both carry every prior commitment with warmth instead of a flat list; this does not touch the still-open D-0016 safeguarding gate. Corrected 20 Aug, after the simulated committee (Nell, Sable) independently caught that the first version of the opening rewrite had actually dropped the safety exception — fixed in place, and this correction is why every remaining beat in this document was re-checked against its original wording rather than assumed safe by pattern-matching. (4) A single running narrative ("Priya"), the same character used in Essentials, replaces the neutral facilitator-supplied example at 1:32–1:44 for cross-product consistency. (5) A genuine light beat added after the opening housekeeping. (6) Flow-theory pacing considered within existing timing.

Deliberately not touched: the mid-session teaching beats (five skills, Stop-Shift-Do mechanics, Human Operating System, State Check, Mental Reps, the shift-routes menu) keep their original wording — these are locked/evidenced content, and the redesign pass targeted the beats that actually carry emotional weight (opening, peak, close, lapse-normalising) rather than rewriting content that was never the problem.

Half-Day Foundations — current facilitator guide

[!DANGER] Not cleared for participant delivery This is the current education-led teaching candidate. It is not permission to run a session. Do not use it until the cohort has an approved participant/referral card, approved and frozen measurement forms, privacy/legal and safeguarding procedures, insurer/host clearance, accessible materials, a resolved butcher-paper route and a successful timed room rehearsal.

1. What this guide controls

This is the delivery instrument for the current Half-Day Foundations arc in workshop-package.html: 180 instructional minutes, two 15-minute breaks, then an optional approximately four-minute immediate form after the teaching close. It replaces the sequence and timings in 10-facilitator-guide-3hour.md, which remains historical evidence of the rejected 44:56 practice-heavy arc.

The communication job is: by the end, adults should understand that mental fitness is a developable capacity for everyday life, recall Stop–Shift–Do, complete at least one small Mental Rep, and leave with one personally meaningful moment they can notice again.

The facilitator teaches the meaning. The slides hold the room's shared attention. The participant materials support recall and private application. None substitutes for the others.

2. Authority and non-negotiables

The following wording is exact where shown:

  • “Mental fitness is how well we navigate life's everyday moments.”
  • “Mental health is how we are doing. Mental fitness is what we are able to do.”
  • the five full public skill sentences;
  • Stop — catch the moment; Shift — create enough space where useful and available; Do — make the next move with intention;
  • “The Passenger is not bad.”
  • “Is my state too much, too little, or workable for this moment?”
  • the full Mental Rep definition;
  • “Think about the person you are trying to become in this season of life.”

Do not:

  • call the product the “3-hour workshop”; three hours describes approximate teaching time only;
  • teach the seven deeper skills as participant-facing content;
  • present the Human Operating System as neuroscience, diagnosis or a map of the brain;
  • turn the State Check into a fourth step, traffic light, mood scale or public disclosure;
  • say amber means calming down or green means the right answer;
  • imply a rep worked only when the outcome was good;
  • ask participants to disclose personal material;
  • suggest unsafe, structural or workload problems are solved by individual skill;
  • claim this workshop causes wellbeing improvement, prevents illness or produces habit formation.

3. Delivery roles and room conditions

Minimum operational roles once cleared:

  1. Lead facilitator — teaching, timing, room observation and opt-out protection.
  2. Host contact — venue, accessibility adjustments and agreed response procedure.
  3. Support/escalation contact — the qualified procedure must state who this is and what they do.
  4. Second facilitator or tested film route — required for the contrast activity.

Room requirements:

  • 12–20 participants; any other range requires a fresh facilitation/load review;
  • accessible entry, seating, toilet and break route;
  • wall or alternative display space approved by the venue;
  • screen readable from the furthest seat, with a tested dark/light fallback;
  • seating that permits individual work without facilitators reading over private worksheets;
  • printed large-type alternatives available without a participant having to justify the request;
  • paper alternative for every digital form;
  • visible clock for the facilitator, not a public countdown.

4. Before the cohort is confirmed

The producer must complete this checklist. A blank box means do not deliver.

  • [ ] The exact workshop version, deck, guide and participant pack are frozen together.
  • [ ] Qualified safeguarding/clinical procedure approved and supplied.
  • [ ] Legal/privacy notice, data access, retention, withdrawal and reporting route approved.
  • [ ] Insurer and host operating constraints confirmed.
  • [ ] Approved participant/referral card contains no placeholder.
  • [ ] Approved baseline, immediate and day-21 form versions are named and frozen.
  • [ ] Random evaluation-ID/contact-key method or approved anonymous alternative is operational.
  • [ ] Butcher-paper versus private alternative is resolved for this cohort.
  • [ ] Any optional team-nomination module is separately approved and actually included—or the shared-Radar aggregate route is disabled.
  • [ ] Accessibility adjustments and non-digital alternatives confirmed.
  • [ ] Contrast film/live route tested.
  • [ ] Full timed rehearsal completed with another person observing the room experience.
  • [ ] Final projector/room-distance legibility check passed.

5. Facilitator preparation

Five working files

Bring only the current versions:

  1. this guide;
  2. slide-deck-half-day-foundations.html;
  3. 21-half-day-foundations-participant-materials-current.md or its production exports;
  4. the exact cohort-frozen measurement forms;
  5. the approved support/privacy/incident procedure.

Form 1 and team-module preparation

Form 1 is completed before teaching begins, preferably before the event or while people settle. Never describe it as anonymous if responses are linked through a contact key.

The routine D-0100 core does not contain the proposed team-nomination question. Therefore:

  • if no separately approved team module exists, prepare no aggregate and use the individual Radar route at 3:04;
  • if an approved module exists, confirm the item was actually asked, suppress unsafe small-cell or identifying material, prepare only two or three de-identified themes, and never infer agreement from nomination frequency;
  • do not show raw free text or identify who wrote anything;
  • if safe aggregation is doubtful, disable the route.

Materials staging

On seats/tables before entry:

  • approved participant/referral card;
  • workshop map;
  • baseline form route, if not completed earlier;
  • pen and accessible alternatives.

Keep later materials out of sight and issue them only when used. This reduces reading ahead and cognitive load.

6. Facilitation conventions

  • [SAY — EXACT] preserves locked wording.
  • [SAY] is a safe working script; natural delivery is allowed if meaning and boundaries remain.
  • [DO] is an operational instruction.
  • [CHECK] is evidence the facilitator must observe; it is not a participant test.
  • [CUT] states what may be shortened if the room runs late.
  • [NEVER CUT] protects the learning or safety function.
  • [GATE] means the session may not proceed without the named condition.

Use we/us for shared human explanation. Use you for direct exercises. Avoid “the system” when a normal verb will do the work.

BLOCK 1 — Why none of us were ever taught this

Arrival — before 0:00

Job: complete the approved baseline without using teaching time and welcome people without monitoring their answers.

[DO]

  • Greet people normally; do not inspect responses.
  • Offer the exact approved baseline route, framed as normal practice — this is just something we do at the start of every session — while stating plainly it's anonymous and genuinely fine to skip. (Reframed 2026-08-19, Hunter, direct decision — matches the same change applied to Essentials — normalised as the default rather than offered as an optional add-on, opt-out and anonymity kept genuinely intact.)
  • Make paper and non-digital completion equally ordinary.
  • If the form is incomplete at 0:00, do not delay the workshop or pressure completion.

[GATE] Use only the cohort-frozen Form 1. If the current form is still a candidate, the session is not cleared.

0:00–0:03 — Open with why we are here

Job: make the session worth attention before explaining process.

[SAY]

“We all have a body. Physical health is how it is doing; physical fitness is what it can actually do. The same split helps us understand the mind. Mental health is how we are doing. Mental fitness is what we are able to do—how we think, work with what we feel, act on what matters, and connect with ourselves and others.

This morning is about something most of us were never deliberately taught: what we can practise in the everyday moments our lives are made of.”

[DO] Pause. Let the premise land before describing logistics.

[CHECK] The opening must not imply mental health and mental fitness are mutually exclusive, and it must not imply mental fitness replaces care.

0:03–0:07 — How today works

Rewritten 2026-08-19, Hunter, direct decision — tone rewrite, matching the same change applied to Essentials (130). Every commitment below is unchanged in substance and stays exactly as binding — K-08's ceiling, the clinical boundary, the choice/opt-out guarantee — this is about warmth in delivery, not a reduction in what's protected.

Corrected 2026-08-20, after the simulated committee (Nell, Sable, independently) caught a real defect in the first version of this rewrite: the safety exception — "if something comes up that suggests someone's safety is at risk, that's the one thing I can't keep to myself" — was dropped entirely, leaving an uncarved "what you write is yours, full stop" promise that Essentials' equivalent beat correctly does not make. That was the "substance unchanged" claim failing in the one product that wasn't the worked example. Fixed below — the exception is now present, worded to match the warm register of the rest of the beat rather than reverting to the flatter original phrasing.

Job: establish choice, privacy, non-clinical scope and the support route with energy, not as a legal recitation.

[SAY]

“Quick bit of housekeeping, then we get into the actual good stuff. This is education and real skill practice — not therapy, not treatment, nothing clinical about it. If you're already working with someone professionally, today sits alongside that, doesn't replace it.

You're in the driver's seat today: sit out anything, step out and come back, or do it a different way if that works better for you — no explanation needed, ever. Nobody's going to ask you to share anything personal, and what you write for yourself stays yours. One honest exception, and I'd rather say it now than later: if something comes up that tells me someone's safety is genuinely at risk, that's the one thing I won't sit on. Everything else stays with you.

Everything about support and privacy for today is on the card in front of you.”

[DO] Point to the card without reading the whole card aloud, briskly and warmly. Name venue access, breaks, toilets and the host/support contact like someone glad to have you here, in the manner required by the approved procedure.

[SAY — a genuine light beat, added 2026-08-19, facilitator's own words, not scripted verbatim]

One honest, self-deprecating aside here, matched to the room — "I promise the rest of today is more interesting than a housekeeping list" or similar. Job: the same reactance-management function as Essentials' equivalent beat (130, 0:03) — genuine warmth defusing resistance better than more careful language does, right after the procedural content, before anything substantive starts.

[GATE] If the support or privacy card contains a placeholder, stop. Do not deliver.

0:07–0:20 — Shared word-association sheets

Job: let participants generate recognition before MFC names the distinction, without making visible participation the price of entry.

[GATE] The routine floor is the approved private route. Use shared butcher paper only when the cohort's privacy, access and participation decision has separately approved it. The activity asks for word associations, not personal experiences. Preserve the later pattern/reveal function without exposing authorship. Passing and non-writing routes must produce an equally complete experience.

[SAY]

“On your table is one sheet. Start with this: when you hear mental health, what comes to mind? Write words or short phrases. Nobody has to explain an answer.”

[DO] After approximately six minutes:

“On the same sheet: when you hear mental fitness, what comes to mind? Add whatever comes. We are not looking for a correct definition yet.”

[DO]

  • Circulate only as authorised by the approved route.
  • Affirm contribution without grading it: “That is a useful word”; “What else belongs here?”
  • Do not ask “why?” of an individual contribution.
  • If something personal appears, do not invite elaboration. Follow the approved response procedure if necessary.

[CHECK] Pens are moving by minute seven. The facilitator is teaching curiosity, not correcting the room into MFC's answer.

0:20–0:25 — Read the room's words

Job: make the room's pattern visible.

[DO] Display each table's sheet using the approved route. Invite quiet reading for 60–90 seconds. Provide a seated/visual-description alternative; standing is never required.

[SAY]

“Just notice the pattern. Nobody needs to defend or explain what is on a sheet.”

[CUT] Shorten facilitator commentary, not the quiet scan.

0:25–0:33 — Name the distinction

Job: connect the generated pattern to the locked public meaning.

[SAY — EXACT]

“Mental fitness is how well we navigate life's everyday moments.”

[SAY — EXACT]

“It shows up in how we think, work with what we feel, act on what matters, and connect with ourselves and others.”

[SAY — EXACT]

“Mental health is how we are doing. Mental fitness is what we are able to do.”

[SAY]

“The physical parallel is useful: physical health is how the body is doing; physical fitness is what the body can do. Exercise can support mental health, but an activity is not automatically a Mental Rep. The rep is the moment you notice and choose what you do next.”

[CHECK] Do not claim the room “proved” the definition. Their words created recognition; MFC supplies its controlled definition.

0:33–0:45 — Teach the gap

Job: remove blame and make education relevant.

[SAY]

“No one is born knowing how to handle every human moment. These skills are learned through guidance, observation, experience, practice and repetition.

Most of us assembled strategies from whatever life gave us—from people around us, things we tried, things that happened, and sometimes nowhere obvious at all.”

[DO] If the approved baseline permits an aggregate answer to the “where did you learn?” item, present only the safely aggregated categories. If it does not, omit the aggregate; never invent what “most rooms” say.

[SAY]

“That does not mean we are broken. It shows a gap between what we may know and what we can draw on while life is happening. It is a gap in what we were taught—not a gap in us.”

[CHECK] The emotional movement should be recognition → relief → possibility, never shame.

0:45–0:57 — Thoughts, feelings and what is trainable

Job: establish a non-adversarial foundation before teaching the tool.

[SAY]

“Not every thought is a fact. Feelings are not good or bad. They can carry information about what matters to us. They are not instructions.”

[SAY — EXACT]

“The Passenger is not bad.”

[SAY]

“A feeling arriving is not a failure, and this session is not about forcing a feeling away. What we can practise is what happens next—what we notice, what space is available, and the move we choose.”

[CHECK] Do not call anxiety, anger or any other named feeling inherently useful, harmful, valid or invalid for every person. Explain function without universalising an experience.

0:57–1:00 — Give the day a destination

Job: name what they can reasonably leave with and include difficult, ordinary and positive life.

[SAY]

“Some moments are difficult. Some are ordinary. Some are joyful, meaningful or easy to miss. There are moments of pressure, connection, distraction, courage, uncertainty, rest, conflict, enjoyment and change.

You are not leaving with a finished skill. You are leaving with one thing small enough to remember and useful enough to reach for in a real moment.”

1:00–1:15 — Break

[DO] State the restart time. Do not use the break to pursue disclosure or inspect private work.

BLOCK 2 — The tool and what shapes access

1:15–1:22 — The five skills

Job: teach the public capacities in full language without adding a recall burden.

[DO] Issue the skills card.

[SAY — EXACT]

  • “Notice — notice what is happening inside you, around you, and between you and others.”
  • “Shift — create enough space to become workable—through your body, or through your thinking.”
  • “Choose — identify what matters and follow through.”
  • “Focus — put your attention where it matters and return it when it drifts.”
  • “Connect — connect better with yourself and others.”

[SAY]

“Workable means enough energy, steadiness and clarity for what this moment needs. It does not mean calm. You do not need all five skills in every moment, and nobody is asking you to memorise this list today.”

[DO] Give one ordinary, concrete example per skill. Keep the five examples to three minutes total.

[CUT] Cut examples from two skills if late; never cut or paraphrase the full sentences on the card.

1:22–1:32 — Stop–Shift–Do

Job: give the room a retrievable handle without teaching a rigid formula.

[DO] Issue the Stop–Shift–Do card.

[SAY — EXACT]

“Stop—catch the moment.

Shift—create enough space where useful and available.

Do—make the next move with intention.”

[SAY]

“The traffic-light colours are a memory aid, named once. They are not instructions from a road.

Red does not mean freeze. It means catch the moment.

Amber does not mean calm down. It means create enough space. Sometimes that is settling; sometimes it is becoming sharper or more connected. Some moments need no obvious Shift.

Green does not mean the right answer. It means the next move made with intention.”

[CHECK] Colour must appear with the step word, distinct shape and fixed position. Do not use a stop palm as the red glyph.

1:32–1:44 — Worked example and retrieval

Job: connect the three steps to an ordinary scene, then make retrieval effortful and low-risk. Narrative thread added 2026-08-19, Hunter, direct decision — same running character used across Essentials (130), for a consistent MFC device rather than a one-off scenario.

[SAY]

“We're going to follow one person through one ordinary moment, then practise getting the steps back — not be tested on them. Answer aloud, point to the card, write, gesture, or just follow along. Nobody's getting picked out.”

[DO] Use one neutral facilitator-supplied example, told as a small scene, not a checklist. Do not ask the room for personal material:

  1. Moment: it's Priya's Tuesday — mid-morning, deep in something else, and an email lands that's clearly going to need a careful answer.
  2. Stop: she notices the pull to fire back an answer immediately, just to make it go away.
  3. Shift: feet flat on the floor, reads it a second time.
  4. Do: writes down the one actual question underneath it, and answers only that.

Real gap, found 2026-08-20, specialist review (A-22): the email scenario is a desk-worker default and won't be "an ordinary moment" for a trade, healthcare, frontline, warehouse or retail audience — it risks reading as belonging to someone else's job, at the first concrete example the session offers. Swap the detail, keep the shape, if the room isn't desk-based — same four beats, different trigger:

Trade/frontline version: it's Priya's Tuesday — mid-shift, focused on the job in front of her, and someone flags a problem that's clearly going to need a careful call. Stop: she notices the pull to react on the spot, just to make it go away. Shift: stops, takes it in properly. Do: works out the one thing that actually needs deciding, and decides only that.

Read the room before the session and pick the version that fits, or ask the host which is closer to the room's actual work — this is a facilitator judgement call, not a script the room self-selects. Not yet tested with a real non-desk cohort; flagged as genuinely open, not resolved by having a second version on paper.

[CHECK] The example demonstrates a possible process, not the correct response. The outcome is not shown as improved, and no one is asked to identify with the scene.

[DO] Hide the step words, then offer all response modes above. Wait before revealing:

  1. “What were the three steps?”
  2. “Which step created space? Which step caught the moment?”
  3. “All three, in order.” → “Stop. Shift. Do.”
  4. “Is red freezing?” → “No—catching the moment.”
  5. “Is amber calming down?” → “No—creating space.”
  6. “Does green mean the right answer?” → “No—the next move, with intention.”

[DO] Finish on item 6 so the final retrieval is the outcome/rightness correction.

[NEVER CUT] Keep the worked example, one complete reconstruction and all three corrections. If the room is overloaded, slow the rhythm or let people use the card; do not cold-call.

1:44–1:53 — Human Operating System

Job: explain why access changes without teaching six more public skills.

[DO] Issue the current three-part HOS sheet.

[SAY]

“This is a teaching model—not a map of the brain, not a diagnosis, and not something you need to memorise. We are using three parts today because they answer one useful question: what is shaping what is available to me right now?”

Driver

“The Driver is what you can reach right now: noticing, paying attention, pausing, choosing and making your next move with intention.”

Passenger

“The Passenger is thoughts, feelings, urges, what you want and need, memories, and how you read a situation.”

[SAY — EXACT] “The Passenger is not bad.”

Engine

“The Engine is your body: energy, tiredness, tension, breathing, hunger, sleep and recovery.”

[SAY]

“The point is not to label ourselves. It is to ask: what is shaping what is available to me right now? What is making a useful response easier or harder to reach?”

[CUT] Do not add Pathways, Navigation or Environment as participant terms in this session. You may acknowledge that context and support matter in normal language.

1:53–1:59 — State Check

Job: teach a private access question and immediately use it.

[DO] Issue the State Check card.

[SAY — EXACT]

“Is my state too much, too little, or workable for this moment?”

[SAY]

“Too much: downshift towards workable. Too little: upshift towards workable. Workable: probably no shift needed. Workable does not mean calm. The words describe what this moment can use—not who you are.”

[DO]

“Run the question privately now. Eyes open or closed. Ten seconds. Nothing written, nothing shared.”

[CHECK] Do not ask for a show of hands, colour, score or label.

1:59–2:08 — Mental Reps

Job: name the unit of practice before asking participants to do one.

[SAY — EXACT]

“A mental rep is catching a moment and choosing your next move, on purpose, toward what matters. You may catch the moment before it happens, while it is happening, or afterwards. The outcome does not determine whether it counts.”

[SAY]

“Have you ever caught yourself scrolling and put the phone down? That can be a rep: you caught a moment and chose a move. A moment by itself is not automatically a rep. Reading about a skill is not automatically a rep. The deliberate application is the unit.”

[SAY]

“You have already done versions of this. The missing piece is often that nobody named it, taught the shift, or helped us practise retrieving it while life was happening.”

[CHECK] Do not say people have done “thousands” unless the claim is framed as rhetorical rather than known fact. Do not imply repetition guarantees capability or habit.

2:08–2:15 — Complete one small rep

Job: practise immediately at low stakes.

[SAY]

“Think of one ordinary moment from today—or one likely later today. Keep it small. You can invent a neutral example instead of using your own life.”

[DO] Four minutes private:

  1. Catch the moment.
  2. Run a State Check.
  3. Choose one small shift or next move. Naming what is happening or taking one slow exhale is enough.

[SAY]

“If you want to, tell the person next to you the moment and the move. You can also pass, stay with your notes, or use the neutral example. No explanation needed.”

[DO] Three minutes optional pairs. Do not roam and listen in.

[CHECK] The activity must feel like practice, not performance. Nothing is collected.

2:15–2:30 — Break

[DO] State restart time. Prepare the shift materials and contrast route.

BLOCK 3 — Use it and carry it into life

2:30–2:40 — Train in easier moments

Job: make low-friction practice legitimate rather than lesser.

[SAY]

“You would not walk into a gym and start with the heaviest thing in the room. You would train with something you could move. The same principle applies here: practise in moments where it is easier, so the skill is easier to reach when it is not.”

[SAY]

“The easy rep is not a fake rep. It is the training ground. A language, an instrument, driving—most skills become more familiar through practice and repetition. That does not guarantee what happens in the hardest moment. It gives us something more available to draw on.”

[CHECK] Avoid the old line that mental practice requires no time in an absolute sense. The moments already exist, but attention and effort still have a real cost.

2:40–2:46 — Four kinds of shift

Job: widen the menu without turning it into a prescription list.

[DO] Issue the shift-toolkit sheet.

[SAY]

“A shift can work through four places: body, attention, perspective or connection. The same tool can bring us down or bring us up. The question is what creates enough space for this moment.”

Give one ordinary example each:

  • body — stand, release shoulders, eat, take a slower out-breath;
  • attention — widen to the room or narrow to one next task;
  • perspective — test whether a thought is fact, or try a more generous reading;
  • connection — ask for two minutes, sit near someone or seek appropriate support.

[SAY]

“Connection is only where it is safe and appropriate, and only with people you would choose. Some problems need support, a boundary, a system change or something outside this workshop—not a better individual response.”

2:46–2:52 — Try two shifts

Job: compare experience without forcing an effect.

[SAY]

“You can watch instead. You do not have to close your eyes, control your breathing, stand, touch anyone or explain what happens.”

[DO] Lead two preselected, accessible shifts one at a time—normally one body route and one attention route. Before each: notice. After each: notice what changed, if anything.

[SAY]

“Up, down, sideways or nothing at all—nothing is useful information too. A strategy not suiting you is information about the strategy, not a failure in you.”

[CHECK] Never intensify breathwork, interoception or eye closure to manufacture an effect.

2:52–3:04 — The same moment twice — the engineered peak

Job: let participants see the process without promising a better outcome. Named 2026-08-19, Hunter, direct decision, as this session's deliberate peak moment — per the peak-end research this redesign is built on (Kahneman, Fredrickson & Schreiber), people remember an experience by its most intense moment and its ending, not the average, and this beat already has the dramatic shape to carry that weight — a real scene, a real contrast, played straight. It just needed to be treated as the peak on purpose rather than one beat among many.

[DO] Run the approved film or rehearsed two-facilitator scene. Same person, same ordinary pressure, same ending; only the response changes. Do not use participant volunteers. Give this scene genuine performance commitment — full pace, full stakes, not underplayed — this is the room's one moment of real theatre, and it earns being played that way.

[DO] After the scene, before any discussion: a real pause, five to ten seconds, held in silence. Let the contrast land before anyone is asked to speak. Do not rush into "what did you notice."

[SAY]

“What did you notice?”

[DO] Accept observation before interpretation. Prompt only if needed:

  • “Where was the moment caught?”
  • “What shifted?”
  • “What stayed the same?”
  • “What made the move intentional?”

[SAY]

“The outcome can stay the same and the rep can still count. This is not a story about a person being fixed. It is one moment handled differently.”

[CUT] Shorten debrief examples, not the second version or the “what stayed the same?” question.

3:04–3:10 — Introduce Radar; choose the route

Job: turn learning into selected moments without falsely claiming a team process exists.

[SAY]

“A Radar is a short, active list of moments you are choosing to notice, practise with and return to right now. It can include moments you want to handle better and moments you want to experience more fully.”

Route A — routine individual workshop

Use when no separately approved team module was collected.

[SAY]

“Today we are going straight to your own moments. We have not collected a team nomination for this session, and we will not manufacture one in the room.”

Proceed to 3:10.

Route B — approved team module exists

[GATE] Use only when the exact nomination item was approved, privacy-reviewed, collected and safely aggregated before the session.

[SAY]

“A separate optional question asked what this room might want to get better at together. Here are the two or three de-identified themes that appeared most often.”

[DO] Name themes only. Do not display raw wording or counts that make an individual identifiable.

[SAY]

“Respond privately and anonymously: does this room genuinely want one shared moment to work on? No agreement is required. No shared moment is better than a false one.”

[DO] Use only the separately approved anonymous response route. Do not ask for raised hands, spoken agreement, visible positioning or a majority vote. Proceed only when the approved decision rule is met without pressuring dissent; otherwise move to private Radars.

If yes, facilitate one sentence: “When [this happens], we will [observable next move].” Confirm an owner only if the approved follow-up process requires it and participants understand what that means. If no/unclear, say: “That is completely fine. Move to your own moments.”

[CHECK] Nomination is not consent or agreement. A majority does not authorize pressure on a minority. Unsafe work conditions are not turned into a team skill commitment.

3:10–3:16 — Write a private Radar

Job: build the approved three-moment personal Radar while preserving both life strands, practical planning and privacy.

[DO] Issue the current Radar worksheet. Model one neutral first-person example without using a participant's story.

[SAY — EXACT]

“Think about the person you are trying to become in this season of life.”

[SAY]

“Choose three personally meaningful moments in total. They can include moments you would like to handle better and moments you would like to experience more fully. For each, add one possible next move you could try. Three is an MFC pilot choice, not a scientifically exact number. Leave anything blank rather than force it. This page is yours: it is not read aloud, collected or inspected.”

[DO] Remain at the front or side. Do not circulate behind participants.

[CHECK] A moment is a recognisable scene or cue, not a goal, trait, analysis or solution. Offer the neutral moment bank if someone is stuck; do not ask them to disclose more.

3:16–3:22 — Choose one cue

Job: connect one moment to an optional reminder without promising behaviour change.

[DO] Issue cue card.

[SAY]

“Choose one moment—not the whole page. Attach it to something already in your week: the kettle, unlocking your phone, sitting at your desk, a seatbelt click. A card, photo, reminder or no reminder at all can be right. No format is better.”

[SAY]

“This is a visibility support, not a contract. Missing it does not break a streak and does not mean you failed.”

[CHECK] Do not describe this as habit stacking that will create a habit. It is an unvalidated support choice.

3:22–3:27 — Make return normal

Rewritten 2026-08-20, Hunter, direct decision — tone rewrite completing the Foundations pass, substance unchanged and re-verified against Essentials' equivalent beat (130, 1:25–1:29) after the committee's earlier catch.

Job: prevent lapse from being interpreted as failure, said like you mean it.

[SAY]

“Real talk: you're going to forget. You'll lose the cue, blank on what to do, hit a moment too big to pause in, or just not get an obvious opportunity that day. All of that is completely normal — none of it is failure.

One rep. Any moment. Whenever you notice you stopped noticing — that's the whole comeback.”

[SAY]

“And to be fair to yourself: sleep, movement, food, your health, your workload, the support around you and your environment all shape what's actually available to you in a moment. Not everything that gets in the way is yours to solve alone.”

[CHECK] Do not say “one rep is enough” as an efficacy claim. It means one is a complete valid attempt for today—not that one attempt creates lasting change.

3:27–3:30 — Close the teaching — the session's ending, weighted deliberately

Job: resolve the opening without claiming completion. Weighted 2026-08-20 alongside the engineered peak at 2:52–3:04 — per the peak-end research this pass is built on, the close carries disproportionate weight in what people actually remember, so it earns real warmth, not a brisk wrap-up.

[SAY]

“You're leaving today with the start of something real, not a finished skill — and that's genuinely the point. This was never a course to complete. It's a practice you get to come back to, as many times as you need to.

Today was your first rep here — not your last chance. I'm glad you came, and I mean that.”

[DO] A real pause before moving on — let this actually land, the same way the earlier peak moment did. Close the instructional session before introducing measurement.

3:30–3:34 — Offer the immediate form

Job: collect the approved immediate evidence without displacing the teaching or creating coercion.

[GATE] Use only the exact cohort-frozen Form 2 after its open privacy/legal, safeguarding, adviser and comprehension gates pass.

[SAY]

“There's one short form before you leave — this is just something everyone does at the end. It's completely anonymous, and it's genuinely fine if you'd rather not; choosing not to complete it doesn't affect anything. It takes about four minutes and asks what landed, what you can recall and what you may try. Please use the private link or paper route in front of you.”

[DO]

  • Do not ask participants to show a completion screen.
  • Do not hover, read responses or let the employer collect forms.
  • Keep the non-digital route equally available.
  • Follow the approved collection/storage process exactly.

7. If time slips

Never recover time by removing consent, privacy, breaks, the gap/feelings foundation, the three Stop–Shift–Do corrections, a real rep, private Radar safeguards or the close.

Recover in this order:

  1. shorten facilitator examples within the five skills;
  2. shorten HOS elaboration while preserving three parts and its boundary;
  3. use fewer optional retrieval repetitions while preserving both directions and three corrections;
  4. shorten contrast debrief examples, not the two versions;
  5. reduce optional pair discussion;
  6. protect the full six-minute Radar window and keep the approved instruction of exactly three moments; invite participants to leave a line blank rather than force it. Do not silently turn a one-moment start into the approved three-moment Radar or change the product because time slipped.

Do not run past the room's agreed finish without asking the host and participants. Form 2 sits after the teaching and may be completed through the approved later route if the cohort protocol permits.

8. Incident, disclosure and distress boundary

This guide deliberately does not invent a response procedure. The approved qualified-human procedure must state:

  • what the facilitator says and does if someone is distressed;
  • when and how the support contact is involved;
  • emergency and mandatory-reporting thresholds;
  • host responsibilities;
  • documentation and privacy rules;
  • the limits of confidentiality;
  • post-session follow-up responsibility.

General facilitation rule: do not invite details, diagnose, counsel, promise confidentiality beyond the approved policy, or improvise a referral. Preserve dignity, choice and the person's immediate safety while following the approved procedure.

9. Rehearsal protocol

Run one complete rehearsal with at least one observer and the actual deck/material sequence. Record:

Check Evidence required
Timing Actual start/end for every beat; both breaks protected; Form 2 outside 180 minutes.
Facilitator load Missed scripts, materials, transitions, privacy risks and recovery points.
Projection Furthest-seat readability in room light; light/dark fallback.
Retrieval Room can answer collectively without confusion or embarrassment.
HOS Three-part model stays within nine minutes and is not heard as diagnosis/neuroscience.
Practice Opt-out works visibly; no forced breath, eye closure, movement, pair work or disclosure.
Radar Individual and conditional team routes are unambiguous; facilitator does not read private work.
Measurement Exact approved forms, voluntary language, paper/digital parity and private collection work.
Safety Approved procedure is usable under pressure; all names/contact details are current.

Any material failure returns the unified package to revision. A rehearsal is operational evidence, not participant evidence.

10. After the session

  • Secure or destroy material only under the approved data procedure.
  • Record incidents and deviations through the approved route.
  • Record which workshop/form versions were actually used.
  • Do not report individual or identifiable participant material to the employer.
  • Keep team-nomination, workshop feedback and evaluation datasets within their approved purposes.
  • Schedule Form 3 at day 21, reminders at days 24 and 27, and closure at day 28 only through the approved participant-contact system.
  • Report only bounded participant-reported evidence. Do not infer causation, objective competence, wellbeing change, prevention or habit formation.

11. Current status

This guide is internally reconciled to the current operational arc and deck. It has not passed a fresh independent artifact review or a full timed room rehearsal. Qualified safety, legal/privacy, insurer, host, form-freeze and real-participant gates remain open.

Material 1 — Participant, privacy and support card

Front

Hard gate: no live participant may receive this card with a bracketed placeholder. An AI, designer, facilitator or host may not improvise the missing wording.

Material 2 — Workshop map

Half-Day Foundations

Three one-hour learning blocks, two 15-minute breaks, then an optional short form after the teaching close.

First — why none of us were ever taught this

We will start with the room's own words, make the mental-health/mental-fitness distinction, and explore thoughts, feelings and what can be practised.

Break — 15 minutes.

Second — the tool and what shapes access

Five skills. Stop–Shift–Do. A simple three-part model. A private State Check. Then one small Mental Rep.

Break — 15 minutes.

Third — use it and carry it into life

Try two kinds of shift, watch the same moment twice, choose exactly three personally meaningful moments for your private Radar, and take one optional reminder for one priority moment with you. Three is MFC's pilot structure, not a scientifically optimal count. Leave a line blank rather than forcing an answer; nobody checks whether you filled the page.

How today works

  • You never have to share anything personal.
  • Your private writing stays with you.
  • You can sit out, step out or ask for another way to take part.
  • “One” is a complete outcome. Nobody is checking whether you fill a page.
  • Toilets, water, access and support: [APPROVED VENUE DETAILS].

The meaning we use today

Mental fitness is how well we navigate life's everyday moments.

Mental health is how we are doing. Mental fitness is what we are able to do.

A mental rep is catching a moment and choosing your next move, on purpose, toward what matters. You may catch the moment before it happens, while it is happening, or afterwards. The outcome does not determine whether it counts.

Material 3 — The five skills

The five skills

Notice — notice what is happening inside you, around you, and between you and others.

Shift — create enough space to become workable — through your body, or through your thinking.

Choose — identify what matters and follow through.

Focus — put your attention where it matters and return it when it drifts.

Connect — connect better with yourself and others.

Workable means enough energy, steadiness and clarity for what this moment needs. It does not mean calm.

Most moments do not need all five. Naming the skills gives us something we can practise.

The five public sentences are locked. The seven deeper skills do not appear on this card.

Material 4 — Stop–Shift–Do

Front

Stop · Shift · Do

STOP — catch the moment.

SHIFT — create enough space where useful and available.

DO — make the next move with intention.

Production must use word + distinct shape + colour + fixed position. Red requires a noticing or catching glyph—not a stop palm. Amber uses a change-direction glyph. Green uses a next-move glyph.

Back

Three things the colours do not mean

Red is not freezing.

Stop means catching the moment. It does not mean halt or wait for permission.

Amber is not calming down.

Shift means creating enough space to become workable. Sometimes that is settling; sometimes it is becoming sharper or more connected. Some moments need no obvious Shift.

Green is not the right answer.

Do is the next move made with intention. The outcome does not determine whether the rep counts.

Material 5 — Human Operating System

A simple model for one useful question

This is a teaching model—not a map of the brain, not a diagnosis and not something you need to memorise.

Driver

What you can reach right now: noticing, paying attention, pausing, choosing and making your next move with intention.

Passenger

Thoughts, feelings, urges, what you want and need, memories, and how you read a situation.

The Passenger is not bad.

Engine

Your body: energy, tiredness, tension, breathing, hunger, sleep and recovery.

The point

What is shaping what is available to me right now?

What is making a useful response easier or harder to reach?

Context, support and what the situation asks of us matter too. This model explains access; it does not assign blame.

This current workshop material intentionally teaches three parts only. The six-part sheet in the superseded pack must not be issued with this guide.

Material 6 — State Check

State Check

Is my state too much, too little, or workable for this moment?

Too much — downshift towards workable.

Workable — probably no shift needed. Workable does not mean calm.

Too little — upshift towards workable.

“For this moment” is the point. The answer may change across a day. It is not a score, mood label or judgement about you.

Nobody asks you for the answer. It is yours.

No colours, scale, traffic-light layout or fourth-step framing.

Material 7 — Shift toolkit

Four places a shift can work through

A shift creates enough space to become workable. The same tool can bring us down or bring us up.

Body

Stand. Release your shoulders. Walk. Eat something. Step outside. Try a slower out-breath if it suits you.

Attention

Name what you can see. Feel your feet on the floor. Widen to the whole room. Narrow to one next task. Put the phone elsewhere.

Perspective

Is this a fact or a story? What else could be true? What would I say to someone I care about in this spot? What matters here?

Connection

Ask for two minutes. Text someone. Sit near a person you choose. Seek appropriate support.

Connection is only where it is safe and appropriate. Some situations need a boundary, support, system change or something outside this workshop—not a better individual response.

When we practise

You can watch instead. You do not have to close your eyes, control your breathing, stand, touch anyone, work with a partner or explain what happens.

If a strategy does not suit you, that is information about the strategy—not a failure in you.

Material 8 — Radar worksheet

Side 1 — My moments

Your Radar

A short, active list of moments you are choosing to notice, practise with and return to right now. It is not a diagnosis, goal list or test.

Think about the person you are trying to become in this season of life.

Before you write

  • This page is private. It is not read aloud, collected or inspected.
  • Leave anything blank that does not help.
  • The workshop asks you to choose three moments in total. Three is an MFC pilot choice, not a scientifically exact number.
  • A moment is a scene or cue you could recognise—not a trait, goal, explanation or solution.

My three moments

1. When / where / what is happening: __________

Handle better / experience more fully / another reason: ________

One possible next move: _________

2. When / where / what is happening: __________

Handle better / experience more fully / another reason: ________

One possible next move: _________

3. When / where / what is happening: __________

Handle better / experience more fully / another reason: ________

One possible next move: _________

What would make any of these moments genuinely easier?

Time, rest, permission, support, a boundary, a different room, less workload, or something being fixed that is not mine to fix:

Side 2 — Optional shared moment

A moment we have actually agreed to work on together

Use this side only if the room genuinely agreed. Nomination is not agreement. Leave it blank if there was no shared route or no real appetite.

When this happens: ___________

We will: _________

Who is involved and has agreed: ___________

A shared moment must not turn unsafe work, harmful behaviour, workload or a missing support into an individual skill problem.

One moment to carry forward

The one I am most likely to notice is:

The shared side may remain blank in the routine workshop. It is activated only when the approved team route in the facilitator guide is active.

Material 9 — Cue card

One reminder—yours

The moment I am watching for

One possible next move

An optional reminder already in my week

☐ This card somewhere I will see it

☐ A photo of my Radar

☐ One phone reminder in my own words

☐ Something else

☐ No reminder

Existing cue: ______________

Missing the reminder does not break a streak. It is not a contract and no one is checking.

One rep is a complete attempt for today.

If you forget or the reminder stops being useful, notice whenever you notice. Then choose the next rep.

  • Form 1 — baseline before teaching, approximately 3–4 minutes;
  • Form 2 — immediate after the 180-minute instructional close, approximately 4 minutes;
  • Form 3 — day 21, approximately 5–6 minutes, with reminders on days 24 and 27 and closure on day 28.

Do not copy form items into this pack. Use only the exact cohort-frozen instruments and approved privacy/contact process. The team-nomination item is not part of the routine D-0100 core.

  • [ ] HOS has three parts, not six;
  • [ ] State Check has no colour, scale or fourth-step styling;
  • [ ] Stop–Shift–Do uses word + shape + colour + position and no stop-palm glyph;
  • [ ] Radar has both handle-better and experience-more-fully strands;
  • [ ] shared Radar is explicitly optional and conditional;
  • [ ] private writing is never collected or inspected;
  • [ ] large-type and accessible digital copies exist;
  • [ ] every QR/digital route has a non-digital equivalent;
  • [ ] exact approved form, privacy and support versions are named in the cohort run sheet;
  • [ ] a greyscale, low-light and room-distance check has passed on the actual production outputs.

22 Half Day Foundations Unified Package Quality Review

Half-Day Foundations unified package — quality review

Review contract

  • Decision under review: may this package become the single internal Half-Day Foundations candidate and progress to independent review and timed rehearsal?
  • Artifacts checked: current operational arc, 80-screen HTML deck, current facilitator guide, current participant-material copy pack and deck preflight/assurance record.
  • Authority checked: D-0091, D-0094, D-0098, D-0100; K-04, K-05, K-07, K-08; founder/Gina and copywriting controls named in the preflight record; existing accessibility specification.
  • Not claimed: this is an integrated Quality Governor pass in the production context, not a fresh independent specialist review and not Hunter, Gina, creative, clinical, safeguarding, privacy/legal, insurer or host approval.

Verdict

PASS WITH CONDITIONS — internal progression only. The package is coherent enough to replace the previous split internal candidates and to progress to fresh independent review and a full timed rehearsal. It is not cleared for participant delivery.

Scope correction, 2026-08-13: “internal progression” does not mean the current architecture has been optimised or approved by Hunter. Before rehearsal is treated as the next design step, the package must pass the mandatory design-intelligence stage: compare credible architectures, screen the full bench, execute the relevant bounded challenges, reconcile them and revise the artifact. This review remains valid evidence of internal coherence; it is not evidence of optimality.

Gate-by-gate review

Gate Finding Status
Mission and product The package teaches ordinary, learnable mental-fitness capabilities in the approved Half-Day Foundations container. It does not present therapy or a clinical intervention. PASS
Evidence and claims The deck stays mainly at mechanism and teaching-model level; it avoids efficacy, prevention and outcome claims. Evidence rationales remain in the operational source rather than being projected as unsupported authority. Measurement language remains explicitly self-report and non-causal. PASS WITH CONDITION — source links and claim inventory must stay current through future copy edits.
Audience and language The sequence begins from recognition and a familiar health/fitness distinction before MFC terminology. It preserves the approved founder/Gina human premise, we/us framing, ordinary as well as difficult/joyful moments, and non-deficit language. PASS
Safety, safeguarding and privacy Choice, opt-out, private State Check/Radar and non-clinical boundaries are explicit. Qualified support/referral wording, participant privacy notice, form governance and the butcher-paper route remain unresolved and fail closed. PASS WITH CONDITIONS — qualified owners must close these gates before delivery.
Conceptual integrity Mental health versus mental fitness, five public skills, Stop–Shift–Do, three-part Human Operating System, State Check and mental-rep rules remain distinct. The routine D-0100 core is no longer falsely treated as containing a team-nomination item. PASS
Accessibility and inclusion Copy uses plain language; colour is redundant with word/shape/position; participation and writing may be passed or done privately. All 80 screens pass local desktop/mobile light/dark render checks. PASS WITH CONDITIONS — print artwork, projector/room-distance, washout, assistive technology, sensory load and actual cohort access needs remain untested.
Technical and operational Arc, deck, guide and participant copy pass the live cross-package verifier. Form 2 is explicitly placed after the 180 instructional minutes. The guide includes staging, recovery, incident and rehearsal procedures. PASS WITH CONDITIONS — actual forms, print files, room setup, film/two-facilitator asset and rehearsal evidence do not yet exist as approved production inputs.
Change control Old 44:56 guide/storyboard files point to current replacements; the 64-screen correction is archived; current artifacts declare product and fail-closed status. PASS WITH CONDITION — topic register, Current State and Hub must be reconciled in this same change cycle.

Prioritised findings

Blocking participant delivery

  1. The participant/privacy/support card contains deliberately unresolved text. No participant may receive it until qualified wording and cohort-specific routes are inserted and approved.
  2. Measurement forms are described but not approved cohort-frozen field instruments. Privacy, safeguarding, adviser, comprehension, storage, retention and access controls remain open.
  3. The butcher-paper opening may expose contributions within a table or room. A qualified cohort decision and rehearsal must choose or replace that route; the current guide correctly stops if it is unresolved.
  4. No full timed room rehearsal, projector-distance test, facilitator-load observation or real participant comprehension/accessibility test has been completed.

Required before the build can be called production-complete

  1. Convert the controlled participant-copy pack into accessible print-ready artifacts only after the blocked wording is approved. Copy completeness is not the same as production completeness.
  2. Name and stage the actual contrast-demonstration asset: approved film or a fully rehearsed two-facilitator scene. Do not improvise it on delivery day.
  3. Run a fresh independent artifact review across deck, guide and participant materials together. The prior specialist work informed the build but is not fresh assurance on this version.

Important design observations

  1. Eighty screens is not a quality target. The count is justified by projected-text legibility, retrieval pacing and one-job-per-screen. Independent review or rehearsal may add, combine or remove screens where evidence supports the change.
  2. The shared/team Radar is a separate governed module, not a normal feature of the session. The default route is now the individual Radar; this prevents the workshop from inventing data that the approved measurement core never collected.
  3. Form 2 occurs after the instructional close. Room booking, host expectation and participant consent therefore need to cover approximately four additional minutes even though those minutes are excluded from the 113:67 teaching balance.

Progression conditions

The current package may be treated as the sole internal candidate only while all of the following remain true:

  • the live package verifier passes;
  • participant-delivery status remains fail-closed;
  • future changes are made against the current operational arc and lifecycle pointers;
  • the next review is explicitly independent of this production pass;
  • rehearsal and qualified-human gates are recorded as evidence, not inferred from artifact quality.

Any failure returns the package to REVISE. Only Hunter or the named qualified owner may approve the decisions reserved to them.

23 Half Day Design Intelligence And Founder Finalisation

Half-Day Foundations — what we know, what we do not, and how we will optimise it

The honest status

Hunter has not approved a final Half-Day workshop. The 80-screen deck is the current internal candidate. It is assembled, internally aligned and locally rendered, but Hunter has not been shown and approved it as the strongest design. It has not completed the new design-intelligence stage, timed room rehearsal, participant testing or qualified-human gates.

The previous review answered: “Do the deck, guide and materials agree with the current recorded decisions?” It did not adequately answer: “Is this the best available way to help these people learn, remember and use mental fitness, and why?” That distinction is now explicit and binding.

What the existing work genuinely gives us

The vault contains more thinking than the previous handback made visible:

  • a Stage 7 teaching-and-outcomes spine;
  • Stage 8 evidence syntheses on context, cognitive load, in-session transfer, implementation and measurement;
  • Stage 9 design decisions;
  • founder and Gina language/copywriting controls;
  • market and category work, including RULER and other close analogues;
  • an operational workshop package, 80-screen deck, facilitator guide and participant-copy pack; and
  • explicit safety, accessibility, measurement and production limits.

That is a strong input corpus. It is not direct validation of this exact workshop. The research itself states there is no direct study of MFC's population, content, sequence and Half-Day format. Most learning evidence supports principles, not a scientifically optimal slide count or precise 113:67 teaching-to-experience ratio.

Three credible architectures now requiring comparison

Approach What it would feel like Why it may be strong Main risk
A. Current education-led sequence Understand the premise and model, retrieve it, then apply it Reduces the risk that activity is performed without meaning; matches Hunter's rejection of the earlier practice-heavy cut Too much explanation may consume attention and make 80 screens feel like a lecture
B. Experience first Begin with a safe lived contrast, then explain what happened Experience can create relevance and curiosity before terminology The vault does not support assuming broad “productive failure”; an unguided opening may confuse or expose participants
C. Recognition–experience–explanation spiral Repeated short cycles: familiar moment → micro-experience → explanation → retrieval → application May preserve meaning while reducing long blocks and creating repeated encoding/retrieval opportunities Could fragment the Framework or overload transitions if poorly facilitated

The current package is Option A, not the default winner. The staged professional review must compare these approaches and may recommend a hybrid. Slide count follows the chosen learning and room architecture; it is never the design target.

Load-bearing choices: current rationale and open challenge

Choice Current reason Evidence status What still has to be challenged or tested
Teach before extended practice Hunter found the 44:56 cut removed the meaning while retaining activities Founder judgement plus learning-design rationale Compare against a spiral, not only the rejected old cut
Segment and signal content Learning evidence supports segmenting, signalling, coherence and low-to-high fidelity Principle-level evidence Test the actual cognitive experience in the room; no evidence supplies a maximum slide count
Retrieval drill Retrieval practice supports memory better than passive rehearing Strong general learning principle; exact choral form not validated for MFC Test dignity, energy, recall and inclusion with intended adults
Immediate applied rep Mastery experience, feedback and contextualised practice plausibly support learning and self-efficacy Adjacent/general evidence; not proof of real-world transfer Test whether participants can perform the rep and later recognise a real opportunity
Radar cue and when–then plan Implementation intentions and cueing are a plausible bridge from intention to action Relevant mechanism evidence; MFC use untested Check burden, comprehension and whether a cue survives beyond the room
Human Operating System teaching model Creates a simple shared explanation of what can influence a moment MFC framework/teaching judgement, not a brain map or validated model Test whether it clarifies or adds avoidable conceptual load; justify its position and depth
Feelings as their own block The response—not the existence of a feeling—is the trainable boundary underpinning later teaching Founder/framework logic and safety relevance Review wording clinically and test whether it lands without invalidation or therapeutic implication
Shared/team Radar Attempts to connect individual practice to a group condition Design inference from collective implementation ideas; routine measurement module is not approved Test psychological safety, consent, facilitator capability, ownership and whether the host conditions exist
80 screens One screen per projected teaching/interaction job, with text broken for legibility Production rationale only Rehearsal and participant testing must decide whether screens aid or interrupt the experience
Half-Day container Recognisable commercial unit with breaks around roughly three hours of content Founder decision and commercial/delivery rationale; not an efficacy claim Buyer value, room energy and actual timing remain untested

Important intelligence that had not reached the build clearly enough

  1. RULER's strongest lesson is not its branded tools; it is implementation architecture. Adults and leaders learn and model the practices, tools remain visible in the environment, and repeated use is supported. Its evidence is largely developer-led, school-based and not proof for an Australian adult workplace workshop, so it is a comparator—not an answer.
  2. The market work recommends leaving reusable objects, not remembered ideas. The current cue card and materials partly do this, but the design has not yet been challenged against a clear “what remains visible and usable on Monday?” standard.
  3. Stop–Shift–Do is not novel as a loop. It sits beside DBT/MBSR STOP, RULER's Meta-Moment, ACT's Choice Point and similar interrupt–shift–act structures. MFC's defensible contribution is the integration, accessible language and moment-based practice architecture—not claiming to have invented the underlying loop.
  4. A single individual workshop cannot by itself establish organisational or population change. Manager/leader support, shared practice conditions and host behaviour may be necessary. The Half-Day must be clear about the boundary between the participant product and a later implementation or organisational layer.
  5. Measurement cannot repair an unclear theory of change. Each major beat should trace to a learning or behaviour mechanism and an intended observable signal. Attendance, satisfaction or one self-reported attempt cannot be called durable capability or social change.

Whole-team coverage, in founder language

The full 25-role bench has now been screened. Nineteen AI roles have a genuinely relevant bounded question for this optimisation, three matters remain qualified-human boundaries, and three roles are conditional rather than automatically run. This does not mean 25 agents have reviewed the deck. It means silence is no longer mistaken for irrelevance.

The staged work is:

  1. Purpose and outside world: Scout (market analogues), Sasha (category), Ronan (public-health and structural context), Grace (impact/theory of change), Iris (audience), Noa (strategy), with Talia controlling source lineage.
  2. How people learn and use it: Reed (learning architecture), Milo (behaviour and norms), Remy (habit/identity/practice), Piper (measurement), Quinn (experimentation), Kai (participation), Wren (experience/UX), Nova (language), Indigo (creative direction) and Cole (delivery reality).
  3. Boundaries and integration: accessibility/safeguarding AI screening plus qualified clinical and legal/privacy gates; Relay reconciles the professional disagreements into one proposal; Compass then reads the founder-facing result cold.

Equipment status, 2026-08-13: twenty of the 25 registered roles now have source-linked baseline professional packs. Piper, Ash, Kai, Noa and Compass have been equipped in this stage. A baseline is a credible starting toolkit, not proof of professional performance. Marlow, Harlan and Foster remain role-only because their conditional domains are not decision-bearing for this objective. Haven and Miller remain qualified-human boundaries; AI preparation cannot supply clinical or legal judgement.

Execution status, 2026-08-13: nineteen relevant AI role lenses have now reviewed the complete proposition in one accountable AI context. Their findings, evidence limits, strongest objections and reconciliation are recorded in 24-half-day-specialist-panel-and-architecture-decision.md. This is not equivalent to nineteen independent humans or separately trained models. Compass's cold read did not execute because this context had already seen the builder rationale; representing that as an independent founder-lens pass would be invalid.

Marlow joins only when a named employer/partner implementation is being designed. Harlan joins only for a government/policy pathway. Foster is not justified now because this failure can be fixed by clarifying and enforcing the existing team's workflow; no new agent is needed.

What happens before Hunter is asked to approve anything

  1. Run a genuinely fresh-context Compass cold read of the revised rendered build.
  2. Run the full timed room rehearsal and record the evidence rather than predicting it.
  3. Bring Hunter one viewable current build with the rationale, what changed and the genuine human or field gates still open.
  4. Only after Hunter views that build and explicitly approves it may the state become Hunter-approved for production. Participant delivery remains separately gated.

Current decision

The first design-intelligence revision is complete, not founder-approved. The system selected a guided recognition–explanation–application spiral, corrected the Radar, retrieval, language and participation defaults, and preserved the human gates. The next valid founder-facing action is a fresh-context cold read followed by showing Hunter the actual revised build and rationale.
