2.9 Material 6 — Worked-example sheet · NEEDS EDIT (minor, but one factual fix)

Grade 5.0 · Ease 76 · Fog 7.6 · avg 9.4 words · no sentence over 25. 481 words — the second longest material, and the one most likely to be read alone later. It reads well.

# Flagged Why Proposed rewrite
M6-1 "Parked in the driveway, before going inside: eleven words." — the quoted reply is "Sorry for the slow reply — I'm keen. Thursday or Saturday?" The reply is ten words as printed. It is only eleven if the reader expands "I'm" to "I am". A participant who counts — and the sentence invites counting — finds the sheet wrong. Small, but it is a printed factual error on a take-home artefact. "Parked in the driveway, before going inside: one line." — or keep a count and make it "ten words." Preferred: "one line." The count was never the point.
M6-2 "Sitting at the lights, they notice it" Two problems. "The lights" is UK/AU shorthand for traffic lights and is an EAL barrier. More importantly, it puts a traffic light into the session's scenery — nine minutes after D-0054 requires the traffic light to be named exactly once, as contrast. This is not a D-0054 breach (it is scenery, not teaching), but it is free retrieval interference in the one session built around distinguishing Stop from a red light. "Stopped in traffic, they notice it" — one word changed, both problems gone.
M6-3 "There's a familiar tightness about it — a small, low-grade dread." "Low-grade" is a medical collocation (low-grade fever/inflammation) and imports exactly the clinical register 11 §1 bans, on a sheet whose fidelity note says "nothing clinical." "There's a familiar tightness about it — a small, quiet dread."
M6-4 "It has a groove worn in it." Metaphor, unnamed, and genuinely opaque without the image of a worn record or path. It is also good writing. Keep the sentence and give it its gloss from the preceding line: "This has happened before. It's worn a groove — the same route, every time, getting easier to take."
M6-5 "I'm keen" (inside the quoted message) AU/UK colloquial for "I want to"; ambiguous or absent for many EAL readers. It is dialogue, so naturalism has some claim. Low priority. If changed: "Sorry for the slow reply — I do want to. Thursday or Saturday?" Recommend keeping the original; changing dialogue for readability makes it stop sounding like a message.
M6-6 "Not workable for a good reply — workable enough for a short one." Ellipsis: "a short one" refers back to reply across a dash. Mild. "Not workable for a good reply. Workable enough for a short one."

Locked content verified: the Stop / Shift / Do headings carry the locked wording; the "what would still have counted" block carries the mental rep's outcome-independence correctly. The closing paragraph is the claims guardrail and is kept word for word.

2.10 Material 7 — Guided practice sheet · NEEDS EDIT (one is a self-contradiction)

Grade 3.6 · Ease 84 · Fog 6.6 — the easiest prose in the corpus. One structural finding and three small ones.

# Flagged Why Proposed rewrite
M7-1 Heading: "4 · Connection / co-regulation" 11's own accessibility spec §1 says, in terms: "Where K-07 uses 'co-regulation', the participant sheet says 'Connection' and explains it in plain words." The sheet says "Connection / co-regulation." The material breaches its own stated rule, in a heading. "Co-regulation" is also four syllables of clinical vocabulary with no everyday meaning. "4 · Connection" — delete "/ co-regulation" from the participant sheet entirely. It belongs in the facilitator guide, where it already appears. This is the highest-priority edit on this material.
M7-2 "Nothing more mystical than that." "Mystical" is low-frequency, three syllables, and register-odd — it answers an objection the participant has not yet formed. "Nothing more mysterious than that." — or, preferred, "That's all it is."
M7-3 "There are four places to reach." "Reach" used intransitively with an abstract object is an unusual construction and the metaphor is unnamed. "There are four places to reach for." — one word, and the idiom becomes standard.
M7-4 "What's the most generous read of what just happened?" "Read" as a noun (= interpretation) is journalistic register and is a documented EAL stumble. "What's the kindest way to read what just happened?"
M7-5 "Be around people without having to perform." "Perform" is ambiguous — theatrical, or achieve-to-standard. Both readings exist and they point different ways. "Be around people without having to be on form." — or plainer: "Be around people without having to be at your best."

Confirmed correct and kept: K-08 rule 6's full opt-out is on the sheet itself, not left to the facilitator; "only where it is safe and appropriate" names the actual action per K-08 rule 5; no practice count, duration or frequency appears anywhere. The 38-word "over 25 words" flag from the automated scan is a false positive — it is four separate quoted questions concatenated by the extractor, not one sentence.

2.11 Material 8 — Radar worksheet · NEEDS EDIT

Grade 4.9 · Ease 79 · Fog 7.5 · avg 10.8 words · 6 sentences over 20. 546 words, the longest material, and the only one a participant fills in about their own life. Reading burden here is worse than the grade suggests because the reading is interleaved with writing and decision-making at 2h53 into a three-hour session.

# Flagged Why Proposed rewrite
M8-1 "Less on." (in the enabling-conditions example list) Two words, and among the hardest text in the corpus. "Less on" is AU/UK ellipsis for "less to do" and is close to unparseable for an EAL reader. It also sits in a list of otherwise concrete nouns. "Less to do."
M8-2 "Something being fixed that isn't yours to fix." Genuinely ambiguous even for a fluent reader: "something being fixed" reads first as something currently undergoing repair. The intended meaning — someone else fixing something that is not your responsibility — is recoverable only on a second pass. "Someone else fixing something that was never yours to fix."
M8-3 "Sitting around both sides." Sentence fragment with no subject, opening the ENABLING CONDITIONS block. A reader has to reconstruct "[These] sit around both sides [of this worksheet]." Also "sides" is doing double duty — sides of a page and sides of an argument. "These sit around both halves of your Radar — My moments and Our moments."
M8-4 "You can't put someone on your Radar without them knowing — that would just be a list of things you want other people to do differently." (25 words) At the hard cap, with the payload behind an em-dash. The second clause is the best line on the sheet and it is currently a subordinate afterthought. "You can't put someone on your Radar without them knowing. That would just be a list of things you want other people to do differently."
M8-5 "Naming it is still worth doing — it stops you treating a workload problem, an unsafe situation, or a missing support as a personal failing." (24 words) Safeguarding-adjacent — this is the participant-facing rendering of the source architecture's binding safeguard against reframing structural hazards as skill deficits. It must get clearer, not shorter. "A missing support" uses support as a count noun, which is administrative register. "Naming it is still worth doing. It stops you treating something as a personal failing when it isn't one — too much work, an unsafe situation, or the help you should have and don't." Longer, clearer, not weakened.
M8-6 "This isn't a separate Radar for each part of your life — it's tags on one list, so you can see where your attention is actually going." (26 words) Over cap; "tags" is unglossed interface vocabulary. "This isn't a separate Radar for each part of your life. It's one list, with labels — so you can see where your attention is actually going."
M8-7 "Choose a few moments → put them on your radar → live your life and do reps → notice what happened, adjust, keep going." Two issues. (a) Accessibility: screen readers handle "→" inconsistently — some announce nothing, some announce "right arrow", some announce "rightwards arrow" mid-clause. In the required plain-text and digital packs this line is degraded or unreadable. (b) lowercase "radar" here versus capitalised "Radar" everywhere else on the same sheet. Keep the arrow chain in the print version (it is visually good and the pathway is K-07's). In the plain-text and digital packs, render as a numbered list:
1. Choose a few moments.
2. Put them on your Radar.
3. Live your life and do reps.
4. Notice what happened, adjust, keep going.
Capitalise Radar in both.
M8-8 "A short, active list of the moments you're choosing to notice and practise with right now." "Active list" is unglossed — active as opposed to what? "A short list of the moments you're choosing to notice and practise with right now. Short, and current — not a list you keep adding to."
M8-9 "The word that matters here is 'agreed.' A moment only goes on this side if the other people have said yes to it." (23 words across two sentences — flagged by the scan as one) False positive. Already two sentences; the extractor joined them. No change. Recorded so it is not re-flagged.

Locked and safeguarding content verified untouched: the Radar prompt is verbatim; the three disclosure lines (not compulsory / three is MFC's design choice, not research-validated / one is a complete outcome) are unchanged and remain before the writing boxes; the "agreed" gate and the enabling-conditions block are unchanged in force.

2.12 Material 9 — Take-home cue card · NEEDS EDIT (minor)

Grade 3.5 · Ease 81 · Fog 6.9 · avg 6.5 words — the shortest sentences in the corpus. This is the artefact most likely to be read alone, weeks later, with no facilitator to ask. It is nearly there.

# Flagged Why Proposed rewrite
M9-1 Field label: "Stacked onto something already in my week" "Stacked" is MFC/behavioural-science jargon (habit stacking) leaking into participant copy unexplained — and it is a field label, so a participant must understand it in order to complete the card. This is worse than jargon in prose. "Something I already do that will remind me"
(the italic examples underneath — the commute, the kettle, the walk to the car — already carry the concept perfectly)
M9-2 "putting the kids down" (in the examples list) "Put down" has a euthanasia sense that is the primary sense for many EAL readers, and the phrase is genuinely alarming misread. Costless to fix. "putting the kids to bed"
M9-3 "Sunday admin" (same list) Narrow: a specific UK/AU middle-class weekly ritual, and "admin" is an abbreviation, which 11 §1 bans outright ("Abbreviations: none"). "paying the bills" — or delete; the list already has five items.
M9-4 "no format is better than another" "Format" is administrative register in a line about choosing a sticky note versus a phone alarm. "none of these is better than the others"

Locked line verified verbatim and untouched: "Most people's first attempts fade. That's expected, not failure. One rep, any moment, whenever you notice you stopped."

Kept exactly: "One rep is enough." · "You don't restart. There's nothing to restart. You just do the next one."

2.13 Material 10 — Disclosure and follow-up card · NEEDS EDIT (highest priority in the pass)

Grade 8.0 · Ease 61 · Fog 10.7 · avg 13.2 words · polysyllabic 13.6% · 4 sentences over 20.

The hardest material in the pack is the safeguarding card. That inversion is the single most important finding in Deliverable 2. Every other material can be misread at the cost of some learning; this one carries the non-clinical scope statement, the consent and opt-out rights, the privacy notice and the accessible-participation offer. A participant who cannot read it cannot exercise the rights it grants.

The constraint governing every rewrite below: K-08's claim boundaries and D-0015's six controls are the content, and none of it may be reduced, softened, or dropped. Every rewrite proposed here makes the card longer. That is the correct direction. 11's own storyboard already establishes the principle at Beat 1: "Brevity is never a legitimate reason to shorten safeguarding text."

# Flagged Why Proposed rewrite
M10-1 "Therapy, counselling, psychiatry, diagnosis, treatment, or crisis support." Six abstract nouns, five of them polysyllabic, as a bare list. This list may not be shortened — it is the K-08 scope boundary and every item is load-bearing. Keep the list verbatim. Add one plain line above it: "Today is a learning session. It is not medical or mental-health care." Then the list. Nothing removed; a plain-language handle added.
M10-2 "It doesn't replace any of those, and it isn't a substitute for care you're already getting or might need." (20 words; substitute and replace are near-synonyms, and substitute is the harder word) The sentence spends its length restating itself and then buries the operative instruction. "It does not replace any of those.
If you are already getting care, keep getting it.
If you need care, this is not it."
Three short sentences, stronger than the original, and it now tells the participant what to do rather than only what today is not.
M10-3 "Being here doesn't mean you're expected to share anything personal." Negated expectation inside a negated clause; heavier than it looks. "Coming today does not mean you have to share anything personal."
M10-4 "Anything you're asked to think about or write can stay private — you're never required to say it out loud or show anyone." (22 words) Two clauses across a dash; the second is the guarantee. "Anything you're asked to think about or write can stay private. You are never required to say it out loud, and never required to show it to anyone."
M10-5 "If you need a different way to take part — written instead of spoken, more time, a different seat, a break — tell a facilitator." (23 words, double-dash parenthesis before the instruction) The instruction (tell a facilitator) arrives last, after two asides. This is D-0015's accessible-participation control and its verb should not be at the end. "Do you need a different way to take part? Tell a facilitator. That could be written instead of spoken, more time, a different seat, or a break. You don't need to explain why." — the instruction moves to the front; a fifth item is added.
M10-6 "There's no course to finish, no programme to stay enrolled in, and no ongoing commitment." Triple negation plus enrolled and ongoing commitment — administrative register in the card's warmest paragraph. "There is no course to finish. There is nothing to sign up to. Nothing is expected of you after today."
M10-7 "Not answering it doesn't mean anything, and nobody will chase you." "Chase you" is idiom. It is also good, human, and its meaning is recoverable from "nobody will." Keep. Voice-protected. Recorded so it is not flagged again.
M10-8 "It asks whether you've used any of this and whether the Radar was any use." "used" / "any use" in one sentence. Cosmetic. "It asks whether you've used any of this, and whether the Radar helped."
M10-9 "[MFC standard privacy/data-use notice — insert MFC's approved current template. This card does not draft new legal wording.]" A production instruction sitting inside participant-facing copy. It must be replaced at production, and the readability of whatever replaces it is unassessed and unassessable here. Approved privacy templates are typically the hardest text an organisation produces. Not a rewrite — a gate. When the approved template is supplied, it must go through this same pass, and it will very likely fail it. Recommend MFC pair the legal notice with a plain-language summary above it ("In short: …"), which is standard practice and does not alter the legal text.

The disclosure sentence — deliberately not touched

"If something that comes up today feels bigger than this session, or something is troubling you — [PLACEHOLDER: what to do next]."

22 words with a nested conditional and a compound subject; on any other card this would be flagged for splitting. It is not flagged, and no rewrite is proposed, because the sentence and its completion are reserved to qualified clinical and legal input under D-0016 items 1–4, and 11 states in terms that "no facilitator, designer, host, or AI system may substitute generic crisis wording… or any other plausible-sounding text into that bracket." A readability edit to the front half of a sentence whose back half does not yet exist is exactly the kind of plausible-sounding change that record prohibits.

Consequence, stated in §2.14.

2.14 The readability gate cannot fully close, and here is why

11's open-gates table lists "Plain-language readability check — Not run. Required before print." This pass runs it for nine materials. It cannot close it for Material 10, and that is structural rather than a matter of effort:

  1. The D-0016 disclosure sentence is incomplete. Its readability depends entirely on the clinical and legal text that will complete it, which does not exist.
  2. The privacy notice is a placeholder. The approved MFC template has not been supplied and is likely to be the hardest text on the card.
  3. Both are reserved to qualified humans. Neither may be drafted, and therefore neither may be assessed, here.

Therefore: the readability gate on Material 10 is sequenced behind D-0016 items 1–4 and the privacy-template supply, and whoever drafts that text carries a plain-language obligation under K-08 rule 12 that this pass cannot discharge for them. Recommend the open-gates table in 11 be amended from a single "not run" row to two rows: "Plain-language readability check, Materials 1–9 — run 2026-08-03 (file 13)" and "Plain-language readability check, Material 10 — blocked behind D-0016 items 1–4 and privacy-template supply."

2.15 System-level findings across all ten materials

Five patterns that no single per-material edit addresses.

S1 · The em-dash parenthetical is the corpus's dominant rhythm, and it is the biggest single readability lever available. Main clause — qualifier — resumption, across all ten materials, at up to 3.4 per 100 words. It is excellent prose and it is a known barrier: low-literacy readers lose the main clause across the interruption, and screen readers vary in whether they pause at an em-dash at all (several read it as nothing, joining two clauses into one run-on). Recommendation: a single global pass converting roughly one em-dash in three to a full stop, prioritising (a) any sentence over 20 words, (b) every safeguarding line on Material 10, and (c) any sentence where the payload is behind the dash. Most of the individual rewrites above are instances of this one move.

S2 · The document breaches its own §1 jargon rule in two places, both of them in headings or tables rather than prose, which is why a prose-focused review would miss them: "activation" and "arousal" on Material 5's Engine row (§2.8.1), and "co-regulation" in Material 7's category heading (§2.10, M7-1) — the latter contradicting a rule that names that exact word and prescribes the exact fix. Both should be treated as compliance defects against 11 §1, not as style preferences.

S3 · "Facilitator" is undefined across five materials, two of them safeguarding instructions. One gloss on Material 1 fixes all five (§2.4, M1-3). Highest value-per-word edit in the pass.

S4 · Idiom density is inverse to reading grade. The three easiest-scoring materials — 3 (grade 3.0), 9 (3.5) and 7 (3.6) — carry the highest idiom load: in the tank, checked out, wound up, stacked, Sunday admin, get the blood going, most generous read, places to reach. This is exactly what short words and short sentences buy you, and it is invisible to every formula. Any future readability check on MFC materials should count idioms explicitly, because the score will not.

S5 · MFC vocabulary is correctly sequenced, and this is worth recording as a pass rather than a finding. Mental fitness is deliberately absent from Material 1 (issued 0:00) and first defined at 0:31. Workable is used on Material 2 (0:47) before being defined on Material 3 (1:41) — the one sequencing defect, fixed by M2-2. Rep appears on Materials 6, 8 and 9, all issued at or after 2:53, after the locked definition lands at 2:35. Radar appears on Materials 8 and 9, both after 2:53. Every other term is defined before it is used. Whoever built the issue plan got this right and it should not be disturbed by any of the edits above.

2.18 What a synthetic readability pass cannot establish

Stated plainly, because the gate this closes is narrower than its name suggests, and 11's own accessibility spec §10 sets the standard for this kind of disclosure.

  1. This is not a user test. No participant, of any literacy level, has read a single one of these materials. Everything above is a model of a reader, produced by a system whose own reading is nothing like the reading being modelled. A twenty-minute session with four adults at the target literacy level would find things this pass did not, and would contradict some of it.

  2. Readability formulae measure word and sentence length, and nothing else. Flesch–Kincaid cannot see idiom, ambiguity, cultural assumption, register clash, missing referents, or the difference between a familiar long word and an unfamiliar short one. §2.6 is the proof: the highest-scoring material in the corpus needed four edits. Do not report the grade levels in §2.1 as the result of this pass. The findings are the result; the numbers are the least informative part of them.

  3. 11's own spec requires a pass "run by someone who did not write them." A-08 and A-12 are credited co-authors of the materials being assessed here. This pass is therefore less independent than the specification asks for, and the spec's requirement is not discharged by it. It should be treated as a thorough author-side pass that surfaces most defects cheaply, with a genuinely independent pass still owed.

  4. Reading conditions are not modelled. These materials are read standing up, in a room with strangers, at 2h53 into a three-hour session, possibly after a poor night's sleep, on paper whose final typography, contrast and stock are not yet chosen. Material 8's real burden is much higher than grade 4.9 for that reason. Effective readability is a product of copy and typography and timing, and this pass only touched the first.

  5. EAL flags are inferences, not observations. Every "an EAL reader would stumble here" above is a judgement about a category of reader, not a report of anyone stumbling. EAL is also not one population: a Portuguese speaker, a Mandarin speaker and an Arabic speaker will find different things hard, and idioms that are transparent in one first language are opaque in another.

  6. Nothing here speaks to Easy Read. 11 records the absence of an Easy Read version as an open gap, and this pass does not close, narrow, or substitute for it. Plain English at Year 6–8 and Easy Read are different products for different readers.

  7. Cross-cultural applicability (F7) remains open. Several findings above are about UK/AU idiom specifically, which is a symptom of the same unresolved question and not a treatment for it.

  8. Material 10 cannot be signed off at all — §2.14.

Recommended real test, when D-0016 allows one. Six adults, recruited for a spread of literacy and English-language background, none connected to MFC. Each is given the pack cold and asked to read aloud and say what each material is asking them to do. Record where they stop, re-read, or guess. That is thirty minutes per person and it will find more than everything above.

05 Specialist Execution Record

Specialist execution record — two-format workshop build

Recorded against the five-part binding rule in 09-specialist-execution-binding.md. A specialist counts as routed only when: (1) spec loaded and method followed, (2) required inputs supplied, (3) independent context, (4) structured outputs produced as real artefacts, (5) recorded honestly, including partial execution.

The failure this record exists because of

First attempt at this objective failed the binding rule outright. The specialists were named in a task list and then skipped; a single-authored answer was written inline and presented as considered work. Hunter caught it: "you need to workshop this. You need to test this with your agents." Recorded as L-025. A second, compounding failure followed in the synthesis of the corrected pass — a specialist's invented illustrative number was attributed to Hunter as something he had confirmed. Recorded as L-026, with a new source-tracing step added to Compass's method.

Both are logged in 80-learning/founder-signal-register.yml. The register now reports hunter_is_the_only_detector at 4 occurrences and reduce_founder_dependency at 5 — both OVERDUE by its own 3+ rule.

Material specialist disagreements — carried, not smoothed

  1. A-10 vs. the adopted design on Human Operating System scope. A-10's professional position is that the HOS should not be a taught segment at all, only a compressed framing device, because no behaviour on the outcomes spine requires a participant to reproduce the model. The adopted design does not follow this. Hunter has stated the HOS is an important teaching metaphor (L-026) — that is the deciding input, and it aligns with K-07, which names the HOS as a first-class architectural layer and as a teaching model participants never need to reproduce. A-10's objection is preserved here rather than resolved away: it is a real cost, paid deliberately. Allocation landed at 18 min of 180 in the 3-hour (10%) and 6 min of 60 in the 1-hour, with three of six components taught at the shorter length.
  2. A-09/A-16 on 1-hour viability. Judged unable to support habit formation as a standalone equivalent. Accepted and acted on — the 1-hour is positioned and measured as an education-and-entry format, not a peer product. This matches Hunter's own position independently.
  3. A-11 on follow-up timing. Recommended 6 weeks over the approved 3–4. Accepted, with the 3-week non-outcome re-entry touch as mitigation. Changes the timing of an essential function and is therefore recorded in the closing decision record.
  4. A-12 on digital delivery. Identified a safeguarding gap outside D-0016's six matters. Accepted and escalated as a new item 7, blocking the digital 1-hour only.

Honest limitation

This record proves the specialists ran in independent context and produced their outputs. It cannot establish that their judgement was correct. The bench remains at CONTROLLED_PILOT maturity with limited live evidence, and A-04 remains accountable for the integration regardless of what any specialist returned.

Final 04 Delivery Models

Delivery Models: What MFC Delivers

Executive Summary

MFC delivers through a ladder of formats — from one hour to four hours — all built around the same core measurement. The measurement is the constant; the format is the variable. In-person delivery is the stated preference and the current focus. Virtual delivery is designed next. Everything else is tested against a single design rule: any format that cannot run the core measurement is not an MFC offering.

This document describes what's built today (Foundations and Essentials), what's being built next (the one-hour digital session), and why other approaches don't survive testing.

1. The Core Design Principle

The measurement is the constant. The format is the variable. A format that cannot carry the measurement is not an MFC offering.

This protects the evidence base while we build multiple formats. It's what makes a ladder one thing, not a catalogue.

What "The Constant" Means

Every MFC offering runs this minimum measurement:

  • Baseline (before): Can you retrieve this skill when you notice you need it? — the primary matched item
  • Then-test (at follow-up): Rate that same question again, to catch bias in how your awareness changes
  • End of session: Does practice in the room move it? — a post-session repeat of the primary matched item
  • Matched retrieval (baseline): A second matched item, also captured at baseline, — to measure whether noticing itself improves
  • Three weeks later: Does it stick? — the primary matched item at follow-up, plus the then-test above
  • The harm item: Did this make anything worse?
  • The referral line: If distress came up, where could you go? — Routing only, no data recorded

This runs on every format. No exceptions. No opt-out. It takes ~2.5 minutes per timepoint.

Longer formats (Foundations, Essentials) add:

  • In-session protected block with situational judgement, linkage code, and the full measurement-instrument design
  • Follow-up at three weeks in depth
  • E-items measuring whether the client commitment obligations held

2. What's Built Today

V1 — Foundations Half-Day, In-Person

What it is: 4 hours in-person, same location, MFC-delivered to a group typically 15–20 people from the same organisation (working assumption — founder-set operating parameter, not externally sourced; see §7 for the reasoning).

The method (corrected 2026-08-13 — this description had drifted from the actual built sequence; see [[90-meta/controlled-automation-v1/topic-control/canonical-topic-register.yml|workshop-delivery topic record]] for the current canonical build): the Human Operating System (three-part model), Stop-Shift-Do, the five skills (Notice, Shift, Choose, Focus, Connect), a State Check, paired/guided practice, a contrast demonstration, one Mental Rep chosen per participant to use after the session, and Radar — run either as an individual reveal, or as a team-aggregate reveal only when an approved, privacy-reviewed team module was actually collected. "Board narrowing," a "full-pass sheet," and a "manager briefing" are not part of the current build and should not be cited elsewhere as current MFC method.

Measurement: Full instrument, protected in-session block, baseline, post, three-week follow-up.

Who delivers: Hunter, the founder, one-facilitator capacity limit.

Founder hours: 11 hours direct (prep, delivery, analysis, report), plus materials/setup (source: the pricing research).

Loaded cost: ~$1,228 per session | Standing price: $2,500 base + $95/person | Margin: 2.18×–3.22× depending on headcount (source: the pricing research)

Why this works: This is the full system in the full time. Pair beats work. Reading the room works. The live rep on your own moment actually happens. The evidence of transfer is cleanest here because the environment is intact (you're with your colleagues, you're going back to the same workplace, the manager is in the building).

What breaks it: Travel distance >1 hour (the 1.0 hr travel line becomes unrealistic). Organisations without a room. Groups under 6 (compliance risk, consent complexity).

V2 — Essentials 90-Minute, In-Person or Virtual

What it is: 90 minutes, taught in-person or digitally, to a group 6–15 people (working assumption — founder-set operating parameter, not externally sourced; see §7 for the reasoning).

The method: Stop-Shift-Do, three public skills (not five), one paired practice, the board narrowing, one mental rep, manager briefing.

Measurement: Full instrument, protected in-session block, baseline, post, three-week follow-up.

Founder hours: 4.5 hours in-person (or 3.2 hours virtual, reflecting ~1.3 hours of reduced travel/logistics) (source: the pricing research).

Loaded cost: ~$500 in-person, ~$324 virtual | Standing price: $700–$1,200 in-person (by size band), $1,000 virtual | Margin: 1.10×–2.18× depending on band and format (source: the pricing research)

Why this works: Shorter entry point for small teams. Still carries the full measurement. Virtual version reaches people who can't release everyone at once or aren't co-located.

What breaks it: Groups under 6 (same consent/compliance risk as V1). Organisations without a named manager commitment (the method depends on follow-through).

3. What's Being Built Next

V5 — One-Hour Live Digital Session, Individually Bookable

What it is: 60 minutes live, delivered digitally, in MFC-scheduled cohorts of 6–12 strangers or to individuals alone. The bottom rung of the ladder — enterable by one person.

The method: Stop-Shift-Do, one public skill (retrieval under load), one live rep on the participant's own moment, the mental rep, no manager layer.

Measurement: Core measurement only (the constant, no protected block). Baseline, post, three-week follow-up.

Founder hours: Estimated 1.5 hours direct per session + ~30 hours build/design (build once, run many times) (estimate — the delivery-models research flags V5 as not yet built, ~20–30 founder hours estimated).

Loaded cost: ~$255 per session across 20 seats (source: the lead-generation funnel research) | Standing price: $25–35/seat (source: the delivery-models and lead-generation research) | Why this works: Reaches individuals who have no organisational sponsor and no 90 minutes to release. Community events, conference hallways, people scrolling LinkedIn. Honest message: education plus a practical tool, not a full workshop. Produces evidence in the form of "reached and measured individuals who used the skill," not "changed an organisation."

The safeguarding exception: This is the most safeguarding-exposed configuration in the entire ladder. A participant sits alone online, with no colleague beside them, no manager to escalate to, no employer with duty-of-care structures. This format requires:

  • Jurisdiction check at booking (Australia only)
  • Named referral pathway shown before the session, not after
  • Facilitator protocol for a distress disclosure with no employer to escalate to
  • A decision about whether MFC collects enough contact detail to act on a disclosure at all (which creates tension with the anonymity the format promises)

These are preconditions of offering V5 — not of building it. The build can proceed. The individual-booking channel cannot open until the safeguarding annex exists and the safeguarding review's items 1-2 (clinical-governance input on distress response and legal review) have qualified input.

4. What Doesn't Survive Testing

E1 — Asynchronous / Self-Paced Only

Why rejected: No baseline that is not self-administered on an unknown day. No protected moment for the harm item to be seen by anyone. No referral line that reaches a human. A format where a distress disclosure lands in an unmonitored form is worse than no format at all.

E2 — Cue Placement in the Environment Alone

Why rejected as a standalone offering: Not a delivery vehicle. It teaches nothing and measures nothing.

Why retained as a free add-on: Cues (signage, prompts, nudges where the moment happens) are genuinely well-matched to retrieval under load. Added to every in-person and virtual format at no additional charge.

E3 — Long Format (Essentials or Foundations) Sold to Individuals

Why rejected: Essentials and Foundations both depend on a team that goes back to the same workplace. You cannot design a follow-up commitment for an individual who came to a ticketed event. (The short V5 format works for individuals because it never claims there will be follow-up.)

Partially reinstated: V5 (the one-hour digital session) is sold to individuals, but the short format that never claims environment support, not a longer one.

5. The Five Tests Every Format Faces

Test What it means Source
T1: Does the taught procedure survive? Stop-Shift-Do, the five public skills, the mental rep survive intact. Most at risk remotely: paired practice, reading the room, the live rep on your own moment MFC's framework-architecture note
T2: Does the measurement survive? The core constant at minimum. Anonymity, linkage code, N ≥ 20 reporting floor must hold the measurement research
T3: Founder hours per session Reported as prominently as dollars, because hours are the binding constraint the pricing research — Hunter can deliver max twice a day, not every day
T4: Which segment does it serve, and what's its role in the funnel? Different entry points bring different organisations in. Assessed as demand mechanism, not just a delivery menu the demand-generation and free-offer research, founder input
T5: How delegable is it? A short, well-specified format is the one someone else can eventually run. This is the first real answer to founder dependency Founder input

6. In-Person Is the Stated Preference

Hunter, directly: "we would rather do it in person because that's the best intervention from what we've seen."

The hedge ("from what we've seen") is his and is correctly placed — it's experience, not evidence. But the evidence on remote skills transfer is actually mixed: meta-analyses don't show remote as categorically worse, but don't show it as equivalent either. The safest read is: every remote option is a weaker version offered so people who cannot be reached in person still get something, not an equivalent.

In-person Foundations is the aspirational product. It's where the full system comes alive, where you read the room, where the live rep on your own moment actually happens. But virtual exists because a delivered-in-your-own-setup 90 minutes is better than zero.

7. The Room-Size Decision

Essentials: 6–15 people. Foundations: 6–20 people.

(Working assumption — founder-set operating decision, not an externally sourced figure; reasoning below is the source.)

These are hard caps. Why:

  • Below 6: Consent gets complicated (every person identifiable), anonymity gets impossible.
  • Above 15 (Essentials): The method depends on reading the room, paired practice with space to move, the board-narrowing exercise working at scale. At 20, Essentials becomes a presentation, not a workshop.
  • Above 20 (Foundations): Per-head margin drops (more people, same facilitator hours), and the measurement load grows (you're collecting from more participants, follow-up becomes harder to manage, the report gets harder to interpret).

8. The Client Commitment — Measured, Not Just Claimed

Every session requires the organisation to make three named commitments:

  1. Voluntary attendance — demonstrably so. Form asks: were you directed to attend, or did you choose to?
  2. One named real opportunity — named before the session, in the next three weeks. Form asks: did that situation actually happen?
  3. One named manager asks once — within three weeks. Form asks: did anyone ask whether there was anything you wanted to use?

These are measured at three-week follow-up and reported split by whether they happened.

This is not an environment layer (the facilitator leaves; the manager stays, but only for these three things). It's a delivery precondition measured as a covariate. If the preconditions don't hold, MFC does not accept a second cohort to that organisation until they're renegotiated.

The consequence is deliberately small: No penalty. No refund. No clause with teeth. A one-facilitator charity's only real enforcement is whether it agrees to come back.

9. Scaling — When and How

MFC is one facilitator. One facilitator can deliver:

  • Twice per day maximum (one morning, one afternoon) (source: the pricing research's founder capacity note)
  • 5 days a week = ~10 sessions per week at absolute maximum (derived from the above)
  • Realistically, ~2–3 sessions per week (estimate, unverified — accounting for prep, analysis, report writing, travel)

So the question is not "how do we scale delivery" but "what does a working first cohort look like, and how do we prove it?"

The ladder is designed so that V1 (Foundations) establishes credibility, V2 (Essentials) builds evidence volume, and V5 (the digital one-hour) reaches cost-effectively without requiring a room. It's not a growth plan. It's a diversification plan around one person's capacity.

Delegability (T5 above) is the real answer to founder dependency. A short, well-specified format (like V5 or V2 Essentials) is something someone else could learn to run. A 4-hour workshop that depends on reading the room and the live rep is harder to hand over. So the order is: build proof with Foundations (hard to delegate), systematise Essentials (medium difficulty), test the one-hour digital (most delegable). Once V5 is proven and systematised, someone else can run it, and suddenly the capacity problem changes shape.

That's in year two or beyond. Year one is one facilitator proving the method works.

10. Delivery Timeline and What Needs to Close First

Nothing is delivered to a participant until:

  1. The safeguarding review has named owners and dates. All six safeguarding matters must have someone responsible and a target date, not "TBD."
  2. V5's safeguarding annex exists (if V5 is offered to individuals).
  3. Clinical governance and legal review have run on the distress-response protocols.

Once those close, the timeline is:

  • Month 1: Foundations and Essentials delivery begins (grant-funded and corporate case-study cohorts)
  • Month 2–3: Build V5 in parallel
  • Month 3–4: V5 launches to individuals and organisations
  • Month 4+: Accumulate measurement data, begin publishing findings

This is aspirational and depends on grant funding arriving and the safeguarding review closing. If either doesn't happen, the timeline slips.

25 Half Day Whole Bench Reconciliation And Closure

Whole-bench reconciliation and closure

Why this document exists

Two bounded evaluation-pilot panels ran on 2026-08-13:

  1. assurance-2026-08-13/ — 18 unique task packets/reviews, an independent A-24 coverage challenge, and a SYS-04-integrated-recommendation-final.md reconciliation. Contract-complete for its scope.
  2. assurance-2026-08-13-evaluated-panel/ — 24 further reviews plus a genuinely independent checker pass (independent-check.md) that returned REVISE, found six Major defects (source-lifecycle drift, an active D-0100/measurement conflict, an active participation-route conflict, overstated transfer/impact language, a missing D-0099 record, and a broken manifest evidence path), and set a six-step correction-spec.yml before the build could be called reconciled.

Neither panel was ever closed by a schema-v2 routing record, so under this vault's own contract (specialist-call-contract.md) neither counted as registered specialist assurance — this is the literal gap Hunter named: real bounded work existed, but it was never mechanically recorded, so it could not be checked, trusted, or built on by a later session.

This document is that closure: it verifies what was actually applied to the live artifact, closes what can be honestly closed, and names — rather than hides — what remains open.

Genuinely open, named rather than hidden

  1. Fourteen non-contract-complete packets (A-11, A-13, A-17, A-18, A-19, A-20, A-21, A-23, A-24, A-25, A-26, H-01, H-02, SYS-03 from the evaluated panel) were not rerun to full five-layer/ eleven-section contract completeness. Their substantive findings were independently reproduced against the live artifact by this reconciliation and by the original independent checker where the finding produced a concrete artifact change (ARC-01, ARC-02, SOURCE-01); those are trusted on that independent basis, not on the packet's own authority. Findings that did not produce an independently-verifiable artifact change (A-17, A-21, A-25, A-26, SYS-03 — all non-change or conditional-defer dispositions) remain reasoned but not contract-complete.
  2. The package verifier is not yet a semantic regression guard (MANIFEST-01, still open) — it can report PASS without checking for the specific defects this cycle found and fixed.
  3. Compass's actual recommendation is unmet. The corrected canonical page is not the same as the beat-by-beat founder-decision interface FL-01 asked for (participant job / why present / authority class / strongest objection / evidence limit / next test, per artifact beat). Presenting the current package to Hunter as-is repeats exactly the failure Compass named: he would have to detect what's approved-decision vs. design-judgement vs. untested hypothesis himself.
  4. Rehearsal, render, accessibility, qualified-human and participant-testing gates are unchanged by this document and were never claimed as specialist-loop items.

Decision

The specialist panel is now formally closed, contract-registered, and honestly bounded — not "informal lenses," and not a second rebuild. The corrections it drove are independently verified live in the artifact. What is not being claimed: that all 25 roles ran fresh contract-complete reviews, or that the build is founder-decision-ready as currently packaged.

Recommended next action (not a new panel, not a rebuild): build the beat-by-beat founder-decision interface FL-01 specified — this is bounded production work on the existing candidate, not new specialist assurance — then run one fresh Compass cold read against that interface before bringing Hunter the viewable build. This is the smallest step between where the build now genuinely is and Hunter being able to make his decision without doing the reconciliation work himself.

Learning disposition

candidate_update — a bounded panel's findings can be independently verified against the live artifact even when several packets fall short of full contract completeness; that verification, not the packet's format alone, is what should determine whether a finding is trusted. Proposed for specialist-learning-register.yml after this record is checked.

Independent check — fresh evaluated-pack Half-Day panel

Date: 2026-08-13

Decision: REVISE

Why this is REVISE

The panel found a real and consequential source-of-truth defect: workshop-package.html is identified as the current canonical arc but contains active measurement, participation and impact logic that conflicts with the current deck, guide, participant materials and approved decisions. I reproduced those conflicts at the frozen hashes.

The proposed response—reconcile the existing package rather than rebuild the workshop—is directionally correct and is the smallest effective product response. The panel itself is not yet complete or contract-clean, however: it contains 24 of the 25 registered roles, has no SYS-04/Relay packet or reconciliation output, omits the controlling D-0099 framing decision, and labels multi-role work from two producer contexts as separately bounded specialist execution without enough evidence to substantiate that label. The current package verifier also returns PASS despite the semantic conflicts and a broken manifest evidence path.

There is no Critical finding at the current internal_candidate stage because participant delivery remains visibly blocked. The same participation and data-design conflicts would become Critical if the package were used to brief delivery or field forms without correction and qualified-human clearance.

What genuinely passes

  1. Frozen corpus integrity: all four current artifact hashes are accurate.

A-19 Ronan Preserve structural routes; relabel wider ripple as hypothesis. Required and supported.
A-20 Grace Use a proximal causal chain; remove unsupported downstream leaps. Required and supported.
A-21 Marlow No change without named partner; require cohort/host run sheet later. Valid conditional defer.
A-22 Iris Preserve audience/cultural uncertainty; run varied participant testing. Required; AI cannot settle interpretation.
A-23 Talia Reconcile canonical identity, supersession and projection. Required and supported.
A-24 Quinn Stage tests by uncertainty and preregister interpretation. Required and supported.
A-25 Noa Reconcile and test; do not expand or rebuild now. Relevant and supported.
A-26 Harlan No policy change; rerun only on a live policy/government trigger. Valid refusal.
H-01 Haven Qualified clinical/safeguarding questions only. Correct human boundary.
H-02 Miller Qualified privacy/legal data-map questions only. Correct human boundary.
FL-01 Compass Founder-decision interface needed; Hunter approval not inferred. Relevant, but this is not Hunter viewing.
SYS-03 Foster Improve semantic projection controls; do not create a new agent. Need test correctly fails for a new agent.
SYS-04 Relay Named as future reconciler; no packet, review or disposition exists. Missing. The full-bench/panel loop is incomplete.

No role should be added merely to increase activity. All 25 roles do need a recorded disposition; SYS-04 is the only missing one. The optimal response is not 25 independent product edits. It is 24 reasoned domain dispositions followed by one genuine Relay reconciliation after this check and any corrected producer outputs.

Independence and activity audit

  • The consequence/strategy receipt explicitly says one performer context applied fourteen packs. The architecture synthesis says ten outputs were produced fresh but does not record a comparable producer-context receipt. The two halves appear to be separate producer passes and their shared finding is independently reproducible.
  • The records do not establish that each of the 24 roles was a separately executed specialist context. Under the controlled call contract, one producing context applying multiple role perspectives is normally same_context_role_lens, unless distinct execution evidence exists. The current bounded_specialist_review labels therefore overstate execution assurance.
  • Fourteen terse Markdown task packets omit several required five-layer preflight fields; their corresponding reviews omit required metadata/frontmatter and do not consistently state professional principles, alternatives, what would change the view and learning disposition. Backfilling those fields after execution would not prove that they were supplied before the call.
  • The no-change/refusal outputs themselves are not manufactured activity: they name a trigger and refuse unsupported work. The defect is execution labelling and traceability, not that every role produced a change.
  • FL-01 asserts fresh-context independence but the folder contains no machine-verifiable context receipt. Preserve its useful objection, but do not treat it as the final rendered Compass cold read required before Hunter review.

Findings by severity

Critical

None at the current internal-candidate stage. Participant delivery remains blocked. If the current canonical HTML were operationalised, the active participation and data-design conflicts would require STOP until corrected and qualified-human gates were passed.

Major 1 — The specialist loop is incomplete and execution assurance is overstated

Evidence: 25 roles are registered; this folder contains 24 task packets and 24 reviews. SYS-04 has neither. Both synthesis files explicitly await SYS-04 reconciliation. Fourteen packets/reviews use a reduced format that does not satisfy the complete controlled call contract, and the consequence receipt describes one performer context for fourteen roles.

Consequence: there is no authoritative accept/narrow/reject/unresolved/escalate disposition, no verified learning return, and no defensible basis for saying the complete evaluated panel has run.

Smallest effective response: do not regenerate the workshop or invent missing expertise. Correctly classify the two producer halves as same-context role-lens panels unless distinct execution receipts exist; rerun only the contract-incomplete decision-bearing calls that must carry separate specialist assurance; then give SYS-04 one complete reconciliation packet containing the producer outputs, this independent check, minority concerns and exact current fingerprints. Preserve all rejected and deferred advice.

Major 2 — Active measurement architecture conflicts with D-0100

Reproduced in workshop-package.html: the Half-Day and Introduction measurement views call themselves “Finalised” and “decided,” retain WHO-5, a personal-facts backup code, routine team nomination, day-90 material and near-100% response claims (anchors include lines 722–724, 737–748, 807–826, 942–983, 1052–1095, 1421–1475, 1527, 1574–1586 and 1611). D-0100 removes WHO-5 and broad non-core research from the routine first-pilot core, requires a random system ID with separately controlled key or unlinked anonymous fallback, and does not establish near-complete response.

Active versus historical: this is a genuine active conflict, not harmless history, because the views are labelled finalised/decided/current and the manifest names the HTML as the canonical arc.

Cross-artifact check: the current guide and materials point to D-0100 and correctly keep exact forms unapproved; the deck contains only a bounded optional Form 2 screen. The defect is concentrated in the canonical HTML and its provenance, not the current delivery script.

Smallest effective response: replace the active measurement projections in both format views with one concise D-0100-derived current summary and links; preserve superseded detail only behind an explicit historical label that cannot be mistaken for an operational specification. Do not design new forms.

Major 3 — The canonical HTML instructs a participation route that the current guide forbids

Reproduced: workshop-package.html line 562 allows “a show of hands or a quick read of the room” for shared-Radar appetite. The current guide at the 3:04–3:10 Route B section requires a private anonymous response and explicitly prohibits raised hands, spoken agreement, visible positioning and majority vote. The deck’s “A private choice” screen agrees with the guide.

The line-619 “Butcher's paper, not anonymous cards” rationale is more nuanced: it labels itself a design argument and says safety is unresolved. It is therefore not an unlabelled operational instruction by itself. It still creates a major retrieval risk because it valorises shoulder-reading inside a page whose footer calls it the current arc and room plan, while the active walkthrough at line 415 and current guide prohibit that behaviour.

Smallest effective response: replace the active shared-Radar appetite instruction with the current private/anonymous rule. Recast the butcher-paper paragraph as explicitly superseded historical rationale or move it to dated design history; do not delete the reasoning. The conditional shared route may remain only when cohort-specific privacy/access/participation approval and an approved decision rule exist.

Major 4 — Active language overstates behavioural transfer and wider impact

Reproduced: lines 364–365 universalise what adults were taught and link untrained moments to burnout, conflict, sector burden and fewer costly moments at scale; lines 388–389 call practice no-time and a habit-stacking mechanism; line 502 says participants have done thousands of reps; lines 525–528 imply easy-moment practice will be available in hard moments; line 588 repeats no-extra-time; line 595 says “a practice you keep”; evidence rows 697, 700–702 present conditional mechanisms with causal confidence; equivalent Introduction claims appear at 1179–1218.

Cross-artifact check: the current guide explicitly rejects thousands-of-reps and habit guarantees, recognises attention/effort cost, and the current deck uses “practice you can return to.” Participant materials do not carry the scaled claims. The panel correctly located a canonical-arc conflict, not a package-wide need to rebuild the teaching sequence.

Smallest effective response: mirror the bounded guide/deck wording; distinguish approved organisational position, mechanism-informed design, working contribution hypothesis and untested outcome. Add one proximal logic chain without claiming causation. Preserve the movement ambition as a testable hypothesis with required conditions and rival explanations.

Major 5 — The governing decision set omits D-0099 and misstates the safeguarding authority

Evidence: the frozen receipt and many packets treat D-0016 as the current approved gate. D-0099 is the later controlling decision: it closes/supersedes D-0016’s formal strategy/build-order framing while explicitly leaving the six underlying delivery protections unresolved. The package also says “D-0016’s safeguarding gate still has to clear” at line 710 and uses similar wording elsewhere.

Consequence: the panel reaches the right practical delivery boundary for the wrong current decision description. That is precisely the kind of authority drift the knowledge system is supposed to prevent.

Smallest effective response: add D-0099 to the controlled corpus and state the distinction exactly: D-0016 is historical and no longer a formal blocker on strategy/pricing/build order; its unresolved substantive protections remain requirements before real participant delivery. Recheck only roles whose conclusions depend on that authority framing.

Major 6 — Provenance is broken and the verifier provides false semantic assurance

Evidence: package-manifest.yml cites assurance-2026-08-13/SYS-04-integrated-recommendation-draft.md, which does not exist; the final file exists instead. Despite the active conflicts above and that broken path, verify_half_day_workshop_package.py reports that the arc, deck, guide and participant copy “agree.”

Smallest effective response: point the manifest to the actual final record; extend the verifier to fail on broken evidence paths and exact semantic invariants for lifecycle, D-0100 measurement, private shared-Radar choice, D-0099/D-0016 framing, bounded behaviour/impact language and closing copy. The checker must report conflicts, not automatically select meaning.

Minor 1 — Pair-choice equivalence is not yet explicit enough to call pressure-free

The guide permits passing, staying with notes or using a neutral example; the deck says “If you want to.” That is a reasonable internal design. Kai’s stronger “choose your own partner or remain solo; both routes receive the same time and closure” is a plausible refinement, not yet supported as required by participant evidence. Preserve it as a participant-test candidate rather than automatically modifying the package.

Minor 2 — The ratio and screen count remain facts, not validated design choices

The HTML explains 63:37 as if “education is the intervention,” while the manifest appropriately says 80 is derived, not a target. Neither ratio nor count is proven optimal. Keep both descriptive and test density, transitions and retrieval in rehearsal/participant research; do not reduce or defend them by assertion.

Hunter Quality Governor gates

Gate Result Reason
1. Mission and decision alignment Fail D-0099 is omitted and active arc claims exceed current approved framing.
2. Evidence and factual integrity Fail Active impact, habit, transfer and response-rate language overstates evidence.
3. Audience coverage and findability Condition open Internal routes are thoughtful, but varied-participant comprehension/cultural evidence does not exist.
4. Charity, safety and reputation Fail for progression Active visible/majority route and obsolete data design conflict with the safer current artifacts; human gates remain.
5. Conceptual and content integrity Fail One canonical page carries competing current states.
6. UX, UI and accessibility Not passed Source-level checks only; no rendered room, print, mobile, keyboard, screen-reader or relevant-user test was supplied.
7. Technical and operational verification Fail The verifier returns PASS despite reproduced semantic conflicts and a broken manifest evidence path.
8. Change control and reusability Fail No SYS-04 reconciliation; mixed-era canonical content; no routing/learning receipt for this panel.

Minority concerns preserved

  • Reed: the current candidate may still overload novices; direct retrieval of Stop–Shift–Do does not establish integration of the wider model.
  • Compass: the visible package still leaves Hunter to resolve which rationale is current; specialist volume is not founder decision-readiness.
  • Iris: “nobody was taught this” may erase family, cultural and community learning even if the intended non-deficit message is valuable.
  • Kai: optional adjacent pair-sharing can still create social pressure; equivalence needs participant evidence.
  • Indigo/Wren/Cole: 80 screens and nine materials may reduce or increase clarity; only rendered and room evidence can decide.
  • Milo/Remy: a cue can support visibility but may be irrelevant where opportunity, safety, authority or context is missing.
  • Noa: additional assurance layers can become avoidance; after source reconciliation, evidence should move into real discriminating tests.

What remains human or field-only

  • Hunter viewing and explicit approval of the exact reconciled build and decision.
  • Qualified clinical/safeguarding review and cohort-specific distress/disclosure/support procedure.
  • Qualified privacy/legal/regulatory review of the exact data map, notices, linkage, storage, access, reporting, retention, deletion and withdrawal.
  • Accessibility review of rendered/projected/printed outputs with relevant users and assistive technologies.
  • Insurer, host and venue decisions.
  • Timed room/projector rehearsal with observed facilitator load and recovery paths.
  • Varied intended-participant comprehension, cultural fit, emotional burden, pair-choice, metaphor, identity-prompt and usability testing.
  • Exact form cognitive interviews and later opportunity/use evidence.

AI packs, even evaluated packs, cannot close these gates.

Required correction sequence and next gate

  1. Correct panel truth: add a whole-bench receipt, add D-0099, relabel multi-role execution accurately, and rerun only calls that require contract-complete separate assurance.
  2. Have SYS-04 reconcile every finding from both producer halves and this independent check, including rejected and unresolved advice.
  3. Apply only accepted bounded corrections in correction-spec.yml; do not rebuild the workshop.
  4. Refresh the manifest and all fingerprints; fix the broken evidence path.
  5. Extend and rerun semantic verification; rerun the named affected roles on changed locations.
  6. Issue a fresh independent decision. Only then present the coherent current build and rationale to Hunter.

Status remains REVISE until those acceptance tests pass.

Fl 01

Compass — fresh founder-intent review of the current build

Independence receipt

This review used the current explicit Hunter instruction, controlled founder sources and the four frozen current artifacts. It did not use the previous assurance folder's conclusions or builder synthesis. It predicts founder-intent fit; it does not claim Hunter has viewed, approved or finalised this build.

Bounded question

Does the visible current package let Hunter understand the participant journey, why each load-bearing choice exists, what is known, what is only proposed and what decision he is being asked to make?

Exact artifact receipt

  • Arc fd8453b39081e494da1535399d2093dd09abcb00e8e0ee806728c05af949cb68
  • Deck 723c6ec782a02d4101d7daacea50cfa271113307a4f2d9bdbf9950ece5ec8f50
  • Guide 4ac38422913252ac119374e3026cd6afb33b3264c82537f59f25e8579594ca9b
  • Materials 6fdfa5d2f465234e5c73c0ac658ef386da8e364e480411781844c2703789be92

Sources reviewed

Current Hunter instruction in this task; K-04 and current K-05/K-07/K-08 references named by the package; 12-founder-context-and-communication-profile-v1.md; 13-founder-voice-v2-explaining-mental-fitness.md; 05-brand-voice-and-language.md; D-0010, D-0015, D-0016, D-0094 and D-0100; the four exact current artifacts; and the evaluated Compass pack.

Professional principles applied

I asked Hunter's recurring questions: what was investigated; how we know; what alternatives exist; why this is strongest; what remains uncertain; what changed; and what exact decision needs Hunter. I checked that everyday recognition precedes jargon, personal capacity does not become blame, collective mission is not overclaimed, and system-created language is not attributed to Hunter.

Position

The participant deck is much closer to Hunter's intended explanation than the visible package around it. The build is not yet founder-decision-ready because the linked canonical arc contradicts the current deck/guide/materials and hides which rationale is current. Hunter approval has not occurred.

The deck follows Hunter's durable explanation: physical health/fitness comparison; everyday moments; five skills; Stop–Shift–Do; access/state; Mental Reps; practice in ordinary moments; Radar and return. It is human, not coded. It also reflects his insistence that personal skill cannot solve every system or safety problem.

What Hunter still cannot confidently answer from the visible system is “Why exactly this architecture?” The arc gives an answer, but parts are obsolete or overconfident: 63:37 is discussed as if the ratio has design authority; movement-scale benefit is implied; older butcher-paper and habit language remain; measurement tabs contradict D-0100. Hunter would have to detect those conflicts himself. That reproduces the problem this intelligence system was meant to solve.

Strongest premise challenge

“The relevant specialists reviewed it” is not the founder outcome. Hunter needs one inspectable chain from current evidence and decisions to the visible participant journey, including dissent and uncertainty. Ten good reports do not help if the visible artifact still carries two states.

Retain / change / reject

  • Retain: the current deck's explanation order, bounded language, ordinary examples, private application, contextual caveats and half-day container.
  • Change: present one reconciled current rationale mapped beat-by-beat to evidence class, decision authority, specialist objection and remaining test.
  • Reject: calling the build final, optimised, Hunter-approved, evidence-based as a whole or delivery-ready.

Evidence strength and limitations

Founder fit is strongly traceable to repeated direct Hunter sources and controlled K-records. The exact architecture remains an internally reasoned candidate, not participant-validated or efficacy-tested. Compass cannot substitute for Hunter viewing.

Objection preserved

The deck may still be too long or too concept-dense, and the education-led arc may underweight experience. There is no evidence yet that a smaller or experience-first version is better. Preserve this objection as a field question rather than forcing another speculative rebuild.

Recommendation and proposed artifact change

Exact location: replace the current Half-Day rat3 and plan3 views in workshop-package.html with a current founder-decision interface. For every beat, show: participant job; why it is present; authority (approved decision, external evidence, MFC design judgement or working hypothesis); strongest objection; evidence limit; and next test. Link the exact deck, guide and materials hashes at the top.

Hunter's later decision should be phrased narrowly: “Having viewed the reconciled current build and rationale, do you approve it to proceed as MFC's internal research candidate for rehearsal, participant testing and qualified-human review?” That is not permission to deliver.

What would change this view

Hunter viewing the exact current artifact and giving explicit feedback/approval is the only way to close founder fit. Reconciled current rationale would make that decision intelligible; participant and expert evidence may still require later change.

Authority limits, handoff and escalation

Compass cannot grant Hunter approval or clinical/legal/accessibility clearance. Hand the reconciled architecture candidate to Relay, then to Hunter for explicit viewing. Preserve A-10's density objection, A-12's hard block and intended-participant gates.

Proposed learning

Candidate update: founder decision-readiness requires one current visible evidence-to-beat chain; specialist activity without reconciliation into that interface leaves the founder carrying the integration burden.

Fl 01 Fresh Cold Read

Compass — fresh independent cold read of the founder-decision interface

Bounded question

Does the new "Founder Decision" view (decide3) actually satisfy Compass's own 2026-08-13 recommendation, well enough that Hunter could now look at this page and understand, without doing any reconciliation work himself, which parts of the workshop are decided, evidenced, judgement calls, or hypotheses — and what's still open?

Sources reviewed

  • workshop-package.html, Half-Day format, id="decide3" view in full (lines 674–740) — the artifact under review.
  • workshop-package.html, Half-Day format, id="walk3" view in full (lines 337–672) — the underlying walkthrough the decide3 table claims to summarise, read to check faithfulness.
  • assurance-2026-08-13-evaluated-panel/reviews/FL-01.md — my own original 2026-08-13 cold read, which this new view claims to respond to.
  • 90-meta/full-permanent-specialist-bench-v1/specialist-knowledge-index.yml, FL-01: block — operating principles applied below.
  • I did not read rat3, plan3, or the linked 25-half-day-whole-bench-reconciliation-and-closure.md — out of scope for this bounded review, and that gap matters to my verdict (see Strongest objection).

Professional principles applied

  • Hunter must be able to see what was investigated, what is known, what alternatives existed, why the recommendation is strongest, and what remains uncertain.
  • Begin with recognisable human experience; explain before jargon.
  • Challenge the founder's frame with evidence and missing perspectives, but never attribute system-created wording or decisions to Hunter without a direct source.
  • (Self-applied, from my own 2026-08-13 review) Hunter needs one inspectable chain from evidence and decisions to the visible participant journey — not ten good specialist reports he still has to reconcile himself.

Position

This mostly does what I asked for, and does it with real fidelity — but it is an addition, not a correction, and that gap matters.

I checked every one of the 25 timed beats in walk3's three blocks against decide3's three tables. All 25 are present, in the same order, with the same time ranges, with no beat invented and none dropped. Where I could check the authority tag against the underlying walkthrough text, it held up: "a teaching model, not a brain map" is a near-verbatim match to walk3's own line on the Driver/Passenger/Engine beat; "the cue's actual effectiveness is untested" for the reminder-card beat matches walk3 word-for-word; Route B being disabled by default, the Radar's "three is Hunter's approved MFC pilot structure, not a scientifically optimal count," and the D-0100 form placement all match their walk3 originals exactly. The four-way authority legend (approved decision / external evidence / MFC design judgement / working hypothesis) is exactly the distinction I asked Hunter to be able to see, stated in plain language, not jargon. The closing "what this page is not" section explicitly disclaims that anything is resolved, proven optimal, or delivery-ready, and links back to my original finding rather than silently absorbing it — that is the honest self-limiting move I look for and it is genuinely there.

So on the narrow question of "does this table tell the truth about the beats it covers," yes.

But my original recommendation was not "add a legible table somewhere." It named an exact location: "replace the current Half-Day rat3 and plan3 views... with a current founder-decision interface." What was built instead sits alongside rat3 and plan3, unchanged, and says so outright: "It replaces nothing — the Walkthrough, Rationale and Measurement tabs are unchanged and still the operational content." My original complaint was specifically that the existing Rationale view carried stale, overconfident content — the 63:37 ratio discussed as if it had design authority, movement-scale benefit implied, older butcher-paper and habit language, measurement tabs contradicting D-0100. None of that was in scope for me to re-check today (I was pointed only at walk3 and decide3), and decide3 itself confirms those tabs are untouched. That means the exact artifact I flagged as capable of misleading Hunter is still one click away, unchanged, still carrying whatever it carried on 2026-08-13 — and nothing on decide3 warns a reader who lands on rat3 first, rather than decide3 first, that the older tab may say something the new one has since corrected.

Strongest objection

decide3 is additive, not corrective. It is a good, honest new front door — but the house behind it (rat3, plan3) was never confirmed to have had its stale claims fixed, only left in place with a newer, better-organised page built next to it. If Hunter (or a future reader) opens "Rationale & Evidence" directly instead of "Founder Decision" — which is exactly as likely, since it's the very next nav button — they can still land on the same reconciliation burden I originally flagged, with no signpost on that tab pointing them to the corrected view. A one-line banner on rat3 and plan3 ("superseded for authority/evidence questions — see Founder Decision") would close this for near zero cost. Without it, this is a real, not cosmetic, gap between what was asked for and what was built.

Evidence strength and limitations

I can verify beat-for-beat textual fidelity between decide3 and walk3 with high confidence — that was a direct, exhaustive read of both, not a sample. I cannot verify from this reading alone: whether the external-evidence citations (generation effect, Bandura mastery experience, Wood & Neal habit formation, implementation intentions) are accurately sourced — that is A-10/evidence-desk territory, not mine, and the citations themselves are plausible but I have not traced them to a source record. Whether rat3/plan3 still contain the specific stale claims from my original review — genuinely unknown from what I read today; the page's own honesty note ("Walkthrough, Rationale and Measurement tabs are unchanged") is the only evidence I have, and it argues the problem is still there rather than that it's been checked and found harmless.

Alternatives considered

  • Replace rat3/plan3 outright, exactly as I originally asked — highest fidelity to the recommendation, but loses whatever operational detail lives only in those tabs and is a bigger, riskier edit.
  • Add decide3 as a new view and leave the others as historical record but visibly marked superseded — most of the benefit of the chosen approach, without the open contradiction risk. This is the fix I'm recommending below.
  • Do nothing beyond a written reconciliation memo (the linked 25-half-day-whole-bench-reconciliation-and-closure.md) without touching the interactive package at all — would have left Hunter back exactly where my original review found him: reading a memo instead of the artifact he'll actually decide from. Correctly rejected.

Recommendation

Accept with one named fix, not accept-as-is. The decide3 content itself is faithful, well-hedged, and answers the authority question I asked for. Before this is presented to Hunter as "the founder-decision interface is done," add a short pointer on rat3 and plan3 directing to decide3 for the authority/evidence/objection view — otherwise the exact defect this page exists to fix is still reachable by the most obvious alternative click. This is a small, bounded, low-risk edit, not a rebuild.

What would change this view

Confirmation (a direct read of rat3 and plan3 against my 2026-08-13 findings) that the specific stale claims I flagged there have actually been corrected at the source, not just superseded elsewhere, would remove my strongest objection entirely. Absent that, the objection stands as a disclosed risk, not a confirmed defect.

Adjacent specialist or human boundary

This review cannot verify the underlying research citations (generation effect, Bandura, Wood & Neal, implementation intentions) — that is evidence-desk/A-10 territory. It cannot verify rat3/plan3's current content — that requires a direct read I was not asked to do. It cannot grant Hunter's approval, and does not claim he has viewed or approved this candidate.

Proposed learning

Candidate update: when a specialist recommendation names an exact remedy location ("replace view X"), and the delivered fix instead adds a new view alongside X, the delivery is not complete until either X is corrected to match, or X is visibly marked superseded — an additive fix that leaves the originally-flagged artifact reachable and unmarked reproduces the exact reconciliation burden the new artifact was built to remove. Whether this rises to a numbered 80-learning/ lesson (versus a one-off note) should be judged against how often the "add alongside instead of replace/mark" pattern recurs elsewhere in this vault's remediation work — I flag it here rather than binding it, since one observed instance is not yet a repeatable-cause finding.
